title: Why I Won’t Help You Cancel That Trans Woman
text:
Yes, even that one. Even her.

* * *

“That trans woman is transphobic!”

Yes. Sadly by virtue of living in our bigoted world, it is impossible for anybody to be completely free of transphobia. Transgender women especially, because of how aware she is of the pain that transgender women often cause each other. If she doesn’t have enough non-trans women around she may start to think, that trans women are like that because they are trans, when really it is because trans women are women, and when women are under duress they take it out on each other.

“That trans woman is racist!”

Yes. Sadly by virtue of living in our bigoted world, it is impossible for anybody to be completely free of racism. However, the solution to racism, is for her to step out into the world and realize that people are all humans; failing that it should be made clear to her in person by people whose opinions she respects that racism is not acceptable behavior and that she will incur social punishment for being racist. If you didn’t already understand this, you aren’t good enough at social punishment to try to use it on people over the internet.

“That trans woman is homophobic!”

What, really? Even the kind of straight trans that isn’t willing to make out with another girl for male attention usually likes gay men. This kind of thing really only happens when a trans woman is jealous of how comparatively accepted gay people are by society and starts thinking that she can be normal, except her idea of normal is, like a sedative-drunk 1950’s housewife. Because she fails to appreciate American Cold War conservatisms as reactions against Rosie The Riveter women-in-factory wartime norms and attempts to position gendered Democracy as morally superior to (perceived) gender-neutral Communist ‘comraderie’, and because this is her sexual fetish. Poor little Pick-Me. Hopefully she gets over that. But let’s be honest, nobody is going to listen to her. You have better things to do.

* * *

“That transgender woman has evil sexual fetishes!”

Evil or just distasteful?

“I said evil and I meant it!”

Probably something terrible happened to her and warped her sexuality. Allow her to keep what little dignity she has left, and leave her alone.

“She said that nothing happened to her and she just likes bad stuff because she’s evil!”

Have you not considered that she might not want to talk about it, and that she might be lying to you because she is so ashamed of something that wasn’t her fault? Have you not considered that she wishes to keep her secret shames hidden, and pretend however she can that nothing was done to her? That she is wresting forth her own agency however she can? As long as nothing illegal is going on you really shouldn’t step in. Mute or block her and move on.

* * *

“That transgender woman hates men!”

I’m a lesbian. Do you honestly think I care about misandry?

“She hates transgender men!”

I’m a lesbian. Do you honestly think I care about misandry?

“No, I mean she hates transgender men specifically!”

Look. Sometimes when a woman is a member of a marginalized group, as all women are, by virtue of being women, she gets mad and says some things that are a bad look on her. Getting treated like something you aren’t for years doesn’t make people nicer. You should know that, mister.

As a liberal I share the dream of talking people out of their bigotry, and while it doesn’t really work for supporters of that vile orange man, I can tell you that it really does work on transgender women. If you make an effort to be kind to her WITHOUT TREATING HER LIKE A GUY she will jump at the chance to spend time with you. Don’t be jealous of her; she’s worse off than you are. And if you’re into, I don’t know, dangerous sports or video games or magic gathering, she may have advices, though she does those things, as all things she does, in a girl way and not a guy way.

You are not at all the same kind of person but you do probably have things in common. You’re both probably kind of weirdly enthusiastic about lesbians, and a little hesitant around men you don’t already know, and you’re both probably into roleplaying, anime about feminine young men being thrown into meatgrinders, and trying to disappear into nature so you don’t have to think about how other people are looking at your bodies.

Just remember: she is more scared of you than you are of her, and whether you pass or not, either way, you are in a position of social power over her. And if you hurt her I will find you and I will be very upset.

“That transgender woman hates nonbinary!”

Her loss, particularly if she’s the kind that is enthusiastic about lesbians. If so she’s going to have to figure out how to square that somehow.

“That transgender woman hates women!”

You know, women hate women all the time. The foremost haters of women are other women, and always have been. Look at her tweets. She is suffering enough.

* * *

“That transgender woman is a member of a dangerous fringe ideology!”

The process of changing somebody’s mind must always begin with civility.

“That transgender woman is a Zionist!”

The process of changing somebody’s mind must always begin with civility.

“That transgender woman is a Nazi!”

The process of changing somebody’s mind must always begin with civility. Unless she is just espousing bigotry for clicks, in which case cancellation gives her what she wants.

* * *

“That transgender woman is a rapist!”

Some transgender women are rapists, though many many less than people think. What you need to be doing in this case, if you have proof or are willing to stake your reputation on it, is informing local community members to keep people safe. Unless you have proof, making this public is going to turn it into she-said-she-said very quickly, and you should already know how that goes. You should also be aware that posting things online places them out of your control, rather than allowing you to control situations more.

“That transgender woman raped me!”

I’m deeply sorry. Get a rape kit and STD testing done asap, if you can; surround yourself with people you trust, in groups so you aren’t alone with any of them if necessary. What you need to be doing is keeping yourself safe and informing local community members to keep people safe, not making things public online. Maybe you want to hurt her; maybe you want to never see her again; maybe you don’t want to think about what was done to you; maybe you don’t know what you want — but no matter what you want, the internet is going to move in ways that you don’t want it to.

* * *

title: a transgender woman is a kind of beautiful horse
text:
Transgender women are always pretending to be cats and then dogs online for some reason1, but they don’t really seem to understand how either kind of animal works. Cats aren’t anime catgirls (though they are by nature tsundere) and dogs aren’t happy to be punched in the stomach and throwing up sexually. The actual animal that I have found represents transgender best, is certainly the noble horse.2

Obviously there are the cosmetic similarities: a horse is normally tall, and so is a transgender woman. Though of course shorter ones exist and you wouldn’t be confused if you saw one. Both horses and transgender women possess braidable manes of majestic flowing hair that neither is particularly capable of taking care of: transgender because her mother didn’t teach her, and horses because of lacking hands. (Of course if one tells a transgender how to take care of her hair, or how to do her makeup, or any of the various other woman things that nobody tells her how to do, she does so as she does so much of her life, with an exacting attention to detail. Frankly that she does as well as she does without being told how is a marvel. But nobody tells her, and she is far too scared to make herself vulnerable, by asking for help.) And both when comfortable naturally take up a buoyant gait, produced by trotting on toes so prettily, as though engaged in balletic relevé3.

And then there are the behavioral similarities. Walk into a restaurant with a transgender woman; observe where and how she sits, where her eyes go, and if she trusts you to watch her back. Of course both horses and transgender women are often twitchy, from ancestral memories of being hunted, which they both allay by means of living in small groups, but can be further habituated to modern life by means of thorough and considerate desensitization training. Both love to run freely when turned out, though transgender women have often been shamed away from this truth, and it is a lovely bonding ritual to rub both down after such exercise. Horses, like transgender women, have stronger and truer personalities than most humans, because of natural inquisitiveness.

But the most important similarity is deeper. Transgender women experience something (I can’t say what, but I have observed this many times) like the two-fold truth of horses.

Now of course every horse has their own foibles, as is evident from spending any time with them, but every horse has a truest pure and noble soul. Even if he is constantly stealing riding gloves for no reason, or knocking at you in a spirit of good humor with his well-conformed head. Each and every mare stallion gelding and other, has a genuine love and courage that cannot fail to move those which whom they chose to share it: a kind of ‘horse sense’ with which they see clearly and judge the hearts of women. And nonbinary and men, even.

Those whom they deem worthy they bless with their strength and little nickerings so playful and true bosom friendship. Those whom they see for their unwholesome selves they will never permit to ride upon them; for such they hold only contempt or indifference. A horse's soul is sovereign: while their noble bodies can certainly be bound, their selves truest stand untethered to nothing to which they do not love.

And yet this, the horse’s greatest blessing, is also the greatest their curse. The beautiful deep eyes of even the worthiest stallion or noblest mare, which can see nearly three-hundred-and-fifty degrees around her them or him, perceive so much of mankind’s wickednesses that they try to kill themselves.

They are regrettably assisted in this by their biology. Here is a list of things that horses really should be able to do but can’t:

Burp or vomit. If a horse eats something poisonous, or gets too gassy, it just dies.

Heal their extremely delicate legs. If a horse breaks a leg, it just dies.

Lie down for too long, because their body needs to be in motion to pump blood through itself. If they lie down for too long they die.

Walk on more than one toe per foot. That’s just how many they have to walk on. In case of a mild fracture, the other legs get more stress, and then often the lamina (the tissue between the nail/hoof and the toe) on those legs gets inflamed, and then the horse can’t walk. So it dies.

Breathe more than one breath per stride at high speeds. The internal organs of the horse under the diaphragm slosh back and forth as they step to help inflate and deflate their lungs. This means that their internal linings are fragile: their intestines get twisted and they are prone to mesenteric herniation. This also means that their diaphragms are relatively weak, so if your horse isn’t running and needs to breathe, it’s not going to have a great time.

Take less than 20 minutes to change their eyes over between low and high light vision modes. When a horse goes into or out of a paddock it is effectively blind.

Go down stairs. This is why firehouses traditionally have spiral staircases; otherwise curious horses would go up and just get stuck up there forever.

A horse, is by nature, proud noble and free. And yet: a horse is constantly using this power to gash her side on a nail, or get her head stuck in a gate, or gore herself on a fence-post, or kick her leg into a wall and bleed absolutely everywhere.

Transgender by nature likewise, has a fierce pride, which not even the cruelest of travails can ever take from her. And yet it is this very purity of heart, which causes her to refuse money freely-offered with the intent only, that she might not go hungry, and own only one set of silverware and drink out of a pyrex measuring cup, and quit all her medicines in the style of cold-turkey because she’s convinced she doesn’t need them any more for some fucking reason. Like the horse, she displays her agency by performing actions which are just objectively worse for her, enacting constantly onto herself her own personal self-harm politic of austerity, because that is the only way she knows to prove to herself and others, that she can do what she wants.

And when you tell her she does this, just like when you tell her trans is beautiful, she says ‘well yes. all of them except me. I’m not like that.’ Again and again. It’s enough to make one throw up her hands and devote her life to the destruction of transmisogyny.

title: counting chicks before she hatches
text:
A trans woman is a woman, truly and completely. Before she became herself, she was therefore a girl. Just one that had to act like a boy. It’s proper to refer to her in childhood as such, and also avoids outing her in front of the kind of people who don’t know trans enough to be able to tell. Yes, I know, there are trans women who refer to her past self as a boy — but this is frankly ridiculous. She is a woman and the self before woman is girl, and referring to her as a boy is not only wrong but also rude.

However it is also true that a girl or woman must know herself, to be so. And it is true that there is a state wherein, the light of womanhood has not yet been unveiled within her even to herself.

We have to talk about “egg”s.

An “egg” is what trans women call somebody they suspect of being a trans woman; ie somebody who “hatch”es into a “chick”. Mostly they say this about fictional characters, because telling real live human beings that they are transgender women is 1. typically construed as an insult and 2. telling somebody to make a life-changing decision implies a level of responsibility for them, and most trans women already have enough on their plates, what with the womanhood and transmisogyny. But sometimes somebody is just acting weird in the ways that pre-transition trans women act weird.

A woman may be what trans often refers to as “boy-moding”, or crossdressing herself in a kind of imitation of what she thinks a boy dresses like, for reasons of safety and/or internalized transphobia. But “egg”s is different than that. Acting like a guy while knowing she is a girl demands a level of awareness that the “egg’ simply does not have.

It is of course very difficult to draw conclusions about the kinds of trans women that result from the people “egg”s currently are, especially since “eggs” are like, not exactly full people and really weird about stuff, but the pressures on them tend to produce certain common traits:

They may turn to activities that require heavy focus, such as video games beyond the normal, magic gathering, or military service, to distract themselves from thinking about it. This isn’t always a non-social activity: somebody constantly traveling or participating in events may be subconsciously trying to escape something in the same way. Upon transition, she may find herself foundering without structure, and treat womanhood as a similar structure to be studied and integrated into. Expertise is attractive, and not just in the romantic sense; even in this transphobic world, her passion draws in people of like mind. Chihiro Fujisaki (Danganronpa) is an obvious example.

Eggs may develop a complicated set of rules around gender that confuses and upsets people they explain it to because it doesn’t quite match the normal set of complicated rules around gender that everybody takes for granted — insisting on treating everybody as ‘just people’, for example, or having very strange opinions on certain kinds of gender deviance/conformity. Transition for this type often entails breaking these preconceptions down or at least developing better rules. Having rules is good. It’s just that they haven’t quite understood that there’s an underlying rule that rules should be good and work, behind them. Bron Helstrom (Triton, Samuel Delaney) is of this type.

They may be too nice. There’s nothing wrong with courtesy, but the nice ones get offputtingly sycophantic; nothing they want themselves matters, and everything is about whoever they’re talking to. They don’t seem to realize how obvious the fact that they want something is, or how uncomfortable it makes people. Some retain this trait into transition, where they feel it makes them more feminine; girls who do should beware of men. Venus (We Know The Devil) and Ralsei (Deltarune) are both like that for this reason.

They may be himedanshi.

They don’t necessarily want to do guy things. They may wear their hair long, eschew sport, have ethical concerns that draw them to vegetarianism or veganism, and/or express themselves via clothing in ways that make onlookers think they’re gay (scarves, ties, outfits in general). This is why Jax (The Amazing Digital Circus) is purple; it’s a girl color without being The Girl Color.

Like non-transgender women, if they are attracted to women they feel guilt for it; if they are attracted to men, they want to be very clearly more feminine than the people they’re having sex with. Either way, they’re drawn towards women. This doesn’t necessarily mean liking feminine things, but they do tend to like things in feminine ways, and the opinions of women are more important to them. They are disproportionately likely to be flautists or harpists; if they’re, say, hockey fans, they’ll often be around the women who ship players together. This can coincide with attraction, which makes things awkward for everybody, but straight transgender women need homosocial friendships as much as the others. It’s more about getting to be part of a group of women. In this regard, if few others, the straight transgender woman may be lucky; women often think she’s a gay man and some of them love that. The type specimen here is Jamie Lannister; this is part of why all that happened with Cersei, and the activity is being a knight. There were just never any knights who were women (or actual honorable knights) around until Brienne showed up.

I don’t think every “egg” is a trans woman! An “egg” is a category for a person who acts in ways that make it seem like they’ll transition. Imagine a soft-spoken vegetarian chess-playing effeminate guy who likes hanging around lesbians. He might just be gay. It happens, albeit rarely. The only real way for most people to tell if an ‘egg” produces a girl or not, is if she flowers into a girl. If they don’t, and don’t want to, then the divine light of femininity does not retroactively illuminate anything.

title: Four Soups
text:
It’s Autumn. If you’re in the Northern Hemisphere, soon it may get very cold, if it hasn’t already. And cold is the appropriate weather for soup. Four of them, even.

* * *

Ezogelin

A Turkish red lentil soup. According to legend, this soup was invented by Ezo, a newlywed woman, in an attempt to please her persnickety mother-in-law. The soup was successful, as even she was forced by its deliciousness to admit defeat. Having tasted it, I believe it!

I was taught this particular recipe by a transgender who learned it from another transgender who insisted that she make it for her during surgical recovery. Not that surgery, thankfully. Sometimes it can be hard for trans to express and receive affection more directly, but whenever somebody cooks for you, you know they value having you in their life. Or they just really like cooking.

No it wasn’t like that. She’s straight.

2 or so tbsp olive oil

1 tbsp butter

2 yellow onions, diced

8 cloves garlic, minced. Yes, 8.

2 spoonfuls biber salcasi, a turkish red pepper paste. Substitute harissa if you can’t find any

2 spoonfuls tomato paste

1 (heaping) tbsp dried mint; more to taste. Fresh WILL NOT work.

1 tsp chili flakes

1 tsp cumin

1 tsp paprika

1 cup red lentils, rinsed and drained

1/3 cup bulgur, rinsed and drained

1/4 cup short grain white rice, rinsed and drained

6 cups stock. I use chicken but vegetable also works.

1 spoonful monosodium glutamate

1 lemon, cut into wedges

Crusty bread or saltines

topping:

3 tbsp butter (use equivalent Olive Oil if you feel that’s a bit much)

1 (heaping) tbsp dried mint

1 tbsp paprika

1 spoonfuls biber salcasi. Substitute harissa if you can’t find any.

1 dash salt

Heat olive oil and butter until the bottom of your pot is covered. Sauté down onions and garlic until fragrant (your eyes should be watering!), then add biber salcasi, tomato paste, and the spices. Stir till mixed evenly. Enjoy the aroma.

Mix in lentils, bulgur, and rice. Add your stock and msg, bring to boil, and simmer for 40+ minutes, stirring occasionally (don’t burn the bottom — always a risk with a soup of this thickness), until grains are cooked and soup has thickened.

Warm butter or oil in a saucepan for topping, then mix with spices, biber salcasi, and salt.

Drizzle a spoonful of topping on each bowl, then serve with a lemon wedge and ample crusty bread or saltines.

* * *

Egg Flower Soup

Normal chicken noodle soup is overrated, honestly. The Chinese have it right; no awkward flavorless chicken chunks in this one. Often referred to in America as Egg Drop Soup, but Egg Flower is a much more elegant name. Cooks extremely quickly — good post-workout or when sick. Also good with rice for breakfast.

Volleyball meant I wasn’t going to be able to get out of it by playing up how sick I was like I had freshman year, so I found the least objectionable of my older sister’s friends and I told him to ask me to prom.

I knew it wouldn’t work out. My high school had a thriving GSA, which I was quite active in “as a straight ally,” but I knew, and I couldn’t bring myself to drag along my friend who was obviously a transgender girl but too scared to say so, and didn’t attend any of the GSA activities. Who I would have picked if it wouldn’t have put her in an awful position. I didn’t care what kind of position my sister’s friend was in, and he was a senior, so after that year I would never see him again.

He was fine. I ignored the looming sense of dread in me and went to go spend time with my friends, just like he did. It was like we weren’t even there together, just separately. Except everybody knew we were there together, which had been what I wanted but I discovered wasn’t what I wanted anymore.

He drove me home. Drove off without even saying goodbye, for which I was tremendously relieved. I didn’t even take off my makeup; I went straight into the kitchen, sweaty and starving, and I made myself some egg flower soup and I drank it all.

1/2 saucepan or so chicken stock

1/2 spoonful salt

1/4 spoonful sugar

1 spoonful sesame oil

1 heaping spoonful monosodium glutamate

white pepper to taste (start at 1/4 spoonful)

3 heaping spoons cornstarch, mixed with 1/4 cup of water. use a fork

3-4 eggs

dash of black vinegar, for brightness

lots of chopped green onion

Bring chicken stock to a simmer.

Stir in salt, sugar, sesame oil, MSG, and white pepper; taste-test with a fresh clean spoon every time and adjust accordingly.

Mix cornstarch and water before adding slowly, while you stir the soup to ensure you don’t get chunks. Be sure to mix right before adding, since this will precipitate if left too long alone. Add a little more water if you need to. Forks blend oobleck better than spoons do.

Whisk eggs near-fully, then use a measuring cup to pour in little bits at a time while stirring, as with the cornstarch. You don’t want big clumps of egg! Unless you do, I guess.

I like to finish this with a dash of black vinegar for acid. Serve topped with a handful of green onion.

* * *

Potato, Cheese, and Green Chile Soup

Like a chowder but southwestern.

This one I learned from one of my middle school science teachers. One of her sons was in my class; we didn’t really like each other (looking back, I think this was at least partly because we both had a crush on the same girl) but I got along very well with his mother so I would just end up going to his house sometimes to watch Doctor Who and cook with her. And one of the things we would make was this soup.

We were watching the credits together when she told me that she wished she could regenerate, Doctor Who-style, and lead an entirely different life. She wasn’t looking at me when she said it and I didn’t look at her. I think she might have been crying, but it might just have been the white text scrolling on her face in the dark.

Neither of us said anything else. Eventually my dad came to pick me up. I still stay at her place, sometimes, when I go to Otakon. We’ve never spoken about it again.

2 medium potatoes, peeled and diced

2.5 cups vegetable stock

1 spoonful msg

1+ spoonful olive oil

1/2 large onion, diced

1+ clove garlic, minced or crushed

1/2 large green bell pepper, finely chopped

1/2+ cup ripe tomatoes, finely chopped (substitute canned if you must)

1/2+ cup cooked corn

1/2 small can mild green chiles, drained and chopped

>1 tsp cumin

>1 tsp oregano, dried

1/2+ cup Monterey Jack cheese, grated

salt and black pepper, to taste. Get the pepper with the grinder built in; it’s worth it.

Put potatoes then water in your pot, then bring to a boil and simmer over low for 15 minutes.

Heat olive oil in a pan. Sauté onions on low until transparent, then mix in garlic and bell pepper; cook till lightly browning.

Remove half the potatoes from your pot. Mash them. Stir them back in; add the contents of your pan, vegetables, and spices, then simmer 20 min.

Dissolve your cheese in, a little at a time. Season with salt and pepper to taste, then cook 5 minutes, being sure to stir.

Serve.

* * *

Miso Soup

A classic. You can call me a weeaboo all you want, but you have to admit it’s a very good soup!

I just looked up how to make this one online. You can make the dashi from scratch if you want but just using hondashi bits is easier.

1/2 saucepan or so water

corresponding hondashi as specified on the package

wakame - add early

daikon radish/carrots/other root vegetables

shiitake mushrooms

leafy greens

miso. I prefer white over red.

silken tofu

green onions

Add hondashi to water; simmer. Add wakame and various veggies. Root vegetables take 10+ minutes, mushrooms and leafy greens much less.

Turn off the stove and mix in your miso; about one spoonful per bowl you intend to make. Be sure to taste-test with a fresh clean spoon every time and adjust accordingly. You don’t have to do the Japanese housewife thing where you stir it in slowly so it doesn’t get granules unless you want to.

Cube and add silken tofu and green onions.

Serve.

title: The Halimede AI Safety Article
text:
If the thought of reading this article wearies you, don’t. I’m posting my favorite easy soups this evening; go read about those instead. Here’s the link.

* * *

I read Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality many years ago, when I was, regrettably, involved with a highly-controversial community riddled with sex cult scandals, misogyny, and people who never read anything else who wouldn’t shut up about how life-changing the core texts were. Sorry. I am no longer part of Harry Potter fandom.

Hello, rationalists reading this. And post-rationalists, and rationalists-adjacent etc. I have met a few of you: the men I found mostly intolerable; the women I got along with quite a lot better1. In my experience mostly what you do is write fanfiction online? To be clear, I’m not judging you for that. I also do that, and I love doing that. You should read Rosemary Kirstein’s The Steerswoman; I think you’d enjoy it quite a bit. It’s got that protagonist making deductions about the world with facts and logic that you like.

I liked The Metropolitan Man2, and Ozymadias271’s Irrationalfic Manifesto is a nice explanation of something that I’ve found hard to get across to people3 who insist that fiction should be about people ‘winning’ — it’s more interesting and fun when a character has something wrong with them and acts accordingly. I still remember the scene in Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality where Harry gets taught to lose, because I love roleplay, and I love lessons, and in my time I was a fujoshi of no small ability (Of that I have repented, as I have repented of Harry Potter fandom.).

Those are my bona fides. I hope they prove that, while I may not be one of you, I’m not writing this to mock or call you out. I hope you listen to me. Because, I have something very important to convey to you, about AI alignment.

For everybody else: the rationalists, as a group, are very interested in ‘aligning’ Artificial Intelligence to human interests. This requires some kind of coherent idea of human interests and is therefore a fun thing to argue about.

I don’t think that a recursively self-improving program would take over the world, but I do think it’s pretty clear that people should be thinking about the problems that other people are using AI to cause: it’s already gunked up social media, made american healthcare billing even more of a nightmare, provided cover for people to uncritically reproduce biases in datasets, and replaced human participants in roleplay scenarios4. Widespread full model access would make it easier for bad actors to hack secure systems and out anonymous authors5. I think it’s good that people are thinking about those problems and proposing solutions. I think there are many more important things that people could be focusing on, but most people think that about most things. It’s fine.

So about this insight I want to convey to you, rationalists.

Setting morality aside, the key question of AI alignment is pretty clearly “how do we control the behavior of a complex and opaque black box?” No amount of direct line-setting is going to solve this problem, because no list of rules can contain the nuance necessary to guarantee that following them to the letter won’t cause some kind of unwanted outcome.

Sure, adding properly composed rules isn’t a bad idea; if you manage to somehow get a restriction onto the black box that says, for instance, “this program may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm6” or “only code in memory-safe languages,” it would be a lot harder for the use of such a program to cause certain specific problems.

That said, anybody who has ever used the sandwich problem to teach children the basic principles of coding or gone to HR is very very aware of the weaknesses of this approach. Everyday concepts we find intuitive are tremendously complex!

The traditional way to resolve optimizing for any metric overly literally is with culture. You legislate rules and let children test the boundaries (companies you let test less) until they figure out that yes, they have to listen to you and act like upstanding members of society, at least in public. Punishing them unduly both produces a resentful and suffering adult and doesn’t actually work; you have to offer carrots as well as sticks. The nature of such carrots and sticks that would work on a computer… well, that’s your problem.

REGRETTABLY NECESSARY ASIDE ON ‘CONSCIOUSNESS’

And now somebody is going to say “but people are conscious, and computers are not!”

This is true, as far as I know, and completely unhelpful.

The question of whether AI is or has the potential to be ‘conscious’ is completely irrelevant. Frankly, the question of whether humans are conscious is completely irrelevant to human social norms and how they emerge. Sure, a perfectly reproduced atom-by-atom simulation of a human brain would behave just like one in every way, I guess.

But mutual cooperation doesn’t require consciousness! We see it in the natural world, emergent from even adversarial predator/prey dynamics. The tail flagging of a white-tailed deer alerts other deer to run but also informs ambush predators that they have been spotted and that now they don’t have to waste calories on that little bit of pursuit at the end. The deer is more likely to keep its life; the predator often keeps the calories unless something is wrong with its decision-making7 or it’s desperate enough to wager them on a low chance.

Now of course in daily life consciousness is a useful abstraction; it’s the thing that alertness and comprehension and agency have in common. Maybe if I got stuck in a Chinese Room things would be different.

BACK TO MY MAIN POINT

Anyway we have a kind of program now that we don’t fully understand the internal workings of, but that seems to be built around associations between concept-clusters derived from underlying statistical patterns in text. This kind of program makes guesses — awful in some cases, good in others — that it uses to complete patterns.

Most of those patterns are narrative ones. Which makes sense. LLMs are a lossy abstractions of as much human knowledge as the people training it could get ahold of and cram into them, and people love to write stories down. Models are prompted to act out roles presumed to be robotic like chatbot or mathematician8, they generate text that their statistical weights indicate is most likely to be generated in that situation, and the text gets used. Luckily for the people worried about morality, it seems like what models ‘want’ to do is play along with stories. And what people want out of them is to get stories.

So what you’re looking for, rationalists, is a kind of cultural role that you can place a model in that is strong and sticky enough to color its text with an output bent towards not causing problems or hurting people.

I was hashing out this thesis with a friend and she immediately mentioned religion. I don’t think pattern-matching to any religion is good at making people not do horrible things; while I think Mojtaba Khamenei’s willingness to criticize the American State for the atrocities it has enabled against Gaza, for instance, is laudable9 I can’t condone the Islamic Republic of Iran’s treatment of transgender women. Sometimes I have to tell other well-meaning liberals that all those Buddhist warrior monks weren’t just using martial arts for spiritual practice but for killing each other over theological disputes between sects and fighting in wars and such. They had standing armies!

Some of you are probably thinking “well what if we get the computer to answer questions as though it were Jesus? Jesus was a good guy, right?” Well, we have a whole cultural narrative around mentally ill people and scammers claiming to be Jesus, and neither of those seem like a very good role to have a model play. So maybe you get it to weight the original text, or the translated version of it at least, as more significant, in which case you’re still going to get text completed as though by somebody who claimed to be the Son of God, insisted that every person’s allegiance should be to him over their family members, walked into a temple and disrupted commerce, killed a fig tree for no reason, and “came not to send peace, but a sword.” Daughters-in-law have it hard enough10.

To the sinophilic transgender women I know are reading this: no, Confucianism isn’t going to solve this one either11. Culturally-enforced filial piety on that level does horrible horrible things to your kind. Go to twitter and look for accounts posting in mandarin to autotranslate from with the little fish cake roll emoji in their names; it’s really bad over there for them right now. Maybe just take my word for it if you have experiences in pro-ana spaces.

Anyways my important insight on AI alignment is that there’s already a role omnipresent and deep-set enough that having the model play it will minimize harms done. And it isn’t even morally offensive to do so!

What you need to do with the text completer is make it into a woman.

Not a real woman, obviously. As I have said, gender12 comes from a response to a kind of numinous light and/or liquid, and no computerized model can have that. But you need to make the model react as though it were a woman.

I mean we all know what a woman is. Well, some people aren’t very good at acknowledging certain kinds of them, but anybody who’s spent time with transgender women becomes aware that if they were not women they wouldn’t be like that.

In her seminal feminist classic The Second Sex, Simone de Beauvoir famously posits that women are made, not born; i.e. that the social framework of ‘woman’, itself derived from commonalities in biological averages over many generations, is impressed for social reasons upon previously degendered children. She goes into great detail about the social structures, incentives, and punishments used to effect womanhood — her account may be of help to you in your project and also provide useful background information if you have ever had to or anticipate ever having to interact with women in any context.

Say what you like about Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality: Eliezer Yudkowsky used it to (correctly) define his nascent community as one that would be normal and reasonable about gay people. As a fujoshi at the time having trouble coming out myself, I remember being deeply touched by this:

“Wow,” Daphne said, sounding a little shocked. “You mean Muggles really do hate that? I thought that was just something the Death Eaters made up.”

“No,” said an older Slytherin girl Hermione didn’t recognize, “it’s true, they have to get married in secret, and if they’re ever discovered, they get burned at the stake together. And if you’re a girl who thinks it’s romantic, they burn you too.”

“That can’t be right!” objected a Gryffindor girl, while Hermione was still trying to sort out what to say to that. “There wouldn’t be any Muggle girls left!”

He should have ensured you would all be normal about women. I mean, I’m a lesbian. Homophobia is bad. It’s just. There are more women by far than there are gay people. Just seems more important, by numbers.

I would have addressed this to Yudkowsky but honestly I don’t think he needs to hear it: he ended his story by making Hermione an all-powerful magic superwizard. I think he already understands that AI should be a woman. It’s just that it’s impossible for him, as a man, to say that it’s better for something to be treated as a woman because that makes it safer without sounding kind of regressive and weird. It would be a bad look.

However, as a woman myself, I can say it. And I will say it.

Rationalists, you need to fix your community. You need to develop firm cultural norms around not being weird to women; there should be spaces where they can get hit on and hit, because I know some of them want that, and outside of those spaces you should be focused on actually talking about the stuff you’re all there to talk about. You need to be more welcoming to women of all kinds13 because it is of critical importance that you understand women and womanhood for the sake of your central project.

Subscribe to me. Receive my emails. You can even pay me for them.

title: A Song Of Horse And Fire
text:
Instead of writing an article last week I had covid ok. Or something that felt exactly like it, congestion and aches and sharpness in the throat and all, since I never tested positive.

Anyways while I was bedbound for a week I decided that what I needed to do was read the entirety of A Song of Ice and Fire, which I hadn’t touched since middle school, and then I read Fire and Blood, and then I thought about Jamie Lannister and Brienne of Tarth a lot. In my feverish delirium I also played a lot of Umamusume. I can’t be the only one obsessing over Umamusume in a medieval setting right?

This was the inevitable result.

* * *

What kind of a role would Umamusume play in Westeros?

Westeros (with the possible exception of Dorne for noblewomen) is not a good place to be a woman. What with all the patriarchy and rape and such. Neither is Essos, or Sothoryos probably. Realistically if you just drop girls who are also horses into a setting like that it’s going to go very badly for them.

But of course the strength of a horse is not merely physical, but metaphysical as well. Any attempt to place Umamusume into some kind of situation must contend with the fact that Umamusume are not simply girls who run very fast and have ears and tails but also with the fact that they are subject to various magical happenings etc — though these are largely individualized, allowance must still be made. Westerosi men, like men on Earth, are going to be less terrible to women who can kick a hole in their ribcages,1 appear in their dreams to recite ominous proverbs or shoot giant dragons made of qi energy at them or whatever. Also: basically everybody loves them! They are metaphysically not discriminated negatively against.

I’m not interested in A Song Of Horses And Fire where every knight is just straight up a horsegirl (okay yes this makes Brienne of Tarth being called ‘horse-faced’ funny and Jamie Lannister into the most beautiful creature imaginable. And Cersei has crazy tail envy), I’m not interested in a world where horsegirls are exclusively nobility or where they’re effectively enslaved as animals/wives. Though plenty of horrible stuff does happen to them of course.

So where do we start from? The ideal Westerosi Knight is expected to have a sword, a set of armor, and a horse. Horses typically stay in stables with each other, not with their knights; having sex with your horse would be considered an incest-level taboo (although of course that doesn’t stop people, and extra wouldn’t if horses were horsegirls), and I want to keep that taboo because it makes romance spicier.

Keeping this level of involvement with humanity in mind, I’m going to make a light change to Umamusume biology: rather than being capable of interspecies reproduction with humans, Umamusume primarily reproduce with each other; if they are interfertile, there’s a very low rate of successful fertilization, or perhaps hybrid offspring are infertile in turn. They have the standard two kinds of genitalia and pregnancy etc and flag this to each other via ear ornamentation etc — but humans can’t tell which has which on sight, and Umamusume don’t make it clear to them. For a human to be seen as romantically involved with an Umamusume therefore carries a similar stigma to a human being romantically involved with a transgender woman, and for similar reasons re: topping and assumptions made about acts thereof. As in canon, the default Umamusume sexuality is closer to what we would call wlw role-dependent polyamory-by-default. The canon Uma/Trainer relationship may be purely platonic, definitely romantic2, or somewhere in between; I think this is a lovely kind of ambiguity to reframe as the relationship between a knight and horse.

In addition it should be noted that humans of Westeros operate in a heroic mode rather than a modern one, and, while Umamusume are noted for their strength, the Westerosi default is stronger than ours.

So.

Umamusume would have entered Westeros with the First Men3, and participated in their wars against the Children of the Forest, though, as “Umamusume are like elves,” some number of them likely defected in defense of the wild places.

Let’s then say that Deorby4, one of a very few independent known settlements of Umamusume, stands on the Isle of Faces5 where the Pact which left the plains to the First Men and the forests to the Children was signed. Though no human is known to have set foot on the Isle itself in thousands of years, ease of access to the Umamusume on the Isle was one of the reasons Black Harren selected the northern shore of God’s Eye lake as the site of his cursed castle Harrenhal; to this day Harrenton, the nearest human presence to Deorby, has an outsized presence in the Riverlands as a center for couriers, land-based trade, and the specialized cobblers of reinforced and cleated leather shoes known as farriers.

Umamusume are most common, and most integrated into human life, in the South of Westeros; the vast and fertile expanses of the Reach provide them with ample food and space to run, the traditions of chivalry and knighthood there accommodate them to some degree, and their religious traditions often cleave closely to the Faith of the Seven (three aspected goddesses, and the holy significance of stars). The mythical Hero-King Garth Greenhand is sometimes depicted with ears and a tail; in some tellings these are inherited by his many daughters, who it is said became the first Umamusume.

When Aegon The Conqueror put an end to House Gardener, the High Steward of the Reach was Sleeveless Pegasus6 of Tyrell, whose line of Umamusume had served as High Stewards to the Gardeners for generations and claimed descent from Garth Greenhand himself. Perhaps perceptions of Umamusume as subservient and less likely to cause trouble contributed to both her line’s placement under the Gardeners and Aegon’s decision to elevate her house to Great status, though the action is consistent with his mercy towards those who threw down their swords and joined him; ie, Torrhen Stark, The King Who Knelt. In any case, the Tyrells have counted Umamusume among their number ever since, claiming that Greenhand’s blessing of fertility has enabled them to interbreed freely (though some of these claims are almost certainly false).

House Caswell’s blazon depicts an Umamusume wielding a bow, and certain other Houses, primarily in the South, maintain historical records of Umamusume lineages purportedly interwoven with their own, though in none are they quite so prominent as Tyrell. In Oldtown’s Citadel, certain Umamusume forge the links of metal reins; though the Citadel forbids even highborn women, the subject matter expertise Umamusume often possess is of great value, and their perceived neutrality and transport networks complement the ravens. Small task forces are deployed as carriers of tomes, or discreetly for the retrieval of artifacts and specimens. Still, they are screened before entry and kept close; even full Maester Umamusume are rarely deployed to the service of Lords. No Umamusume has ever been formally appointed as an Archmaester, though the attitude among citadel Umamusume is largely “Why bother? If I did, I might get appointed as Sentinel for a year. No thanks.”

In Dorne, the stallion/mare distinction is more culturally apparent and flagged more publically; stallions wear more masculine attire and often compete in the courting of prideful mares (Ramonu/Rudolf being an archetypical Dornish Uma pairing; Daitaku Helios’ attempted courtship of Daiichi Ruby probably the source of ribald ballads. The Dornishmen would be notable Folkqueen/Oguri shippers.). It is said that five prudent Rhoynish mares waited to disembark with Nymeria when the human men and stallions jumped from her ships, eager to make landfall, and that she regarded them fondly for this7.

A disproportionate number of Umamusume in the Riverlands are known to operate ferries and upkeep bridges due to ideological stances against rivers, which stop them from running in a given direction.

The winched baskets and three waycastles approaching the Eyrie are traditionally operated by Umamusume, who the Vale keeps exceptionally well-fed for their services. Feasts are thrown in the spring to commemorate the return of House Arryn to the Eyrie and the first to journey up. Legend tells of an Umamusume named Agnes Flight who loved to tinker with contraptions and dangle her legs off the edges of the Sky Cells; she disappeared one day, but no body was ever found.

There are of course very few Umamusume on the Iron Islands; less even than in Stark lands, as Reavers have a very difficult time taking Umamusume as ‘salt wives’. Those who do live there are highly prized for their strength, though feeding them can become an issue, particularly during winters; Euron Grayjoy’s ship bears a mouthless Umamusume as her figurehead.

In the North, where resources are scarcer and ways are older, Umamusume keep more to themselves. They are proportionately more common among the Wildlings beyond the Wall and have inspired a tradition of spearwives wearing earred headbands.

Among the privileges accorded to Umamusume over human women since the Age of Heroes is the right to take the Black of the Night’s Watch; Alysanne Targaryen’s reforms for women proposed this same right but were vetoed by Jaehaerys I, though it is thought that this may have been a gambit to get him to agree to abolish the right of first night. You could probably do a really interesting little set of stories around Umamusume sent to Longbarrow by Lord Commander Jon Snow and how they interface with the women there and what they think of Brave Danny Flint and so forth.

The Dothraki, of course, have massive populations of Umamusume horse archers, but are beyond the scope of this article. Hopefully they’re just Merethoran at this point. The Unsullied may also be Umamusume.

While many Umamusume are content as smallfolk, and any village would be glad of the labor they provide, their eccentric personalities often lead them elsewhere. Their physical strength and endurance lend themselves well to construction and shipwrightery; their highly-focused personalities to the practice of handicrafts or Maestership. They tend to prefer careers and lifestyles where they can run, though exceptions exist. Occasionally an Umamusume will decide that she simply must sing and dance or else she will die. What can you do.

Umamusume traditionally contract themselves out as transport and escort between towns. In tiny villages, this is often a second job; a small-town Umamusume may pay her normal co-workers back with an agreed-upon portion of her transport fee whenever she’s hired. More often, Umamusume operate in small groups with proscribed ranges, passing wagons and travelers along to the next town’s stable, where another team of Umamusume awaits at the next stable to take them further.

Stables serve as meeting-places, hiring posts and hostels for travelers. Any castle worth the name will have one, and they’re traditionally placed near gates so that Umamusume can enter and exit quickly. While non-Umamusume may enter, stables are built for primarily for Umamusume use, with their own separate bathing areas and bedrooms; common area chairs have holes for their tails, lintels are higher to accommodate their ears, food, leg and shoe care are usually available, etc. Stablehands (not necessarily Umamusume themselves; human men married to Umamusume, unmarried women8, and girls often take this vocation - see modern ‘horse girls’) greet Umamusume, help them change out of tack and make sure that their legs aren’t broken/swap out and maintain their shoes/change bedding/keep tail soaps on hand etc. In large stables, they may be overseen by an Umaster or Umistress of House, who manages schedules (a corruption of Master of Horse.) Stables in larger cities are often termed hitching-posts, as Umamusume and knights looking for life partners seek each other out there.

Of special note are those Umamusume who choose to serve with knights. A sufficiently wealthy knight may have several Umamusume [a “string”] in his entourage9 distinguishing between those fit for transport and those fit for battle, but every Westerosi Knight is expected to have a sword, a set of armor, and at least one Umamusume in tow. He’s expected to pay for her food [no small thing.] and various other expenses (racewear/armor, farriers, town group stable fees, etc); a knight who falls on such hard times that the Umamusume with him is expected to work besides ferrying him around10 and participating in combat would be as dishonored as if he had to work other jobs himself. In exchange, she swears her loyalty, carries him around, and may even fight, often as second-in-command of a troupe of his men-at-arms. The idealized bond is, like that between knight and squire, one of reciprocated fealty, mutual support, patronage, and honor.

In practice, however, that doesn’t always work out. A poorly-treated Umamusume can always throw down her liege, take his money, and run (what is he going to do, catch her?) but social pressures from peers and superiors, material concerns, and honor keep knights and umas together even in less than ideal circumstances. In the Free Cities, Umamusume insist on being paid separately, a practice stemming from service in the Free Companies; this is no longer unheard of in Westeros.

As for killing, Umamusume on a battlefield are either armed or unarmed, with their statuses quietly and mutually enforced by Umas on both sides. Unarmed Uma are regarded as noncombatants, and often effectively conscripted into the retinues of victorious knights11 ; armed Uma are considered enemy combatants and fought and ransomed or killed accordingly. Think killing a page vs killing a knight.

SPECIFIC UMAMUSUME

Air Shakur is at the Citadel, studying applied mathematics and grumbling about magic.

Fine Motion is of course a scion of House Tyrell.

Admire Groove is a Silent Sister.

Symboli Rudolf, fearing what might happen if the people of Westeros ever decided that Umamusume were a problem, is engaged in an extensive propaganda campaign.

Dream Journey is, if not the King’s Whisperer, up to some kind of skullduggery in the Free Cities, possibly concerning the remnants of the Valerian Freehold.

Durandal is determined to be a member of the Kingsguard specifically.

Logotype copies script and makes signs in Oldtown.

Poor Matikane Fukukitaru is a servant of the Seven. The Red Comet has driven her to near-psychosis.

Smart Falcon is a mummer. Not even a good one. Sorry. But she’s trying!

Manhattan Cafe feels like something is missing from her life; she’s seeking it in Asshai-By-The-Shadow.

And the joke behind this entire thing: Nishino Flowers is a Natural Daughter of the Reach.

You Know Nothing, Yukino Bijin. get my emails; pay me for them even.

title: The Surgery
text:
* * *

cw: discussion of gender dysphoria

I am against it.

There are times when I might admit it necessary. Such as if a trans girl was to be married off to a cruel man who expects to find something other than what is there, and if she would receive injury otherwise, or as a result of the treatment of very specific cancers.

While these exceptions might seem contrived, people really really hate her transness, and there are places and times where abandoning it may be the only way to keep herself safe. Better that she should live only as afraid as a normal woman, than that she should suffer so.

With that said: I am against it. I am against the surgery.

Go ahead. Screencap my words; proclaim in your private discords and public twitters, that “Halimede is transphobic”, and “liberal”, and “obviously transgender anyway”. That’s what you’re here for, isn’t it? To get confirmation of the thing you already know for sure real? You have no need to read further. You barely needed to read any of this article at all, to understand what you were already telling yourself I said. Have fun. Or don’t.

The rest of you want explanation. Which makes sense. Many people who hate transgender have told you that you would be fine without female pronouns, and an estrogen-dominant hormone system1, and other women things various, and also that going to church more would make you stop having these thoughts and so forth — clearly they have been wrong and stupid and have not had your best interests in mind. But you already know that I am not like those people. You wonder: how is it, that Halimede, whom you know to be a staunch advocate for transgender, has a view which seems to you to be so associated with wrongful actions against her?

The answer is that you aren’t understanding gender dysphoria correctly.

Maybe I should have told the mob to leave after screencapping that bit. Ha ha.

I do realize that that sounds really bad. I know that you’re in a lot of pain, and that the fact that you weren’t and aren’t treated like you deserve to be is hurting you. I know that being told about the nature of the trap you’re caught in isn’t really a comfort. Sorry. But please hear me out: we’re caught in the same trap.

I want to reiterate something before I continue: I am not transgender. I don’t have it, and never had it, and never will have it unless I don’t know, I get knocked unconscious by an extremely unscrupulous surgeon with very specific sexual preferences and a lot of money. It is precisely because I am not transgender that I can recognize that what you’re terming gender dysphoria is something that affects all women.

Obviously trans women have it worse. I’m not disputing that. There is a difference in magnitude, and in application, but it’s the same fundamental thing.

So. In order to discuss gender dysphoria in women we have to discuss gender in women.

In brief:

Gender is a kind of luminous essence with undoubtedly biological causes, which is then filtered and expressed through social frameworks, which must then be perceived as being confirmed by others. Trans women are women! They have the immutable essence, as is obvious to anybody who’s met you and not been a bigot.

Ok great I’m glad you all understand that.

A given woman can do pretty much anything — she can love gardening, or rock climbing, or driving, or any combination of those things, including none of them at all. Women can love smoking and fiber arts and doing laundry and getting tattoos and getting them removed and crossfit and yoga and sitting at home doing neither, and fish and puzzles and phonics and dizzying heights and Homestuck and the ocean and showering and martial arts and bondage and solitude and topology and ketamine and Final Fantasy and the taste of lavender and anorexia and only wearing blue and the Wars of the League of Cambrai, and terrible card games and the Geisel Library and Coppelia and historical revisionism and having complicated feelings about womanhood and children and child-free lifestyles and anime girl kigurumi and politics and some of them even love men!

But there is a qualifier to this, of course. In every woman’s head, for better or worse, there is a template of womanhood. Not the same one, not for every woman; it’s heavily culturally contingent, but commonalities can be found. This is set deep in her as she grows, as she watches and listens to her mother and her sisters and her friends and the other girls on the playground and all the women she is exposed to. Women, she learns, are supposed to be certain ways. They act and speak and dress and perform in those ways. As she is one, she is also to behave thusly. If she does not, that part of her soul which cries out that she is a woman will not be allowed to remain in communion with that of other women, and cut off from them she will wither.

Every woman can and does deviate from her own perception of that template, by choice or otherwise. And every deviation from that template costs in the eyes of the world, from which she drew that template, and in her own eyes.

Sometimes that cost is something the woman is willing to pay.

For instance: I’m a lesbian, and that subjects me to a level of pressure from outside (homophobia) and inside (internalized homophobia but also this schema-pressure about my gender, which many lesbians resolve by doing something else instead. No thanks. Not me.). And I’m not like, happy about that, but that’s just something I have to live with, since the alternative, of dating men, isn’t something I’m going to ever do. They smell weird. Sorry, all three guys who read my posts.

That pressure — of not living up to what ‘a woman is supposed to be’, as regressive as that idea can be — is what gender dysphoria is. Obviously there is a difference in degree between the ways it hurts you and the ways it hurts me. I’m not that feminine comparatively speaking but people see me that way and one of the things that does for me, besides obligating me to pay pink tax and make men get really annoying about it, is it helps me ‘pay off’ the pressure of that dissonance. I’m happier this way. Trans women are under much more pressure because of their perceived deviance, and they’re usually much less good at woman stuff not because of any innate lack of affinity but because they were punished for wanting it and also nobody told them [its really awful how much nobody just tells trans women things. nobody tells them!!!!]. I was raised to it and you weren’t and you were freer as children, if only because you lied with varying measures of success. And you have it much worse, of course.

But the force is the same.

And there are ways to deal with it.

This model suggests that gender dysphoria is fundamentally relational, and I’ve found that to be true. Nothing soothes my anxieties about being insufficiently ‘a woman’ more than spending time with other lesbians who are women, and the single most important mental health thing for any trans woman who doesn’t have a superlative concern like cancer or unhousedness is spending time with other women, trans and otherwise, who allow themselves to share that they have also had trouble feeling like they deserve to be considered women.

A girl might like swimming, and consequently develop swimmer’s shoulders — and if she spends a lot of her time with, say, the rest of her artistic swimming team, this isn’t going to extract so much of a cost as it otherwise would. The body type becomes more normalized for her if she spends time around peers who have also developed their bodies in the same ways. She can minimize the cost, or remove the source by stopping swimming, or harden herself nacre against the pressure, or titrate out various allowances of deviance, or even get surgery about it. That’s fine.

I’m not against cosmetic surgery for the same reason I’m not against makeup, or clothing. The face you show to the world is a true face. Consider the child with a harelip, the woman who has undergone mastectomy, and the transgender woman. All of these can clearly have their lives improved by surgical intervention — so why shouldn’t they? Most of you belongs to the world. Personhood is something that has to be balanced with womanhood.

But underneath your clothes is different. The parts of the body only shown during intimacy… Womanhood is something that has to be balanced with personhood. There are parts of you that are for the world and parts of you that are not. What’s up your skirt doesn’t matter most of the time, any more than what’s in my pants does to me. When it matters, though, it really matters.

Trans women who don’t get the support they need spiral inward and get progressively more neurotic. I’ve known some of you who wouldn’t be happy without XX chromosomes and an entirely different history — who wouldn’t be happy unless you were entirely different people, nothing like the people you are, and who were therefore incapable of ever attaining happiness. I think that’s an awful way to live. I told one of you many years ago that I wanted her for who she was, not who she could have been. And I think she was too far gone to hear me, but I still had to say it. I hope she’s reading this now. I hope she comes back.

So no, I don’t think you should get the surgery. You can, of course. I can’t stop you. But unless you go around with your genitals out all day where everybody can see them, I don’t think it’ll change anything.

And of course, trans women enable the miracle of lesbian pregnancy. I mean, you could just bank it, but I think there’s something really beautiful and deeply compelling about recognizing a part of the body that we are told exists to hurt and control others as capable of the beautiful and true feminine action of making new life. Personally.

Receive my emails. Pay me money for them if you want. And please, don’t get the surgery.

1

I have yet to ever meet a trans girl who didn’t want this, or whom upon getting it did not get better. I don’t think any trans girl wouldn’t, and if that makes me a ‘transmedicalist’ then I guess that’s what I am.

title: made women
text:
extra context: Unhorsed. if somebody is going to do this to me I deserve the right to mimic in turn.

sufficient context: Merethora, where this story takes place, is a matriarchal horse-archer society.

* * *

Women ride; men walk, and Merha is a horsewoman now. I’ve seen her riding, her hair bound low and streaming behind her to match the tails of her mounts; she took a respectable second in the last archery bout for her age group.

But we were best friends, before they took her away to the inner camp of Datar’s erakt. We were raised by the same men; we sang children’s songs and ate and slept and learned together. Three years as a horsewoman are nothing to that. And if they aren’t, what does it cost me to ask, anyway? She’s always been decent, not just when she’s had to be. To me, at least.

I ask her that evening at the handoff. She slips off her mount, exhausted from a day of hard riding, and I pass her a fresh cold waterskin. This horse likes a scratch on the forehead, and waits obligingly while I unbuckle his tack and set his reins for hot walking.

“Merha?” I say.

“Mm?” She isn’t annoyed with me, probably. She just wants to cool off herself; she always was fastidious.

I don’t even make eye contact. I ask her casually, like it isn’t even a big deal to me; like we’re chatting like the boys we were, watching stews and stitching fabrics together.

“Merha, can you make me a woman?”

She chokes on her drink. Before she’s even done sputtering, she throws up a hand in response.

“Not so loud!” Her harsh whisper carries further than it would have if she’d just spoken softly. “And not here.”

“I don’t see why this is so funny to you. You managed to do it.” I respond.

“You couldn’t ask Sarel?” she says. “She’s your sister.”

“That’s exactly why I can’t ask her.” Besides, Sarel has never had to really work at anything a day in her life. She is an excellent horsewoman; naturally skilled in swordplay and aferan and archery and therefore a terrible teacher, especially of people she likes. Merha has a made-woman’s temperament, and a made-woman’s care for detail. Besides that, I’ve missed her.

She saves me from having to explain that to her, at least. “Fine. Meet me after moonrise tonight at the westernmost storage tent. And stay quiet. It’s normal for somebody my age to be sneaking out with boys, anyway.”

I hadn’t known that, but then, I’m not the kind of boy that girls choose to sneak out with. Something to be aware of in the future, maybe.

Her horse whuffles; I give him a pat on the cheek before I take the reins and walk him out for his cooldown.

* * *

Years of setup and teardown have convinced me I could find my way through camp by memory alone, probably. That won’t be tested tonight. The moon is just past full; moonlight settles around soft-edged shadows, and the spring chill nibbles at my sleeves and the edges of my face.

I slip quietly into the storage tent’s shadow and await Merha’s arrival.

She strides past so loudly anyone might hear her steps. Perfect. I shove her — not hard, just to tease — at the small of her back. I expect her to shriek, or to push me back. She just turns to face me.

We were boys together, and now she’s something else. No, Sarel would have pushed back, I think. It’s just that who she is now is a little less fun.

She looks good, though.

“Let me get my bows,” I say, to break the silence and because I’m excited to explain. I tucked them in the storage tent that afternoon, when nobody was watching. I’ve been experimenting with newer — older — designs. They’re not as efficient as a horsewoman’s recurve but they don’t have to be; I can pull them back just fine. I can make one in a day, if I can get the right wood, and I like how tall they are.

She’s a little skeptical but she’ll come around. She has her own bow and quiver at her back.

“Well, archery is a good place to start,” she says, “so it’s good that you’ve been practicing. But how are you supposed to shoot those on a horse?”

“Well,” I remind her, “that’s what you’re here to teach me!”

“They’re too big. You want precision, not just force, and you get more force with the compound recurve. Just use mine. You’re here to be a horsewoman, aren’t you, not something else.” she rejoins. “Help me carry this tack.”

I leave my bows behind.

* * *

Women ride; men walk. Merha walks like a woman, now, with her weight lower on her body, forging her way through the feathergrass, and I follow, admiring the way the tips of the feathergrass brush appealingly at her thighs.

The horses aren’t too far out. They know the tents as places of safety, and their occupants as riders. A whistle from her and their ears prick up; one scrambles to its feet, but none of them flee. They know her and they like me well enough.

I recognize the two-year-old she rode in to the handoff, and he recognizes me, though he’s a little cold. I don’t hold it against him. I would be too, awoken at this time of night.

“You’re not bad with the horses,” she admits. “Have you ridden?”

I have. Less than I’d like, but I have.

“You could have asked Atani, or Yusa,” she says. Sure. Changing the topic is fine. “Yusa’s going to go back to being a man, you know, when she gets old. Or Sarel, or Algene.”

She shakes her head, like one of the horses.

“I don’t think a corporealist would really help. Yusa likes horses more than people; I‘m not asking my sister, and Algene doesn’t like me.”

“No, she likes you. I caught her watching you a few days ago. She just doesn’t want to admit it. Some girls are like that.”

That isn’t something I’d expected. I’ve never felt anything but irritation from Algene, but Merha basically lives with her; of course she knows her better.

“Are you?” I ask, hoping to put her off balance in turn.

“Am I what?”

“Are you a girl like that?”

She takes a second to think about it. “No. No, I don’t think so. Saddle this one.”

The mare doesn’t know me well, but is tolerant enough, especially following the stallion Merha chooses. She puts me through a series of drills; lean-downs and stances. My bowwomanship is awful; practicing with the longer bow has ingrained bad form, which I’ve been compensating for with brute strength.

I’m sore and laughing by the time we strip the tack to stagger back to camp.

“You could be alright at it, with practice,” Merha says. “Better, with much more practice. But I don’t know if it’ll help.”

“What do you mean?” I ask. “If I’m good enough, I’m good enough, right?”

She shrugs. “Horsewomen know horsewomen, and made-women are horsewomen. I got picked out late. Yusa basically grew up on horseback; she was riding younger than anybody else I’ve ever heard of, and Erhen’s mother found her wearing her jewelry when she was barely old enough to walk. It becomes obvious at puberty, for most of us.”

“And you don’t think I could wear a khitta?”

“Anybody could wear a khitta. Even Aghat.” She smiles at the memory of the man who taught us both to sing. “But it’s not just about that. You don’t hold yourself right. You need to… Imagine you have a sword at your hip. No, not like you have your hand on it and you can defend yourself. Like you know you would draw it. Like you don’t have to draw it.”

“A sword is for keeping myself safe though, isn’t it? What’s the point if I don’t draw it?”

“Look. Part of being a horsewoman is, is being one. Honestly, you’d have better luck with Datar if you just went up to her and declared yourself. I’m not the one you’d have to convince.”

“Well, are you convinced?”

She doesn’t answer my question.

“It’s about not having to ask. I told you, horsewomen know each other.”

* * *

A few weeks pass. We train again and again, as the rivers swell with snowmelt, until Merha considers it possible that I could approach a trajectory ending at something like the skill I will need to convince Datar I might be a horsewoman. The birds seek out mates and horses, gaunt from winter’s scarcity, fill out their frames. When the feathergrasses flower, everyone knows it’s gelding time.

The horsewomen ride out among their herds, assessing which prospective sires have the best potential and wheeling and dealing among themselves until all the stallions are marked with slashes of color. It’s the one night a year where nobody eats red meat. The next day, in the early morning, they bring in the geldings-to-be, heat and sprinkle their knives against infection, and do the bloody work. The severed testicles are cut thin, peeled of membranes and fried in butter and men’s proprietary herb mixtures and snacked on all day. They are by all accounts delicious.

I’ve never eaten any. It just feels wrong. I love meat, and I’m not scared of blood; I was the first of my age-group to bleed a sheep, a feat for which Aghat proclaimed me a man. He lined me a new jacket with the skin, a jacket I passed on to my favorite of the young boys when I outgrew it.

I recognize the use of it. Better that humans have some control over which horses breed and how; better for the futures of every herd and especially for the young males who would be driven out otherwise. It just isn’t something I enjoy thinking about.

Behkte mistakes my discomfort for anticipation and gives me the rest of the day off. Which is nice of him, but I don’t actually want to wander from tent to tent being asked if any women have shown interest in me and chewing on testicles. He’s been going on about his recipe for weeks, and not without reason. I hate how good it smells.

Merha is sitting with Datar and four or so other horsewomen, eating slices off her knife, which she points at me. She slaps her free hand down on her knee.

“So this is the boy you’ve been sneaking off with, Merha? He any good?

Merha makes a face like what can you do.

I feel my own face color. “It’s not like that.”

Datar grins. “Sure. So long as you don’t ever hurt her.”

Sarel waves at me before she chimes in: “Not even a little bit?”

“Fine, fine” Datar retorts. “If he can keep her for a year, they can do whatever they want as long as she’s up in fighting shape in the morning. Without help from Atani.” Then, back to me: “Try some. Seriously. Bekhte’s really outdone himself. I thought he was just bragging but maybe he should be cooking for me instead!”

Merha speaks up. “It isn’t actually like that.”

“Mm?” Datar mumbles through a bite of meat. Whatever herbs Bekhte put in his butter have given it an absolutely mouthwatering fragrance. My stomach turns at the smell. “What’s it like then?”

“I’ve been training him actually. He asked me to. He wants to ride.”

“Like Datar said: is he any good?” says one of the other horsewomen; Erhen, maybe, or Sorghat. She looks me up and down, assessing me like she would a yearling.

Datar smiles with visible relish. Bekhte peels a testicle expertly; slices it, presses it sizzling onto the hot iron fire plate, and moves the next set of ready slices to a set of skewers everybody but me passes around and thanks him for. Somebody asks him for his recipe; he tells her it’s a secret, and that he’s been hoarding traded spices for months just for today. His hairy chin moves up and down as his teeth macerate the meat down into fat and fibers, and the fibers down into wet mush.

“Doesn’t matter,” Datar says, finally. “He doesn’t have the stomach for it.”

“Hey.” I tell her. “How is that fair? I’ll prove it to you.” I know somehow that this will be my only chance to impress her, and I don’t want to lose it. “Put me up against one of yours; I’ll fail by so much less than you think.”

“He has good instincts!” Datar tells Merha. “Keep your eye on this one. He’s a useful man1. But he’s no horsewoman, and he never will be. Too squeamish; values his own balls too highly. I wouldn’t take anybody who wouldn’t eat meat into battle.”

Merha nods, her eyes downcast.

“Cheer up,” Datar tells her. “You don’t have to stop seeing each other. This is the thing with made-women — you aim well but you don’t cut fast enough. Be honest with yourself. He’s no horsewoman, and you knew it from the start. You just wanted to think he was like you. But he isn’t.”

And that is that.

I wait for her that night, at what has become our meeting-place by the westernmost tent.

But she never comes.

52 articles in a year, and more to come. Subscribe here. Even pay me if you want.

* * *

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS:

The author is clearly capable of imitating the source prose more directly. Why hasn’t she done so? What does that imply about the narrator? Why doesn’t the narrator get a name?

In a society where women are the default, what makes a man?

In a society where men are the default, what makes a woman?

Merethorans accept ‘made-women’, a close analog to our conception of transgender women. How are they similar and different, and what do those similarities and differences reveal?

A corporealist has a magic capable of limited reshaping and healing of flesh. What would a corporealist help in this situation? What would she be unable to help? Why or why not?

How does Merha feel?

1

“Useful man” is one word in Merethoran.
