title: the girl you think I am
text:
She is trans, of course. It’s the single most important thing about her. Of course, being trans is the single most important thing about anybody; a trans woman could set any record or cure all cancer forever or cause a genocide and all people would care about was the fact that she was trans. But like more so, for her specifically. Her transness is indelible and inescapable; the shapes of her body and soul have been defined by it in ways that would render a hypothetical version of her who hadn’t suffered in the same ways completely unrecognizable.

She is transgender and she is happy.

Why shouldn’t she be? She’s doing so well, especially for a 36 year-old trans woman. Which is not an easy age or kind of woman to be. She passes, mostly, as long as she doesn’t open her mouth. Being white and a little chubby (lucky for her face, and for her chest) and within the normal bounds of woman’s height (82nd percentile, she knows) does a lot for her. Or enough at least. She only dresses as a boy1 when she absolutely has to, which isn’t often. She’s glad of her gender neutral name for those times she needs it.

She drums her nails on her desk. Click-click click. Click-click click. She did them yesterday: five nails, five stripes on the trans flag. Click-click click. The cuticles are messy but they’ll flake into neat parabolas in a day or so, and until then she doesn’t have any reason to think anybody else will see them. Click-click click. Click.

She’s doing so well. She has a six figure salary now, and a few of the surgeries she’s had her heart set on since she was a teen; the rest are in sight. She paid off her student loans three months ago (though Dad hasn’t been doing so well lately, and she makes sure to help him out where she can, and lately he’s been needing a little more. Which is fine. He doesn’t always get it but she’s going to keep him around as long as she can, just to stick it to her mom.).

This batch of seasonals is excellent; Jadugaar, TGITS, Kaiju Girl Caramelize, Sayonara Lara. She hasn’t even gotten to Kimishinu. Yanineko annoys her but maybe if it gets hyped enough she’ll get back on it; she really hates the presumption that marijuana is the kind of thing that ruins lives. It’s not nearly as bad as alcohol. Wizards of the Coast has finally made their moral rot obvious to anybody bothering to look, and OSR taking off means she barely has to think about how they mangled her favorite game. She pulled Digitan’s Halloween alt on a spare ticket yesterday. Everything’s going her way.

She had last night’s Thai takeout leftovers for breakfast; she already knows her lunch will be open-faced tomato sandwiches. Right now she is sipping tea, which will leave her sufficiently caffeinated. She doesn’t need to use the bathroom or get off or drink more water, and she took a weed gummy recently enough that it wouldn’t be a good idea to take another. She breathes very evenly. She slept alright last night, and the night before, and she doesn’t need any more exercise: she takes long walks on her lunch break on the three days a week she works from home. Nothing could be wrong with her body.

Well, her bangs are getting in her eyes. And there’s all the stuff that is wrong, obviously. But that stuff has always been wrong and there isn’t anything she can do about a lot of it and she’s already had three surgeries and it’s no use thinking about it right now.

She has two girlfriends, both, obviously, transgender: one of whom she visits every three months, who she calls her sister in the right company (she has an actual sister, two years older, who she hasn’t spoken to since she came out). She is negotiating boundaries with the other, who has been insinuating recently that she could move in with her and ignoring her qualms, which are all logistical and therefore unrelated to the fact that she doesn’t actually want this girl to live with her. She’s nice but she doesn’t know if she wants to be that entangled. Yet. That girl is such a furry. The tail is fine, the ears are fine, but kemono is a different thing than that. And besides, living alone has suited her just fine for the past two years.

Nobody is bothering her. There was one neighbor who gave her the stink-eye in the elevator every time but he moved out a month or so ago; his apartment is still empty, as far as she can tell. She’s lucky.

Why shouldn’t she be happy? She has everything she wants.

And of course she has twitter.

She pulls her hair back and low; reconsiders; pulls it high.

This girl you think I am has a whole thing she does, on twitter. It started six years ago, as a way to get back at the cis girl she thought she was going to marry, and now it’s self-soothing in a very different way. She goes on twitter pretending to be her cisgender ex to reassure transgender girls ten years younger than her. She fawns over their bodies and tells them things will get better.

It really will get better for them. It has to. It won’t, for some of them— they’ll detransition or end up like [some names she does not pronounce, even in the safety of her skull] — but the ones who will make it need to hear it, or at least they want to, and hearing it won’t hurt them, the poor stupid things.

No cis woman would really care about them like this. They pretend to; they say the right things, or at least things that sound right enough, and transgender women sucker themselves into believing that their hearts are in the right places at least and that’s good enough as long as it means they get to feel even a little bit included, until the cisgender women in question decide to ruin her entire life. When she says something nice and then never interacts again that’s a needle’s sting — a kind of inoculation against the idea that a real one might someday love you back. Might as well save them the trouble.

And she never could quit her posting habit, anyway.

She stretches in her reddit-recommended desk chair; crosses and uncrosses her long supple legs. She types like the pianist she might have been if she’d stuck with the instrument for more than eight years, like there’s a delicate egg under each of her hands. In a sense, there is. She posts something pointed about how cisgender women just want to use transgender women for their bodies and clicks send.

Half her audience is girls who desperately want a cis woman to use them for their bodies. The other half searches obsessively for secret evidence that she isn’t who she says she is. Both of them are missing the point.

Every post exists primarily to cement her own femininity. The best way to secure one’s womanhood, as she learned from her mother, is to find a woman lower than you on the totem pole2 and posit your superiority over her. She is making them more like herself, in the doing. She would say that she is trying to teach them to be stronger; she would refuse to admit that she considers herself strong. ‘T4T is like incest,’ she said, and she meant it.

She has an acquired taste for spice, left over from the days when her classmates would prove their masculinity with hot sauce and she couldn’t afford to lose. That’s how she weathers the slings and arrows of outrageous internet hatedom. Her relationship to pain informs her perception of transness: to her transness is a wound.

And obviously this causes her to become tremendously sexually compelling but it isn’t good.

She suffers so beautifully, for an audience of only herself. Nobody has ever told her that she is the most beautiful girl in the world, and if anybody did, she wouldn’t believe them. Nobody has ever seen her true self but you.

You are convinced that this girl, who isn’t even real, is me. You are convinced that she is mocking you in some way, or that she is taking something from you, or that she is trying to hurt you by saying what I say. She exists in a great number of your heads and I don’t really know what to do about that. I mean she’s clearly some kind of projection on your part. She’s not you, but she’s somebody who kind of haunts you, or something. And a really distressing number of you are buying, what she is selling.

The scary thing to me is that some of you are so convinced I’m her that you seem to think you’re in, on some kind of joke that there isn’t. And that if I did manage to disprove against her, some number of you would stop caring for my message. It’s like the thing where some you wouldn’t listen to me if I didn’t make my desires obvious, as a means of assuring their authenticity, but opposite and bad; and I don’t know what to do about it.

I could post my face I guess. But that one young transitioner already did that and some of you tried to go after her. If you think a woman is prettier than you, you won’t listen to her; if you think a woman is uglier than you, you don’t think she’s worth listening to. What am I even supposed to do? I mean, aside from continuing to be clear about who I am and the fact that I am not trans.

I don’t really know what to do about this. But I thought I could at least write it down.

* * *

Fifty articles in eleven months. Get more in your email, or pay me for them even.

1

title: Phallic Vulnerability II
text:
Previously: The girl can have that, and it can be touched gently, and she can be vulnerable. She can be girlish, even. She can make a feminine little noise, or even a feminine slightly-larger noise. Gender dysphoria happens when a girl is treated like a man, even by herself. But she is not a man. She can experience pleasure gently rather than forcing another body to provide it to her — and in fact a bit more easily than somebody with the other standard genital set. Her arousal and consequent emotional vulnerability are readily apparent. She doesn’t have to hate her body for the weapon that people think it is and the harm they think it could cause, because she isn’t causing any harm with it. She can give and take pleasure mutually. She can be loved.

* * *

So in Part I I established the thesis underlying a counter-framework to the common understanding of the penis as an implement used to dominate, control, and cause harm. Maybe that all stuff holds true for everybody else’s penises; I don’t really care. But when a transgender woman has it, that is a special kind of vulnerability, not a threat or weapon.

How does that organ make her vulnerable?

Well, society hates the clitoris. No wonder that a transgender woman, who has essentially biologically more of that, causes such revulsion. But beyond that:

We’re used to thinking about the vulnerabilities conferred by the standard set of female genitalia1; menses is painful and messy, pregnancy and childbirth exact heavy tolls on the body, and the womb’s ability to be impregnated irrelevantly to its bearer’s consent is the source of a truly horrific amount of fear and suffering.2

What, then, are the vulnerabilities associated with the non-standard set?

Chief among these is the social. Transphobes hate the whole transgender woman of course but the part they hate the most is her penis — hence their fixation on policing bathrooms and sexuality. Just by having that she is rendered vulnerable to the predations of bigots who use it as a justification for declaring her a threat, to the point where many trans pursue surgical intervention to feel safe.

Now of course this vulnerability wouldn’t matter in a post-transphobic world, but despite my best efforts we aren’t yet there. The fear of involuntary impregnation wouldn’t matter in a truly feminist world either.

Obviously nobody3 enjoys an impact between the legs but trans women have, well, more attack surface. Her there is vulnerable to both social threat of revelation and physical attack — but the most beautiful vulnerability that her transness gives her is, I would say, her lack of ability to conceal physiological arousal.

* * *

APPLICATIONS AND IMPLICATIONS:

Given that her there is a delicate and vulnerable place, how should she be touched?

Gently. Softly. Obviously on estrogen her whole body becomes more sensitive, and she more comfortable with being touched on it. One of the most awful bigotries is touch starvation — though you may find it necessary to just hold her for a while while she cries and such. Which can also be nice. But maybe not what you were looking for. There are so many places on a transgender girl that she is so starved of touch for; put your fingers to them. Neck, ears, inner wrists; the small of her back, the gap of her thighs, her feet . Her there is important but it’s not like sex for anybody is just that.4

You may find it necessary to counterbalance her lingering body image problems with her there, no matter how much biology on the homologous structure of the clitoris you impart to her. The ideal method is by gently stimulating her nipples, a pretty definitively girl part of her body that she will not have thought to touch herself. Or else she just pulled on them way too hard and then got discouraged, because nobody tells trans women that that isn’t how to do it. There really should be a book. Written in a clinical yet accessible style.

What about oral?

Well what about it? Straight people and gay men seem to think that giving head is a fundamentally submissive act. Ridiculous. Only lesbians are reasonable about the whole thing. Just like basically every other romantic and sexual norm. Giving head, like almost everything else, is contextually dominant, submissive, or uncharged depending on the people, roles, and energies involved.

You are putting her most vulnerable place right by your teeth. She is the one who has to trust you here. Obviously she can take charge with her that, and possibly some sidenafil, but the default expectation is that the person with the sharp bits is the person in control. Of course it can be fun to pretend otherwise but you should be aware; it may be expedient to convince her that it isn’t something that’s going to hurt you, by putting your own fingers and such in her mouth, and also yours.

What about the strap?

Well, the strap is pretty definitely an implement of dominance. I guess somebody could sub with one of those but it isn’t really… it’s used to cause sensations, not feel them. Look okay I know about strapless and double-ended and texture-ended of those but given the angles they do stimulate and the ones they don’t it’s not a vulnerability. The strap can feel good, and can provide psychological and physiological pleasure to the person using it, but it’s not sensitive in the ways that an actual body part is.5

But a strap can be considered such an implement because that’s how it functions, and it can function that way, as a permanent marker of dominance, because it is removable! Trans can remove hers, once, but then she stops being trans, and also the strap is good at and for different things. Probably if you’re the type who likes using one it’s great to use on a trans. But I’m not interested in doing that myself.

Well this advice all seems a little lesbian-centric. What about men?

Well what about men? I am a lesbian so of course all my advice is lesbian-centric. Well then, men, what you should do is talk to your straight or bisexual transgender woman, and listen to and satisfy all her needs. Simple enough. Don’t mess her up.

title: how you should treat nonbinary people
text:
It has come to my attention that a lot of you have no idea how to treat nonbinary people. I mean, most people really have no idea how to do this, but you transgender women especially need to be told how — because the general public seems to think that you and they are kind of the same thing. You aren’t, of course. But nonbinary people also often don’t know very much about you, and often assume that you have similar kinds of stuff going on. Which you do, in some ways, and not in others, but not in the ways that they often seem to think.

And it seems like people who aren’t transgender women, may also want advice on such matters. Most of this advice should be generalizable anyways.

So: in order to understand how to treat nonbinary you have to understand what they’re trying to do, and then you have to understand how they think of you and what they want and don’t want from you. And in order to understand all of that, you have to understand what nonbinary people as a category want.

It’s a very broad category! Trans women are very easy to understand: each and every one of you contains a kind of divine essence-light of womanhood but has a bit of trouble actualizing it due to a biological error and consequent social effects. You are able to actualize it by getting on the proper hormones and such. And it radiates out through you beautifully. Trans men are also very easy to understand: stupid parents raise boys as girls sometimes but it doesn’t make them girls. Though it does make them gay a lot of the time.

Nonbinary though… That’s a very big tent. Is being nonbinary an intentional political decision? Is being nonbinary due to having some kind of innate biological factor? Is what they want even possible, let alone desirable?

This differs I think by individual nonbinary and also it doesn’t really matter to me. It’s not my problem1. The problem is that most people don’t know how to interact with them, and I’m here to fix that, because I support transgender women.

* * *

So in order to interact with nonbinary you have to know about them. Here’s some types.

As I have said: there are nonbinary people who really want to talk about being nonbinary and make sure you know their pronouns and nonbinary people who really don’t want to talk about it at all with anybody who isn’t a close friend, and even then only sparingly.

The first is a bit easier to interact with because they really want to talk about it. So you can just listen to them and ask questions that indicate that you’re listening. And you shouldn’t bring it up with the ones who don’t.

There are, thankfully, many other ways to subdivide and categorize people using this label.

There are nonbinary people who are culturally lesbian or gay or bisexual, nonbinary people who are not, and nonbinary people who have taken up that label as a means of defining their relationship to queerness or their relationship to straight people. Some nonbinary people do it descriptively, and some nonbinary people do it aspirationally. There are nonbinary people who report feeling clearly and specifically like they have a nonbinary gender. There are nonbinary people who report feeling no gender and decide that nonbinary gender is the best way for them to express that. There are nonbinary people who use the label and then go on to transition in binary ways, and nonbinary people who have tried transitioning in binary ways and found that that was very much not something they wanted and nonbinary people who don’t conceptualize whatever they do as a transition at all. There are nonbinary people fixated on presenting androgynously, nonbinary people who want to have many clashing gendered signifiers, nonbinary people who want to have as few gendered signifiers as possible, and nonbinary people who get really into schemas like childhood or seeing themselves as like robots or animals that they think of as free from gendered norms. I’ve known rude nonbinary people and I’ve known boring nonbinary people and I’ve known reasonable nonbinary people and I’ve known nonbinary people who really like to draw me crying in backless dresses. I don’t know what’s up with that last group. I mean it’s very nice but it’s also a little weird. But like it’s fine.

Joe Biden was so right when he said that there are at least three genders. You have the two cardinal clusters, of girls -> women and boys -> men, various deviances among them, like gay, and then you have all these people trying to do their own specific things. Really the only thing uniting nonbinary is that they have a contentious relationship to at least one gender, to the point that they are trying to get it off them, and they aren’t doing the other cardinal one.

There are however a few broad patterns:

Nonbinary people who declare themselves as such are more likely to be people expected to be women than people expected to be men. There are three main reasons for this:

People raised as men are far less likely to think of themselves as restricted by their gender presentation at all, in part because they are less restricted and in part because manliness is considered a power to be taken up, not something with downsides2. Conversely, there is an awareness among people raised as women that womanhood is a thing that chokes, and so many more people raised as women are able to conceptualize that “this is something that I want to escape.”

When the general public sees people it perceives to be women deviating from their gender role, the perception is that they should be ignored, and then corrected if that is deemed necessary. Their agency is denied and they are considered misguided, not dangerous. When the general public sees people who are perceived to be men deviating from their gender role, however, those people get hate-crimed. So it’s easier for people perceived to be women to be nonbinary, because they get ignored about it rather than deemed dangerous, and nonbinary people perceived to be men mostly keep their heads down. These patterns are most obvious when you look at how trans women and trans men are treated but they arise as a reaction to transgression, so they also apply to nonbinary people.

People with any kind of cultural marker collect themselves around themselves, and people who are expected to be women mostly know other people expected to be women.

Nonbinary people don’t really have a cultural place. We have sets of things for women, and men, and subsets of those categories, and yes there are various third-gendered groups of various levels of slur-hood in various places around the world, but there isn’t really a spot for them mostly. They are kind of defined by not having one. They are keenly aware of this and they want to be seen as not being the gender they were raised to be, and so many of them are trying to make this spot, very loudly. This is a natural point of friction with transgender women, many of who (claim to) just want to be normal women who dissolve into society3

Consequently nonbinary people tend to be concerned with visibility, especially that of visible gender nonconformity. Of course they are. They are trying to get an entire other gender role than the Cardinal Two to exist. It’s true that there are seemingly antithetical subsets of the cardinal two — gay men and lesbians among them; lesbianism is a structure that serves many of the same roles as a gender in lesbian lives, to the point where many consider ‘lesbian’ to be their gender4 since so much of conventional womanhood is about men . But a third entire, is another thing altogether. Theys are often jealous of the hypervisibility that trans women get, because they think if they had it they could put it to use. They couldn’t, of course. The grass is greener always, on the other side of the fence. But for a group who people roll their eyes at and turn away from, the fantasy of being seen seems like the first part of being listened to. As a transgender woman — as a woman — you have to figure out how to give grace to people who are jealous of you even when maybe they shouldn’t be.

* * *

As a transgender woman — as a woman — you have to figure out how to give grace to people who are jealous of you. Even when maybe they shouldn’t be.

* * *

I should play with insert quotes more often. That’s so fun! Anyways.

Nonbinary people are often new to being nonbinary. Just like trans women new to acting her truest self becoming often start seeing transness everywhere, nonbinary people tend to project their own experiences onto others. This goes very badly for everybody when they start going on about how actually gender is so flexible and not real, because for most people, myself included, gender is very inflexible and very real.

As I’ve said: The two conventional cardinal genders work just fine for most people but categorization systems should accurately reflect their data points; having another cluster specifically defined by not being men or women seems like a good idea because some people are best understood as neither men nor women, and describing them as such just doesn’t give very good results. There should be a place for the placeless. Even if it isn’t going to capture them all because there is always going to be somebody with a boutique gender designed specifically to upend all metrics, it’s going to fit more people better and therefore be a good system. Nonbinary people deserve to be socially legible — to not be asked about their pronouns unless they want to be; to get to have names that declare them as nonbinary, and to be treated as such, once they decide what that means; to have different things expected of them than society asks of men and women.

I don’t really think they will succeed but I think it’s a valiant effort. I think the idea that people could escape is a beautiful one, and that the impossibility of achieving this dream makes me more well-inclined towards it. My views on this are like… well, I don’t agree with a lot of Socialist thought but I think it’s pretty clear that a move leftward is necessary to counter the right-wing right now; all things move towards the center, in time. It’s like that. If they succeed, there will be a slightly different system; a better-fitting one once their ideals actually come back to Earth. That is something I am unequivocally in favor of.

As you know, people who are transgender women and aren’t transitioning get really twisted about the whole thing. In that same way, nonbinary people who haven’t made significant life changes accordingly (getting on hrt, making themselves visibly nonbinary, doing whatever it takes for them to feel nonbinary) tend to get weird about it. So be aware of that.

Now you might have questions, like “so how does dating work if the people a nonbinary wants to date are attracted to them for traits/behaviors/body parts they don’t like having?” or “how does somebody know if they’re nonbinary instead of just a gender non-conforming member of a gender” or “why aren’t they bothered by being grouped with women in Women And Nonbinary groups all the time”? Those cans of worms are nonbinarys own business, and not my problem. Or yours most likely. If they are, you should talk that out with the nonbinary in question.

* * *

So now that you know basically what the deal with nonbinary is, and how somebody like that may think of you, how do you treat them?

Obviously you should take people at their word and make a good faith effort to refer to them with their names and pronouns as long as they aren’t transparently lying to you about those things. If they are lying about those things it will be obvious. If you slip up, apologize without making a huge deal of it and continue the conversation.

They are trying to be in a different box, which they are also actively trying to construct, and so it is rude to position them in one of the standard two. Consider them as acting in roles5 rather than related to you by polarities of gender. Asking somebody nonbinary to do something very gendered (attend your bridal shower, enter your locker room with you) should be considered weird. If you do, you should position your attitudes towards them against the gender they’re trying to escape. Ask beforehand of course but assuming ‘guy stuff’ for ones who are pointedly not girls and ‘girl stuff’ for ones who are pointedly not guys (while also being sure not to alienate them from portions of their contexts that they want to keep) indicates that you take them seriously.

It’s also important to be aware of their feelings about their life histories — for instance a nonbinary who is pointedly not a woman may have the thing that women do about wanting to inflict womanhood on others, from having had that levied on them in childhood, and may be willing to teach you skills that you might be stressed about learning from a woman. They are often less likely to pick these skills up because of the alienation, but may also have put disproportionate work into them in attempts to fit in. It depends, as with almost everything with thems, on the individual they in question and the life that has produced them.

Nonbinary can come from almost anywhere really, even just raised by their parents without gender stuff, though this is rare. Nonbinary often comes from lesbian (there are a lot of he/they gay men, particularly in academia, who are nonbinary and don’t really want to discuss it as well). Nonbinary can come from just about any kind of person except transgender women. No transgender women can ever be nonbinary. If a transgender woman ever declares herself to be a nonbinary, that is an act of self-harm. She needs attention, and you should give it to her while making it clear that she can get more of it and better than from hurting herself with that, in other, more productive ways.

And that, transgender women, is the most important thing you need to know about nonbinary: that’s not you. That does mean it’s ethically acceptable for you to marry them, a thing which a number of you do that would be surprising to people who didn’t know you as well as I do.

title: Otakon 2026
text:
Otakon 2026 was so exhausting and so so good.

Panels:

Didn’t do many this year since a few longtime friends made their ways there and we spent our time catching up. Really great to be in the room when Discotek announced that they got the licenses for Penguindrum, Patlabor, and Toradora!

Artist’s Alley:

Was hoping to see that one mech artist for Dianna and Kihel charms but it looks like they didn’t make it in this year… Lovely to see so many Uma charms. A few even, of my favorite. This is where most of the Amedeji merch ended up, though I did see the manga at Kinokuniya’s booth.

Dealer’s Hall:

Retro Saikou always has the good stuff. Picked up the Turn A Gundam soundtrack CDs; was hoping for a Turn A Laserdisc to frame but there’s always next year. Notable sights: Shaddiq Zenelli charms 2$ (NOBODY WANTS HIM); Hidamari Sketch Honeycomb, Namaniku ATK, and Kanbaru Suruga artbooks; copies of the Higurashi shooting game and the Umineko fighting game; Madoka Movie premiere pamphlets. Their Type-Moon wall is always a delight, and this year there was a sealed first edition Tsukihime copy! The coolest thing on display was a laserdisc of the Daicon III and IV opening animations. Very happy to see the annual Watch Symphogear! sign with an And Umamusume Too!

Fragmented Nostalgia specializes in magical girls; I was particularly enchanted by the pair of Utena’s shoes they had on display. Apparently the Anthy pair already got snapped up. I would have bought them but that would have made me feel like Touga.

Akiba Anime Store’s prices are on the expensive side but having a big table of unsorted Umamusume merch to pick through created a natural meeting point and center of conversation for Uma fans and cosplayers as people announced what horsegirls they were seeking. So many people wanted TM Opera O! Right next to that they had some fanbooks and uma plushies and wall scrolls etc but the best thing there was a shelf of SK Japan Throughbred plushies, labeled only in katakana. I got to help people find their oshis! Didn’t find any 99gen (with the exception of Haru) though… I was really hoping for an Adobe1. Perhaps next year.

Gundam Planet wasn’t in the Dealer’s Hall but their Mecha Kaikan setup is so nice. Love to watch a panel on 60s and 70s mecha history while snipping out and assembling a little robot. A friend who flew in with me got to build her first gunpla!!! Thanks Gundam Planet. They saved a crate of Turn Xs and sold them for a very fair price; if they didn’t already have my loyalty as a customer that would have earned it for sure.

Encounters:

A Shiki Ryougi! And an Arcueid nearby who was visibly miffed I didn’t call her out for a picture. Sorry. If you wanted me to get a photo, you should have been cosplaying the better Type-Moon heroine.

Two Nakayamas Festa at a fancy self-shuffling mahjong table with an Agnes Tachyon and a Tomoko Kuroki. I’m pretty sure that was an episode of Akagi. or possibly Saki: Achiga-hen.

A Panty and a Stocking doing their nails on the train in.

Three of you, my loyal followers. Thanks for taking me out to lunch. :)

Quite a lot of Saiki K cosplayers who I kept mistaking for wearing Shadow Girls uniforms.

Three Anthies and their Utenas. A Saionji and a Touga. and one Juri, walking around with a Ruka.

A Paptimus Srirocco who, on being asked for a picture, walked up and wordlessly handed me a tiny plastic haro.

SO MANY UMAMUSUME. I was at the photoshoot, though I didn’t cosplay as an Uma. Here are some highlights:

A Tannhauser asked a Fukukitaru to bless her 10 roll. Fuku did the whole Woiya Happy! Haiya Lucky! chant, totally focused, hands moving over the phone… and Tannhauser got nothing whatsoever. Sorry Mambo. Your luck was character accurate. Actually, of the two Tannhausers, one lacked a hat and one lacked ears. Not by any fault of their own either… No wonder they were drawn to her enough to cosplay her.

A Curren Chan who did all the poses. #cutecurren #lovecurren #lookatcurren. #LookAtCurren.

One single Smart Falcon who went up alone in front of everybody and did all the ridiculous cutesy posing you would expect of Smart Falcon, to massive applause.

Six Symbolis Rudolf, one of whom was wearing a DILF hat. I met two early on, then three, then by the photoshoot time they had arrayed themselves in an orderly queue waiting to be called and passing the names of the next umas to be called along to the audience. They had perfect postures, upright ears, and immaculately-planned schedules.

Two Gentildonnas flexing their back muscles, a Brian who did the fist, and a Hishiama with the little gochisosama puppet who did the claws! And a Mayano Top Gun who ran up with her arms out like an airplane. Lovely.

Two Still In Loves who did a pose with one of them reaching out and one hiding her face.

4-5 TM Opera Os gently holding the arms of their Meishos Doto. Such a good couple’s cosplay. Also, a Vodka and Daiwa Scarlet who were clearly dating — right by all the Digitans. Honestly Digitan would be so fun… you could get a friend to ask for pictures and position yourself in the background with binoculars for all of them…

Seven or so Taikis Shuttles! Other horses in this category: Rice Shower, Tokai Teio, Stay Gold, Silence Suzuka.

The cutest little elementary schooler. Fusaichi Pandora. Nobody knew her so it took them towards the end to call her. But when Main Story 2 rolls around, people will see she was a true feminist all along.

Various Daitaku Helioses doing 6-7. Of course.

A KFC Collab Tachyon?! You had like what, a week to make that?????

A Bakushin who nailed the ridiculous laugh.

A Dream Journey doing the Dream Journey Victory Pose but with two fingers out and down. Like for. well. We know.

A Silence Suzuka driving a mobility device and another Suzuka who posed like she was running her over. Wow. That’s a lot. Suzukas can reclaim though, I think.

Most represented horses: Oguri, Golshi, Mcqueen, Tachyon, Cafe. Also a whole bunch of Trainers. It looks like BOANE and Cingrey are the entries American fandom likes the most. As for unreleased horses, people love Gentildonna and Stego + the entire Gold Clan.

And get this: THERE WAS NOT A SINGLE SPECIAL WEEK. Wild!

* * *

Jaxxes in maid outfits I guarantee you were not fooling anyone.

* * *

FANDOMS ASCENDANT: Amedigi, more recent Jojo parts, Panty and Stocking, Umamusume. more Lolitas. Kasane Teto.

FANDOMS TRIUMPHANT: Deltarune, Touhou (so many mokous), Final Fantasy, Vtubers, Pokemon (eevee and evolutions especially), Guilty Gear, Witch Hat Atelier. It feels like all the Vash and Wolfwood people went for Qifrey and Olruggio.

FANDOMS DECLINING: Genshin (though Honkai might have had something to do with this, splitting up the Hoyoverse cosplayers), Chainsaw Man, Studio Trigger Shows That Aren’t Panty And Stocking, Trigun: Stampede, Frieren

FANDOMS EVER-PRESENT: 07th Expansion, Soul Eater, DMMD. and of course I saw a Vriska.

* * *

You want more of this kind of thing in your inbox, don’t you. yes you do. I’m sorry

look I have to get the database animal raving out of my system somehow. so you get to read this. thankfully for the dignity of all involved, this little rant won’t take up An Article Slot — I have one I’m working on for later this week.

1

title: My Ideal Odyssey
text:
There’s been a lot of buzz about Christopher Nolan’s Odyssey lately. Well let me tell you: I haven’t seen it and I don’t particularly want to. Every generation, newly infatuated, bends the Classics to its own modernity; the texts are deep and strong, and they can take it, but that doesn’t mean I have to like it.

It’s just. People keep taking whatever they want out of the damn things. Supergiant keeps making very fun games that are deeply upsetting to me as somebody who cares about how stories end; Campbell’s corpse should be dragged through the streets. Dan Simmons’ Illium vexed me in middle school. I wanted to like Madeline Miller’s Circe; really, I did. But it was just so bad that I returned her Song Of Achilles to the library without reading it and had to have a very awkward conversation with a book club I am thankfully no longer part of1.

I don’t mean to be a snob, or worse, a fundamentalist. Obviously to read, and to write from reading, is to bring one’s own self and cultural context to a (hopefully grounded) approach to the work. So that’s what I’m doing. I am bringing my own self, and my experiences, and my cultural contexts to The Odyssey, to produce my ideal adaptation.

* * *

Here is the crux of my ideal adaptation of The Odyssey: I don’t think Odysseus could make it through Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.

Obviously he wouldn’t be able to read English. But I think the problems go deeper than that.

* * *

But not by will nor valor could he save them,

for their own recklessness destroyed them all—

children and fools, they gorged themselves fat

on waterfall-frothed chocolate, and were taken up in tubes;

men pressed as grapes to wine for their presumptions,

unmindful others borne to deep and sunless tombs.

The last to their ends were moved

by their own devices.

Consider, of course, The Chocolate Waterfall Room — a test right out of the tales Odysseus spun for the Phaeacians, full of horror at the breach of ξενία by consumption2.

Wonka seems at first to honor guest-friendship. He offers his wondrous chocolate gardens freely to the hungry; Charles and Joseph Bucket indulge, delighted. Only when Augustus Gloop falls in, contaminating the entire chocolate river, does Wonka exact his punishment — for ruining food, Augustus is rendered3 thin. If we grant, as the Greeks might, that in contaminating a great deal of valuable foodstuffs Augustus has committed a crime against his host, then Wonka is well within his rights to answer that transgression with an appropriately ironic punishment. Remember, he does send him off with a truckload of candy and the promise of a lifetime supply afterwards. In time Augustus Gloop will surely return to his former stature. No lasting harm has been done, except possibly to his psyche.

Odysseus’ men would not be so lucky. None but the man of many ways himself are so god-favored as to receive a Golden Ticket; the only way at all reasonable for the black ships to end up at Wonka’s Chocolate Factory is for them to have been blown far, far off course. The men are (as Odysseus makes a point of mentioning on multiple occasions) starving, and cannot all be reasonably expected to understand all the hygienic principles that underly modern food safety. Only Odysseus manages to obey the proper courtesies and present Wonka with a gift: a silver-studded sword won from the Sack of Troy. Wonka takes a shine to it, and wears it at his own belt, though he disparages it as a weapon; perhaps, he says, it will serve some Oompa-Loompa in cutting rare fruit. But the gaze of Willy Wonka falls harsh upon those who follow not his laws, and we can safely assume those who do fall in and get sucked up the tubes will never return to Argive shores.

Next of course is Violet Beauregard’s trial: the stick of chewing gum. Those who have not read the original text, and are familiar via the strictly inferior movie adaptations, will likely fail to appreciate the actual test here: while Violet’s gum-chewing is certainly unsanitary, her real crime against Wonka here is her pursuit of κλέος4 at his expense, a distinction which would not have been lost on the Greeks. For weary and long-suffering Odysseus to take part in the Phaeacian games, and for him to fire the fateful arrow through the ten axe-heads, he must first be roused to action by insult. To display virtue is fitting, but virtue, especially that demonstrated by skill in arms— as in so many Greek games— must be rendered seemly through the guest-compact. Recall: Odysseus responds to Euryalus’ taunts by issuing his own challenges to all save Laodamas, son of his host Alcinous.

Who quarrels with his host?

Only a madman—or no man at all—

would challenge his protector among strangers,

cutting the ground away under his feet.

(Odyssey VIII.217-220, trans. Fitzgerald, 1961)

Violet Beauregard has no such care. She presumes to take one of her host’s treasures and suffers the inevitable result.

Here Odysseus and his men fare better. Troy is not so far from Chios, where mastic resin (the astute reader may recognize the root from which our mastication is derived) has long been produced, and gum is not known for its nutritionally-sustaining qualities (besides which, many of the men have already sated themselves at the chocolate waterfall). The lure here is in their desire to prove themselves at cost to their host. Whichever of them take the gum are lost — but the chocolate waterfall has conclusively demonstrated that Wonka’s domain is full of dangers, and they likely heed his warnings.

As you know, Veruca Salt is hurled down the trash chute by Wonka’s army of trained squirrels. She is punished for her greed, and while the opening of Aeolus’ sack of winds handily demonstrates the greed of Odysseus’ crew, I think it likely that several of them perish here for a different reason: here, at last, they are tempted with what is to them reasonable food. One imagines no small contingent of the men wary of chocolate and confectionry unrecognizable to them, and still starving as a result; these would certainly recognize nuts and squirrels as edible and suffer the consequent downfall. Eurylochus might credibly be described as a “bad nut”. Remember: Eurylochus fears to return to Circe, a cowardice for which Odysseus considers killing him, and Charles Bucket only receives the Golden Ticket after spending a ten of the fifty-pence with which he should really buy food for his own starving family on a second Wonka’s Whipple-Scrumptious Fudgemallow Delight bar. In both Homeric and Dahlian cosmologies, ambition and indulgence are rewarded — so long as hubris is held in check. One imagines Eurylochus’ rhetoric: the crew are simple men; they presume not above their station, and will partake in food befitting of it. Surely they have now passed the tests set before them, and surely the Lord of the Factory will be merciful.

But if he flares up over his rodents lost,

wishing our lives destroyed, and if the gods

make cause with him, why, then I say: Better

whatever fate he has in store for us

than waste to skin and bones far from the sun!

Here Wonka will be identified with the Divine; perhaps in an attempt (however futile) to assuage his wrath. Odysseus, skilled in all ways of contending, must by this point have recognized Wonka’s malicious intent. Unsure of the candy-maker’s capabilities, as when he observes suitors and Phaeacians alike, the great tactician bides his time.

The fourth test is the Chocolate Television teleporter. The Nut Sorting Room tests for idiocy, and this one, its counterpart, for love of one’s own intelligence — a trap set for Mike Teevee, and perhaps for Odysseus himself. Though Mike Teevee is a tedious child, many of his criticisms are quite reasonable! But like the rest he fails.

At the fourth test, the deliberate nature of Wonka’s cruelty becomes obvious. In seeming accordance with the laws of guest-friendship, he offers the remaining men a way home. Having progressed through the Great Glass Lift, and being terrified by the godlike powers Wonka demonstrably possesses, the second that television shows their homelands (and it will! Willy Wonka’s Chocolate Factory holds temptations custom-tailored to any victim he pleases) the last of Odysseus’ men plunge into the screen, never to return. There are no televisions in Ithaca.

And now war-wise Odysseus readies himself. Wonka may seem to him like a god, and as with the gods, his vengeance is always justified — and yet even earth-shaking Poseidon relents, in his time. As with Penelope and the olive-trunk bed, the man of action understands that there is a time for tests and that that time is over. William Wonka has intentionally sabotaged his crew by setting forth challenges he knows they will fail. If he is a god, then there is little to be done5. Athena intercedes, but not when men call her; the grey-eyed goddess helps those who help themselves. But if he is a man, he can surely be killed.

How have we wronged you, wily Odysseus asks. Lord of men, skilled in craft and rich beyond compare, why have you treated us so? I gave you my very sword.

You have contaminated my chocolate, and chewed of my gum, and tried to eat my squirrels, and jumped into my television, replies Wonka. I warned you against all those things! I told all those men that they shouldn’t have done what they did! You at least gave me a sword about it. But you’re still going to have to go. You’re neither moldable nor young enough to inherit my chocolate empire.

I will go peacefully, says lying Odysseus, if you will but answer a single question. How did you earn Olympus’ favor, that the gods have blessed you so?

William Wonka recognizes his own methodology — Odysseus has given him just enough rope to hang himself with. His ego will not let him deny his own success, and the powers that back Odysseus will certainly empower him if he speaks against them.

The ways of the gods are mysterious, Wonka replies. I must have done something right.

And then many-minded Odysseus is on him.

They share a single fierce kiss, tumbling on the floor. Wonka draws blood. But it’s Odysseus who comes out on top: he has drawn the sword at Wonka’s waist and stabbed it deep into the floorboards with the crossguard at William’s neck, so that a single gulp will draw blood from his throat — and now his mouth is full of Odysseus’ saliva.

In keeping with Wonka’s own perversion of ξενία, complicated Odysseus has allowed him a way out— so long as he does not succumb to temptation.

William can only chuckle, and lightly, lest the blade part his skin; he has been bested and bound by the very guest-gift which he so appreciated.

Up through the Factory Odysseus journeys, through rooms unfathomable to him and to us. He makes up a story about his men eating the Cattle of the Sun. That will be easier to explain. Making it through the Chocolate Factory— really making it through, not just limping away with a bloodied tongue — means earning Wonka’s approval. Odysseus knows that for all the passion in their bodies, that man would kill him if he ever saw him again.

Oh, and the Oompa-Loompas should sing in dactylic hexameter.

“Herald! Here, subscribe to Halimede. Let her feast and be merry, with my compliments. All men owe honor to the poets — honor and awe, for they are dearest to the Muse who puts upon their lips the ways of life.”

title: Phallic Vulnerability
text:
cw: frank discussion of transmisogyny, with examples.

Context: pink and purple, a part at the seam, the penis monologues

The depth of hatred bigots display towards transgender women is horrifying in ways that non-transgender women often struggle to grasp. Even still, after years of defending trans women, I occasionally encounter an allegation so sick that it makes me tear up and the transgender women who see it sigh wearily. These people define their entire lives around ruining the lives of innocent transgender women — and they hate no part more of her than her penis.

And so it is her penis that they seek to destroy.

This is a particularly pernicious avenue of attack because many people are very used to being scared of penises. We live in a society that mythologizes masculine penis-worship cults. Achilles is picked out from the women of Lycomedes’ court when he grasps his father’s ash-wood spear; the term vagina originates as a euphemism for scabbard, ie; that into which a sword is thrust. Men are taught to treat their penises like guns and swords; weapons charged by their ability to rape, wound, and invade. Those who have been subject to men (weaker men included) are taught that the phallus is a vector for harm through culture and experience.

Consider the violence of the verbs we use for the act of penetrating: ‘smash’, ‘crack’, ‘bang’, ‘hit’, (as well of course the lack of words denoting activity and agency for the act of getting penetrated). But these contexts are necessarily invoked to weaponize the penis because the penis is a body part, not a weapon. You know what else people use to do lots of horrible things to others? Hands! The hand is the implement of control, and yet we recognize that it can perform gentlenesses as well as violences.

Unfortunately as long as men keep being like that about their penises, I fear the uninformed are going to assume that a woman with a that would be the same way. Even a second’s thought makes it obvious how wrong this is. If a woman had such, as some women do, she would go about her life mostly normally, and hide it, of fear that people would consider her a sexual aggressor. But most people rarely give this that second thought, and so the cultural connotations of the penis continue to be used to persecute women.

THEREFORE. In the interest of protecting transgender women’s bodies, I propose a new discursive framework centered around the following proposition: the transgender woman’s penis is a marker of her vulnerability.

We can get there through anime.

* * *

ANIME

That’s right. This is actually Weeaboo Womanhood III: Girls Who Have It.

Weeaboo Womanhood I and Weeaboo Womanhood II are Required Reading. This isn’t going to make any sense without them.

So: how do we see trans women, or at least, women with traits characteristic of trans women, in popular culture?

You can get there via the classic tall and beautiful neurotic and anorexic top: Rei Asaka, Grell Sutcliff, Jinshi, Symboli Rudolf, Saber1. She is so beautiful, and so tortured. She is typically an object of desire — if a purer and more beautiful desire than many of the representations of twomen later on this list — rather than a protagonist, so it’s difficult to access her internality.

Also sometimes transgender happens because an editor insists that something be changed but the author doesn’t really want to change it so they write her like that anyway. Hiro Hidamarisketch, Kurako Koibuchi2, Saber. This kind of thing is rare, though less than you might think.

But these two types of woman are not usually recognized as transgender3 women, but as ‘tall cold women with problems’ or ‘oh, a woman with a relatively normal relationship to femininity.’ or Saber. Phallic vulnerability isn’t really applicable here, except insofar as it fits with the tendencies of both categories to conceal their true intentions and have repressed sexualities.

Very well then. Let us discuss Girls Who Explicitly have That. Girls Who Explicitly Have That traditionally fall into three categories:

Tall, stacked, often racialized, and sexually aggressive, ex. Motoko Kusanagi, Poison4, certain Umamusume. This is the ‘third-gendered’ category, though she may be depicted as intersex. The intended eroticism for the Male Reader here is in either in being penetrated/having boundaries broken by a more sexually experienced woman or in conquering a woman with an attribute narratively associated with masculinity; consequently if she has it she very much has it a lot.

In her case, the phallus is a tool of domination. Just on a woman. And while there are certainly trans women with such relationships to thereof, and while they are very beautiful, they are beautiful despite the pressures which this archetype applies to them, not because of it. And her phallus is certainly not vulnerable. Except in the way that even those of cisgender men are (as much as they hate to admit it), by virtue of having bits that can be hit.

‘Trap’ girls. What a despicable thing to call her. You can tell these are girls because they are subject to misogyny and that particular flavor of sexual debasement that people feel free to direct at transgender women. Nobody is more ‘not like the other girls’ than the girl who claims to not be a girl at all. These are typically bottoms, in keeping with roles expected of women. Chihiro Fujisaki, the Mariya Shido type (though Mariya herself is obviously a top), Bridget, Saber. Clearly has internality but the role demands its suppression. If you’ve ever had the misfortune of trying to get through to an Astolfo cosplayer, the reason that Jax and Hato Genshiken are like that is obvious. The intended thrill for the Male Reader is in sexual subjugation via the demonstration of their own superior manhood, though some project into the ‘trap’ seeking abnegation (and of course Fujoshi enjoy reenacting out of toxic heterosexual dynamics, through the effeminacy of such ukes.)

The phallus here is a marker of abjection. It doesn’t really bring her any pleasure, or do much at all, but mark her as a transmisogynized subject to be predated upon for failing to perform masculinity. This is a kind of vulnerability, sure, but not one conducive to intimacy and relationship-building, just rough sex. Which is what some transgender women want, I suppose. This category is, I suspect, one of the main reasons newly-transitioned girls keep boying herselves — she associates sexual abjection and being desired with being the target of stronger men.

Of course in anime there are sometimes totally normal girls who just woke up one day and there was. such. But that isn’t based on anything in real life and doesn’t happen, except to about two or so percent of the population in a small portion of the southwestern Dominican Republic, where most people are not. And possibly in a few other such enclaves around the world, and for Saber one time. It’s just wish fulfillment.

So all three of these framings have obvious failures as well. While transgender women might want to make use of them for sexual reasons, the first demands she exist entirely in relation to her penis, the second is about erasing her internality for men, and the third ignores all the context of what being a woman with that is like in real life, and context is necessary for sex.

I think at least one way forward in is a distinct but related category: the girl who is ascribed a transness in fanart. To be horrifically reductive, I here draw a throughline that goes like this:

Wanting to draw girls = Romance

Romance + More girls = Harem Anime

Harem Anime - The Boy = Moeblobs5

Moeblobs + Somebody’s Special Interest = Cute Girls Doing Cute Things6

Cute Girls Doing Cute Things + We Need A Viewpoint Protagonisty Character But Not A Guy = A Girl Who Has Certain Traits That Make Her Disproportionately Likely For Fans To Read Her As Transgender.

Consider: Iroha Sakayori, Oguri Cap, Bocchi TheRock!!!, Kobayashi Dragonmaid, Jill VA11-hall-A, Homura Akemi, Nano Shinonome.

This kind of girl protagonist tends to have some kind of special interest, be isolated from her female peers, and consequently drawn to other girls and kind of neurotic about it. As a girl, her boundaries between close friendship and romance are thin. She’s also disproportionately likely to have black hair, since the Japanese understand correctly that blondes are Othered. She’s often thin, because she doesn’t take very good care of herself and flat-chestedness is relatable, and in emotional pain, because himedanshi are often in love with a girl and incapable of ever just telling her about it.

This kind of girl is not created to be sexually consumed (though wanting to create a sexually consumable anime girl is a perfectly fine reason to create one, as long as you aren’t weird or gross about it.). She is created instead for projection. Remember: fujoshi reenact dynamics via fictional men as a means of eroticizing the trauma of enforced heterosexuality and himedanshi are trying to erase and redeem themselves by projecting into girls. When this kind of girl is well-made, she has a lot in common with transgender.

Now the question is: why does this kind of girl have it? What are the fanartists picking up on?

Well, the himedanshi cares about girls’ internalities. If he didn’t, lesbian romance would hold no interest to him and he would just be looking at tasteless pornography or Gurren Lagann or Solo Leveling or whatever flavor of bland manslop is currently on the male menu. In all likelihood the himedanshi has been taught the fear of stronger men in very similar ways to the ways girls have. He understands correctly that “men who get in the way of yuri should die,” and possesses a nigh-on-pathological awareness of the implicit harm done to women by the centralization of heterosexual relationships.

And so the himedanshi, while often plagued by guilt and neuroticism, has a much more reasonable relationship to the penis than most men. A penis is, after all, a part of the body, and the body is made to feel.

This carries over into their depictions of intimacy. Of course people love to draw their faves pregnant and such, and of course this is not a mode exclusive to himedanshi (more on that later) but there’s a sizable minority of content where a girl has it and her arousal is visible and another girl touches her there and she blushes and goes very still. The himedanshi isn’t interested in establishing his masculine dominance and stroking his ego over the girl, though his self-insert character may take the lead, out of the desire to see a girl make a vulnerable face in intimacy7. It’s about girls feeling things together.

The girl can have that, and it can be touched gently, and she can be vulnerable. She can be girlish, even. She can make a feminine little noise, or even a feminine slightly-larger noise. Gender dysphoria happens when a girl is treated like a man, even by herself. But she is not a man. She can experience pleasure gently rather than forcing another body to provide it to her — and in fact a bit more easily than somebody with the other standard genital set. Her arousal and consequent emotional vulnerability are readily apparent. She doesn’t have to hate her body for the weapon that people think it is and the harm they think it could cause, because she isn’t causing any harm with it. She can give and take pleasure mutually. She can be loved.

Just because this method is characteristic of the himedanshi8 doesn’t mean that it’s somehow tainted or man-specific. The fact that men can, if they are thoughtful and respectful and intelligent, produce good art9 should not be in doubt at this point.

Look at post-himejoshi Inori (Rae Taylor, I’m In Love With The Villainess10), trying-not-to-be-a-girl11 tsukumizu (Chito/Shijima Tsukishima, Shoujo Shuumatsu Ryokou/Shimeji Simulation) and so so much of manga kirara carat! Aki Hamazi, Izumo Ito, Rasuko Okuma… Once you’ve been exposed to Hidamari Sketch it’s impossible to unsee Ume Aoki’s fingerprints all over Madoka’s cast — not just their designs. Look! Yes, that means you, transgender woman reading this who understands all these references and barely leaves her room. Look! Cis women are making this kind of protagonist too, you know! The ones who do tend to be a bit alienated from their gender but that comes with the experience of being women attracted to women in a patriarchal world!

Lesbians care about girls’ internalities. Lesbians have been taught the fear of stronger men in very similar ways to the ways straight girls have. Lesbians understand correctly that “men who get in the way of yuri should die,” and possess a nigh-on-pathological awareness of the implicit harm done to women by the centralization of heterosexual relationships. I think that lesbians are very well-positioned for this particular discursive framework — which makes sense, since many lesbians are transgender women. And also because lesbians understand that giving head is something done with agency. (Though I’m saving more discussion of this for part II.)

Which isn’t to say that himedanshi are lesbians. Though some of them turn out to be, as they were actually girls all along. Just that alienation from one’s gender and being pathologically into women create certain commonalities, which result in frameworks of tenderness and empathy which can then be applied to the bodies of transgender women.

Well, why cite that protagonist type as coming from himedanshi, then? It’s just that the alienation is easier to see in himedanshi and himedanshi-derived works because they’re less good at hiding it. Sorry guys. You don’t mask it nearly as well as you think you do.

If you liked this one, the next one will be along shortly. in like 2-3 days I think. and you can pay me dollars. not for the article though, that’ll be free. as they almost always will be.

title: Ultimate Horseoscope 2
text:
previously, in my deranged ranting about umamusume: The Tokyo Yushun Is Decadent And Depraved

* * *

as a feminist it is genuinely great that guys can dress up as uma musume at cons. when men can have female athletes as role models, not considering her worse or weaker for her gender, but just aspiring to be like her? then Woke will truly have won. @HalimedeMF

As the world becomes more free and diverse, more kinds of people are forced to grapple with the classic lesbian question1: do I want to kiss this girl or be her?

Obviously this question and the changes on constraints in the answer space over time could reveal some really interesting things about how we percieve gender and attraction. And they will, even, as being a girl becomes less stigmatized by society. But now it’s time for:

MORE THINGS YOU CAN TELL ABOUT SOMEBODY BASED ON THEIR FAVORITE UMAMUSUME (if she’s in the first 120 by internal ID number):

(if you do not have a favorite Umamusume you can just read the descriptions to discover which anime girl bearing the name, legacy, ears, and tail of a racehorse from another world will lodge herself in your heart like a splinter.)

* * *

(Some Umas have been updated. But you can start at Transcend if you want to get right to the new stuff!)

* * *

SPECIAL WEEK - You like white rice, the piano, and childhood friend romance. You had vanilla ice cream with real vanilla once and it was okay but you prefer the normal kind.

SILENCE SUZUKA - You like actual horses. You fondly remember your first love. You know big breasts are overrated, and you want to support your lover rather than have them support you. You know what the RAADS-R is.

TOKAI TEIO - You like short shorts.

MARUZENSKY - It’s that Showa era glamour, isn’t it. That or her swimsuit. You love physical sensations, especially softnesses. You like it when a lady has appetites and takes the lead.

FUJI KISEKI - You know what otokoyaku means. You had a thing for your highschool senpai, and you wanted to heal that sadness in her eyes that only you could see. You think Nanako should have gone after Kaoru instead. You admire the lack of shame with which she wears her racing silks but you can’t bring yourself to look at that diamond cutout without blushing.

OGURI CAP - You wish shounen had girl leads. You don’t like wearing skirts. You may have a connective tissue disorder and you definitely have some level of what people on the internet refer to as autism. You deserve all the food you can eat.

title: doubting thomasine
text:
I attended a (LGBT+ inclusive, of course) church service with a transgender friend recently, because she insisted that no really it was actually really nice and that she knew some people there who would love to meet me.

This is what that felt like.

* * *

Greetings! I really can’t express how wonderful it is to be here today with all of you. This is a really lovely place, you know that? Just looking around makes me feel so grateful to be here with you all. Really! I’d never been here before, and honestly? I was a little bit nervous. This place has kind of a reputation, you know? Some people out there — not all of them, but some of them — well, they’re a little bit down on this place. They say doing this, being here, isn’t worth it, if you can believe it, what with the way things can be and well, the way people are here.

They are of course entitled to their opinions of course.

But I’ve had a wonderful time so far, and I’m just going to come out and say it: I think they’re jealous. I’m starting to think that everybody who told me that just must have been exceptionally rude, if they weren’t just outright lying, because everyone here has been so kind to me. I’m starting to think that, well, they might have just visited some other place that isn’t this one. Is there another place that’s just exactly like this one in every way, with the same name and location but bad where they must have somehow gone and been? That’s how different this place is from what those people told me. That’s how different you are.

People aren’t always so nice to people like me, and I’m learning that they aren’t very nice to you either. I don’t mean to imply that we’re the same, of course; you get to spend your time here in this, can I say it again, absolutely lovely place and I don’t. But I think we could maybe be friends. I’ve been all over and, looking around, this is just about my favorite place I’ve been that isn’t where I’m from, because that’s where my heart is, although there are a lot of things that there and here have in common. You wouldn’t know it, but I do, and I think that if you went there you might feel the same way but in reverse. Home is where the heart is, isn’t that true? My home’s there for me and yours here’s there for you.

Now, I haven’t been here nearly as long as most of you. I haven’t been here for any time at all really; not enough time to see the way things get throughout the year; to see the ways everything changes and stays the same. And I freely admit that without a complete picture like the one you undoubtedly have it’s really difficult for me to do justice to the way things are here that here deserves to have. But I can tell you this: I haven’t spoken with a single person who hasn’t been ready to put down whatever they were doing and help me figure out how this place works, except for the ones who weren’t working on something more important, of course. But you can’t expect them to step away; I wouldn’t, and I didn’t, and even still they weren’t unpleasant. I hope I haven’t been a bother.

Thank you, thank you. Thank yourselves! You’ve made a wonderful beautiful joyful place for people like me and people like you, who aren’t always safe in the world out there, to focus on what’s really important in.

Now, before we get started I just want to thank our hosts for providing such a gorgeous venue. Everything looks stunning. You can really tell what’s important to you as a group just by looking, really looking, at how everything is all laid out. I love the light and the symbolism and how warm and welcoming this space feels — how it makes me feel just being lucky enough to be here today with all of you. And well, if I can be honest with you for just a moment? I’ve been around — not all over, but around enough to know what’s up in the places where I’ve been, and having been in those places I can tell you that I’ve been in places where that isn’t necessarily the case — or worse, places where it is, and where they don’t really have the right sense of what matters. Well, it might be what matters to them, but it isn’t what matters to me. Or to you, for that matter. We know what matters to us, and it isn’t necessarily what matters to other people; those other people who do know what matters are members of us, and the ones who don’t, well, we hope they see reason.

I am moved. I am moved just by being here with all of you today, all of us intent on our common purpose. I am deeply and irrevocably changed by this experience, as I hope through my efforts things beyond and above me will irrevocably change you. Everybody needs change — for some of us, that change will shake things up, which we have to be prepared to accept, and for some of us, that change will come in the form of stability, as long as we trust that that change is going to happen whether we like it or not, maintain our steady course towards what we believe we know is right, and are strong enough to let go.

Can you feel it? I’d like to invite you to close your eyes with me, and take a deep breath, and focus on what we all know is there. It can be easy to lose track of things we know because of how much goes on in the world today, but in here, in here, we aspire that this should be made to be a place of peace. We prepare ourselves for what comes next; for what has been asked of us and what we know we must do. We know that there is no reason to be afraid, because we will be provided for. As we speak we are being provided for and sustained. You can feel it now. You can know: it is safe to let down your burdens here. This is a place of safety and healing; a place where everyone, no matter who, can be welcome always. This is a place of love.

I can feel that love, and I know you can too. We want what is good and right; we want what is real and true; we want what is best for each other.

Once again, thank you for having me. Now who’s first to get their nipples cut off?

sorry. that’s what it was like though. subscribe to me for dollars even, to support a more LGBT+ inclusive experience. than that.
