title: Reasons You Think I Am Transgender
text:
You just think I am transgender because you cannot imagine being loved by somebody unlike yourself.

That you think I am trans indicates that you consider the womanhood of trans women separate — and as Simone de Beauvoir says in her seminal feminist classic The Second Sex, separation implies inequality. Just look at the post-Reconstruction American South. You think of yourself as a lesser kind of woman, if you think of yourself as a kind of woman at all, because the world is so cruel to you.

But transgender women are women; you only make sense through lenses used to understand women; to treat you otherwise is not only bigoted but produces incoherent analyses. The fact of your obsession with the question means you have not understood the truth I have so desperately been trying to convey to you for like five entire years: that you and I are of the same kind.

And no, I am not transgender. But that fact should be treated as largely incidental. I could have been, if I had been born differently, and been strong enough to become the me I would always have been becoming made to. I would be less upset by you calling me transgender if it wasn’t a way for you to convince yourself that what I am, a girl who is not transgender, could never care about you.

I would still be upset, of course. But I would be upset in the way I get upset when somebody files something incorrectly, instead of the way I get upset when you hurt yourself.

* * *

Here is the process enacted upon transgender girls that makes her think I am transgender (I am not transgender):

•

She is made to suffer by those close to her who should know better. She is made to pretend to be something she is not and never can be by the application of physical and social force. This creates in her the psychological reproduction of the bigotries leveled upon her within her own mind, so that by preemptively enacting them on herself and controlling her behavior she can retain some semblance of agency and avoid ego destruction.

•

As a direct result of this suffering she is afraid — afraid that she will fail the performance she must enact, which brings inevitable punishment, rather than fear of the punishment itself. She treats punishment for impropriety as a natural law rather than a constructed reality, as changing it is impossible for her. Her fear exists to keep her safe, but it ends up ruling her life.

•

As a direct result of this fear she isolates herself. Isolation decreases the vectors by which she can be made to experience pain, at the comparatively low cost of decreasing her ability to interact with the world. She trades the possibility of love for the surety of minimizing her pain. At this point she often becomes a Stoic.

•

As a direct result of her isolation she longs to be known. She longs not directly for acceptance, nor for the decoupling of ‘wrong’ behavior and punishment, because these things seem fundamentally impossible to her. She wants only to be seen and understood for who she is. She perceives this simple request as imposing enormous social obligation, and minimizes herself to try to make it more palatable.

•

As a direct result of her desire to be known going unfulfilled (how can it be, when she has isolated herself?) she becomes twisted with detachments and ironies. She becomes incapable of simply expressing her true feelings — and yet they cannot be repressed. They seep out in her art, in her relationships, in her dreams, and, yes, in her sexuality. She is plagued by subtext.

•

When she has become contorted into a self she believes unknowable, she comes to think that she can never be loved. How can she be loved without being known?

•

And when she thinks that she can never be loved, and encounters clear evidence otherwise, she tries to discredit it. The idea that she could be understood is just too painful. And so she insists that I could only make my gift guide, because I myself am transgender, even though I am not transgender. Q. E. D.

I do not know these things because I am transgender; I know them because I am a lesbian (the single greatest kind of perceived gender deviance in our society, bar transgender, which really should not be considered a deviance at all), and alienated women share many common experiences. Go through this list and substitute the word gay for the word trans. I also make sure to include transgender women in my life, and I have a level of empathy that should really be considered the human baseline.

* * *

“But I know somebody who knows somebody who met you in Chicago! She says you’re trans!”

Well I know somebody who knows somebody who met you in Chicago, and she says you need to be more critical of your sources. I brought four friends with me to the Chicago meetup, each of whom was instructed to act as though she were me. Two of them were transgender; two of them were not; one of them has taken testosterone until she got the results she wanted. You think you can tell but you really can’t.

* * *

You think I am transgender because you think only the experiences of being transgender can result in a woman who has empathy with you. Well, the experiences of transgenderwomen are not so different from the experiences of many women; she is the women of women, after all.

But you also think of transness as a marked category overriding your womanhood (or even, in particularly desperate cases, your manhood), which explains why you keep saying I am not real on twitter.

What is markedness? Well, Simone de Beauvoir’s seminal feminist classic The Second Sex lays out how people think about identity categories with incredible clarity, especially for the time in which it was written. You conceptualize identity categories as deviations from the socially-defined ‘norm’, rather than as innate attributes. Women are the titular Second Sex, ‘marked’ and defined against men by all the ways in which they are not the default.

For instance: the default stick figure body children draw is male; women get longer hair or a bow. You call the head of a committee the Chairman. You consider testosterone-dominant heart attack symptoms the standard, leading to worse outcomes for those with oestrogenic endocrine systems. Women are defined by the ways in which they are not-men.

As a woman — as any woman — you need to rip this internalized misogyny out of your head.

Transgender lesbians in particular struggle here because you think being transgender and being lesbian cumulatively is somehow too much deviance, like that makes you into the ‘perfect moe character with every moe trait’ joke from Welcome to the NHK instead of recognizing that you are a woman who should not be measured against the yardstick of men.

You think a non-trans woman supporting you is ‘impossible’ because you view people in terms of identity category separation and distance from a norm; if anything you think non-trans women are further away from you than men. This is because bigotry has been pounded into your skull since you were born.

But that’s a very generalized case. Let’s look at something more specific.

This obsession with measuring people against how far they deviate from a hypothetical straight cis white middle-aged christian man makes you question me. What, just because I like good anime and am a 24 year old white lesbian who does not believe in God, that makes me ‘unrealistic’? You forget that many of these things are correlated - younger people are more likely to be out and to enjoy anime; gays are less likely to believe in god (though more inclined to astrology), half the people on Earth are women, and lesbians specifically like trans much more than trans do! You’ve seen that chart! There are so many people in the world! You should at least be comparing yourself to an idealized hypothetical woman rather than a man!!!

You think that the more identities you tack onto somebody, the less realistic they get. It’s true that it gets less likely with each qualifier but when you center men in your thinking, you systematically reduce the possibilities you consider realistic for women. You create your own glass ceiling, into which you crash your own head. You also neglect correlations - a ‘bisexual transgender woman’ for instance, sounds ridiculous to you, until you remember that women and transgender women are both much more likely than the rest of the population to be bisexual. And god help you if you’re racialized on top of that.

You don’t need to create your own glass ceiling! A significant portion of the rest of the world hates you for being women already! It’s hard enough!

Consider yourself. Roll your own identity categories around in your head — you feel as though you are unrealistic. You feel as though you exist to fill some kind of diversity quota or whatever. And yet here you are. Clearly reality runs numbers better than you do.

Now consider me again.

You act like people have so many ‘identity points’ they can put into deviating from the norm, when the norm is actually a retroactively-decided template overlaid onto real life people. And you think my number of ‘identity points’ is unrealistic.

And yet in the real world you do exist. And in the real world, I also exist, as a girl who is not transgender.

As I keep having to tell you.

You can subscribe or even pay me, for my newsletter. I am not transgender.

title: Halimede's List Of Gifts For Transgender Women
text:
Principles For Good Gift Giving As Extended To Transgender

Know the recipient well.

Get her something she would never get herself — a fancy version of something cheap; a permanent version of something disposable; something a little more daring than she would allow herself normally. Experience gifts are great here, as a trans girl short on money, as transphobia so often ensures they are, may not feel like she can justify those purchases herself for mere memories.

Use your specific expertises in gifting. That doesn’t mean getting her something you want for yourself; it means leveraging your knowledge to get her something she doesn’t yet know she’ll be delighted by. You also want to keep in mind that you don’t want to talk down to her — her relationship to her femininity is often raw and sensitive, and giving her a bunch of skincare, for instance, might imply to her that you think she needs to take better care of her skin. Which maybe she does! But it may still be rude. It is the recipient’s opinion, not yours, that matters in such cases. You can get her makeup, haircare, or skincare products, but be sure that she isn’t going to feel humiliated by receiving them. Clothing and shoes may require sizing, and you want her to feel good about her body.

Get her something with a clear and appealing use case.

Do NOT get her that six hundred dollar cashmere, even if you can afford it. I know it would be so soft on her and she would look so good in it but remember: giving a gift creates a connection, and if that connection is one of obligation she will feel trapped and come to resent you. It is possible that she likes feeling trapped like this sexually — but if that’s the case and you know it, then you don’t need my gift guide. And I’m happy for you. Really. I am.

Trans women are often the type to decline gifts; with the holidays, this is your chance to make sure she has things she needs, and nice things besides, without her turning them down.

Consider also just giving her some money in addition to whatever you get her. Things are hard for trans.

Oh, and I just want to give a shout out to the New York Times for their egregious both-sidesing on trans issues, without which I would still be enjoying the Grey Lady’s company and subscriptions would be high on this list. I wish you were better and I miss Modern Love but I can’t justify subscribing again until you publish an apology and back transgender rights.

Before we get started, I want to take a second to let you know these are all non-affiliate links. Every product you buy from my recommendations earns me zero money whatsoever, because of a lack of any kind of advertisement deal on the products in question. So if I manage to convince you to get something, and you click through, I don’t benefit at all, except by knowing you got something nice for somebody who deserved it — possibly even yourself. That’s because I haven’t partnered up with anybody to bring you any kind of discount and zero percent savings when you input any kind of code or otherwise.

* * *

CATEGORIES:

•

For the trans girl who’s always cold

•

For the trans girl gamer

•

For the trans girl who prefers non-video games

•

For the trans girl who needs help with self-care

•

For the trans girl you have your eye on ;)

•

For the repentant weeaboo

•

For the unrepentant weeaboo

•

For the trans girl who loves mecha

•

For the trans girl who deserves a sword!

•

For the trans girl who makes things

•

For the trans girl who just needs to relax

•

For the transgender rationalist who needs feminism

•

For the trans girl who belongs in the kitchen, without the misogyny

•

Plushies

•

For the trans girl of truly exquisite taste

* * *

For the trans girl who’s always cold

A blood test and some iron supplements. Just because she doesn’t have periods doesn’t mean she can’t be anemic.

A soft blanket for her couch; if she already keeps one there, get her another for her desk chair. I personally don’t feel right at my home desk without one.

Pajamas are nice but there’s nothing like the full-body looseness and softness of a plush robe.

Not having periods doesn’t mean her tummy won’t hurt - get her a heating pad for pain relief and make her use it. If you don’t make her use it she will not use it because she doesn’t think her pain matters. But it does.

An electric kettle scales to any budget and is tremendously convenient. Get her a cute one.

* * *

For the trans girl gamer.

This will depend very much on the kinds of games she likes and what she’s already played.

Girls who like parrying, furries, those who found Hollow Knight too easy but loved Silksong, and/or sinophiles will enjoy Nine Sols, Red Candle Games’ blistering taoist condemnation of the CCP. Delightful narrative; excellent gamefeel.

Visual novel players may enjoy Misericorde (gay nun murder mystery), Ladykiller in a Bind (gay and stupid butch simulator), Of The Devil (ace attorney but gay the other way), and of course Umineko no Naku Koro Ni - but if she has read Umineko she will not be able to stop herself from talking about it, and if so you should get her a Beatoriche fumo. I got my own Lambda and Bern from Purupurupikopuyo.

Give the girl who’s played everything else the gift of Sylvie Games this season. Sylvie of love-game creates mind-melting boutique precision platformer microcosms with kittens that make me type like I’m on Fragrantica just trying to describe them. I cannot play these games. I have tried, repeatedly, but they are too much for me. But I have it on good authority from several expert gamer trans that these bring fresh delight to their jaded gamer lives. Sylvie.io Gaming.

Try Sylvie Lime, Clockwork Calamity in Mushroom World: What would you do if the time stopped ticking?, or Sylvie RPG: Seven Elf Apocalypse. Suggested pricing is Pay Her.

*the following words are to be read in the tone of a cigar commercial*

Inscrutable narrative; gamefeel unlike anything she’s ever felt before. Soft and fluffy kitten. Sylvie.

* * *

For the trans girl who prefers her games non-video.

You can get her some dice, of course. Dice never go amiss.

But if you want something more thoughtful, get her some card sleeves for the various board games with cards she already has, a hard copy of a ttrpg by Jenna Katerin Moran (transgender women LOVE to read Glitch), LANCER, or Beam Saber, a storage organizer for a specific game off etsy, wood components for her copy of Wingspan, or, if she wants a real challenge, Cole Wehrle’s Root - which I have found very difficult but very worth it. Very difficult. Seriously. Plan to play at least three full games before you get it, all ideally with the same people. The Marquise De Cat Shall Rule Supreme Forevermore!

* * *

For the trans girl who needs help with self-care

(And don’t we all, sometimes?)

This is the miscellaneous category.

Bath bombs. What you pay for is what you get, with these; pay the extra for a fancy set, and get her a sampler pack to smooth over individual misses.

If she has curly hair, get her a wet brush and a nice hair dryer with the spiky showerhead-looking attachment for drying curls.

They call the humble backrest pillow a “husband pillow”, for heterosexual reasons; and so I am well within my gay rights to refer to such as a Wife Pillow. They’re quite affordable — but be warned: it may be harder to get her out of bed if she’s relaxing with one of these.

A Tarot Deck. You’re never supposed to buy your first one. Pick Rider-Waite for the classic imagery, or get a little spicier with one more tuned to her personality. Obviously the Tarot is better understood as a symbolic font of possibility than a prediction of literal fate but I found two swords one time after I drew the two of swords so take it up with the person leaving swords everywhere.

d’Annam’s Vietnamese Coffee fragrance will cause her to be grasped and accosted by women. Dangerous. Get the whole Discovery Set 1 so you can be sure.

Nadaam has the best-feeling cheap cashmere. Uniqlo, unfortunately, disappoints. But they do have that viral ten dollar bag as a stocking stuffer. 25 dollars now???? Well you can probably get it on sale in store but that’s awfully rude. Maybe you should just get her a heattech fleece turtleneck in off-white or plum. Hmm… One in each.

She probably has some kind of hyperspecific hobby that she’s desperate to tell you about — so let her take you to a shop that sells relevant items and buy her something nice. Maybe it’s a synthesizer; maybe it’s a lego set; maybe it’s a specific tree-grafting branch or Japanese-made chisel or chalk bag or fighting game controller box. Enjoy her company.

Take a class of some kind with her. Pottery, cooking, skiing or surfing (keeping in mind how uncomfortable trans often are with swimwear), rock climbing, fencing, dance — what matters is that you have a nice time together and she isn’t the one paying. As long as she has sufficient fine dexterity, trans women LOVE to be taught about fiber arts.

* * *

For the trans girl you have your eye on ;)

A nice glass statement vase. She probably won’t have one around; she’ll smile and thank you and go to put it away thinking she’ll never get any use out of it, and why did you get it for her anyway — and then you bring out the flowers. Refresh as needed. Note: this will NOT work for t4t relationships, so don’t try it.

* * *

For the repentant weeaboo

Trans who like anime is often ashamed. Get her something nice, so she can feel a little less sad all the time.

Girls Last Tour by tkmiz (Manga, with a nice adaptation). Essential for the girl who likes to think about standing wistfully in the snow, or the girl who cries thinking about Homura/Elster/Yuno Hidasketch. Somebody really needs to release Shimeji Simulation in english already.

Genshiken and Genshiken Nidaime, by Kio Shimoku (Manga). Pretty cheap on ebay. God I hope Spotted Flower gets released someday. For the girl who has always wanted fandom friends, or the girl who keeps getting cuckolded.

Yokohama Kaidashi Kikkou, by Ashinano Hitoshi (Manga and OVAs) drips with that particular Japanese sentimentality. “Ah…. This scent is nostalgic,” you may find yourself saying, and mean it.

Bocchi The Rock! Blu-rays. For the girl who is slowly coming out of her shell to sit on a couch and watch with her friends who she is all not-so-secretly a little in love with. I usually dislike CGDCT but this is very sweet.

Various paraphernalia associated with her favorite anime girl. High-risk but high reward if chosen properly. A Soul Gem necklace that she can hide under a shirt, a ring she can fiddle with; Kim Kitsuragi’s bomber jacket (that man is an anime girl.) Remember: this is for the weeaboo who knows shame. Anything that anybody might actually see or understand is going to be too obvious for her.

* * *

For the unrepentant weeaboo

For the trans who likes anime who should probably be a little more ashamed.

Full Metal Daemon Muramasa - 40$ on JAST. Buy it. Now.

Where there are Demons, I slay them.

Where there are Saints, I slay them.

Mine is the Way of the Sword.

Want more than that? Fine. Ittetsu Narahara’s thesis on victimhood and the hideous nature of the sword contains: the horrors of nationalism and colonial regimes; Emiya Shirou but a girl; explanations of swordplay with diagrams, right in the middle of fight scenes; the single most brutal critique of the nuclear family I’ve ever read; a blonde very dear to my heart, and a stacked elf who knows only her duty with skimpy clothing and no sense of self-worth. You animal.

The Oguri Cap. A hit with any girl watching Cinderella Gray, which should be all of you.

If she still likes Naruto for some reason: get her into Chainsaw Man. If she won’t stop talking about how Araragi is a girl no really I promise he’s a girl no trust me, get her the Monogatari novels. If her terrible taste leans pornographic, get her the Re: Cutie Honey OVAs.

* * *

For the trans girl who loves mecha

Full Metal Daemon Muramasa - 40$ on JAST. That’s right.

All that other stuff and it also has robots.

Get her some Gunpla: it’s the more sophisticated version of adult coloring books. The snip of nippers through sprue… ah! I can’t get enough! Also, every time I go to get some in person I see at least one other non-trans girl in the hobby shop looking through them. Seriously. You don’t have to worry about this being a ‘boy thing1’.

Pick a mobile suit she likes. Here are the grades: pick RG if you want small fiddly parts and delightful engineering at about $40, MG for a bigger, higher budget model from $50-80, HG for lower cost and wider selection, typically around $20-30.

Here’re some easy picks:

•

HG Aerial

•

HG Aerial Rebuild

•

HG Schwartzette

•

HG Zaku/Char’s Zaku

•

HG GTO Char’s Zaku II

•

HG Barbatos

•

HG Freedom (revive)

•

RG RX-78 2.0

HG GTO, WFM, and Gquuuuuux lines are all great.

If you already know she likes gunpla, or just want to get her a little more, throw in some better nippers, a craft knife, some clear coat sprays, a little stand so she can pose her mobile suit in the air, Gunprimer Balancers for that gorgeous polished finish, paints for hand painting or airbrushing, an airbrush — etc etc and so on.

If she loves the Universal Century, get her Heaven Will Be Mine, a visual novel about navigating the costs of queer assimilations or the refusals thereof, with my favorite take ever on Char Aznable. This one is up there with stories like Revolutionary Girl Utena and A Series of Unfortunate Events in the defining impact it had on me.

If she loves Victory or Iron-Blooded Orphans, get her Coquette Dragoon, a visual novel about how a trans girl taking agency in her life can turn it all around and end up in a much better place.

If she is desperately horny for Armored Core VI, get her a 30MM Nachtreiher/STEEL HAZE and whatever weapon pack has a loadout she liked. I cannot endorse Warhound for ideological reasons but I also don’t want trans sex workers left out in the cold. So if she is thusly inclined, you should buy it but not read it.

If she likes workplace sitcoms or cute butches, get her into Patlabor!

Oh, and watch Mobile Suit Gundam 0080: War In The Pocket with her for Christmas. She’ll know where to source it discreetly.

* * *

For the trans girl who makes things

Pay her money for one of her things, and then a little extra. Tell her that the thing she made is good. Display your copy prominently.

She may also appreciate supplies specific to the art she practices. Ask her!

* * *

For the trans girl who deserves a sword!

Get her a shinai or practice prop sword! LARPer and sword girl With-A-Martyr-Complex (@martyrwith, on twitter) recommends polypropylene, or latex for active prop use. Real steel and/or swordplay lessons are for if you really like her and she’s willing to accept them.

She also recommends various cosplay cloaks and capes and such but I can’t in good conscience recommend you get those for a trans, as all the ones she recommended me, were for men.

* * *

For the trans girl who just needs to relax

A deep tissue massage. The poor thing really needs it. Consider making it a couple’s massage (you don’t actually have to be dating; you can go as friends) if she’s worried about her masseuse being transphobic. Be warned: this will leave her, and possibly also you, unfit to drive afterwards; you should pay for the rideshare.

Therabody’s Theragun is expensive but worth it. That weird triangular handle is actually incredible at making sure you can get it where it needs to be. No, it isn’t a sex thing.

The (formerly Hitachi) Magic Wand is a sex thing. Every woman should own one of these. Excellent alone or partnered. Also good on the back, although the heavy handle makes it a little harder to maneuver. The old-school corded version has a slightly deeper rumble but a less nice head; the Rechargable can be disconnected but will shut down periodically for overheating reasons, and has a (nasty or wonderful, depending on how you feel about this) habit of shutting down at the worst possible time. I hear there’s a Mini but cannot attest to the ability thereof.

A sex toy should look like a piece of modern art. Tenga’s make me wish I could try them. Njoy’s stainless steel commas, wand and plugs in particular, are the darlings of dozens of internet sex toy reviewers for good reason. I think Fun Factory’s Manta might be something, but it’s hard to know without the testimony of trans women who have tried it to confirm… If you do, let me know, in detail, please. If you get her a penetrative sex toy you should also get her a lube sampler, as preferences tend to be extremely individual; be aware of body safety/silicone is a bad choice with silicone toys/etc.

* * *

For the transgender rationalist who needs feminism. And also you.

Rosemary Kirstein’s Steerswoman series is incredible, and I can’t even tell you why. Acquire a paperback, not the 80’s one. 11.99 on Amazon; probably a little more expensive at your local bookstore. You want this one for her, and to buy it for yourself, and to have an extra copy to lend out. Trust me. And then you will want the sequels.

My one single tiny qualm is that I’m not sure Rosemary Kirstein realizes that Rowan and Bel are gay. But they are gay. To me.

* * *

For the trans girl who belongs in the kitchen, without the misogyny that phrase typically implies

I can hear the straight girls sighing in sadness already.

I buy myself half a gallon of good olive oil whenever I run out. Maybe you also want to get her a container that will be easier to serve it out of than that enormous glass jug. Personally I just have had to get very good at not spilling it all over the counter.

She won’t bother buying herself a cute apron; she will pick something utilitarian. So! Do it for her; put it on for her; tighten it just so at her waist from behind. Enjoy the resulting noise.

Get her a set of culinary tweezers if she isn’t adept with chopsticks and several sets of cooking-length chopsticks if she is. She probably needs an end-grain cutting board; if she has one, she probably needs another.

Go to an H-Mart with her, load up a full cart with snacks and ingredients and some of the home goods they always have there for some reason, and pay for it all.

If you give her a molcajete so she can grind her own spices you will profit enormously; once you’ve had them freshly-ground, you’ll never want to go back.

Yes ok Wirecutter every girl wants more Maldon finishing salt. Yes, I know. You keep saying so. It’s true though.

* * *

The Plushie Section

Public transit vehicles, a Fumo of a beloved character, her favorite mammal, reptile, amphibian, insect, Pokemon, fish, bird, mythical creature, etc (C elegans!), her favorite food, the Epstein-Barr virus and other pathogens, BMO. They make stuffed versions of basically anything you can think of.

* * *

For the trans girl of truly exquisite taste

Gift her a paid subscription to my Substack, which you are now reading, and the satisfaction of supporting a writer she loves. Just click this very link to get started.

You can also subscribe to me normally. In fact, you probably already have. but you could also pay me, which, statistically you most likely have not. If you have, wow! Thanks!

... And some Gunpla and cheap nippers or a copy of The Steerswoman. Seriously. Those are really good gifts and I for one would feel much happier if she had them.

And also give her some money. It’s rough out there for trans right now.

Be safe, all of you.

title: Defamiliarizing Trans Women
text:
The poet recontextualizes; she makes the strange familiar and the familar strange. In between annual poetic phases I am not a poet and do not care to be but I think ostranenie1 is a concept ripe for cultural application, particularly regarding the destigmatization of ideas considered inflammatory.

* * *

I’ve been thinking a lot about trans women lately. More than usual, I mean. Here’s a thought experiment I keep coming back to.

Let us define a woman Alice such that she is definitionally not transgender.

Let us say that Alice’s parents would have preferred to have a son. We don’t even have to go fully bacha posh/Qiyan Agula/Naomi Wu with it, although that precedent certainly exists. It will be sufficient that she be despised for not being something that she is not capable of being.

Let us say her gender presentation is policed. This should go without saying, as she is a woman. But let us say the environment in which she is raised devalues femininity in her, rather than enforcing it upon her and devaluing her directly. This is unusual but not unheard of; perhaps she has several brothers and a mother who hates women. As a young child she is content to play in the woods, before her hair is cut and she is given an ultimatum: acquire expertise and demonstrate worth, or be worthless.

Let us say furthermore that she is comparatively tall, flat of chest, and masculine of face. Not in a way that is unusual — but without makeup, not one she can control.

Let us say that she has the cluster of psychological and physiological traits that would previously have been classified under Asperger’s Syndrome: certain interpersonal difficulties, an affinity for categories and systems, specific reactions to sensation.

Let us say she is taught to regard her desires as evil. If she is attracted to women, she will be taught that they are completely unlike her in every way, and that if she ever changes this she will lose every social connection she has. If she is attracted to men, she will be taught they want her to be feminine, but not too feminine — an impossible line to walk for any, but doubly so for one who hasn’t been taught how to present herself. If she is attracted to nobody at all, then she will be considered defective.

Let us say that she is taught to hate her body, and that those who desire her are deviant; that straight men want her in upsetting and off-putting ways; that straight women consider her an object of pity at best and an active threat at worst. She has probably at some point had an eating disorder, as a means of punishing her body for not being what she is told it should be. She might still have it, but put it out of her mind for more pressing concerns.

Let us say, most critically, that Alice is alienated by one or all of those factors that alienate women from womanhood. I would choose lesbianism because that is what I am most qualified to discuss — but often the mere condition of womanhood suffices.

Given these premises, here are some expected results:

Alice is weird around and about other women. She is nakedly, painfully, jealous. If she doesn’t know it, she can’t help but express it constantly; if she does, she withdraws compulsively, afraid to drive other women away. Nobody has ever told her that her feelings of inferiority are unwarranted, and if they did, she would not listen to them.

Alice swings back and forth between insisting gender doesn’t matter, as though by disavowal she can wipe away her pain, and that gender matters tremendously. This leaves people around her confused and wishing to avoid the subject, which Alice mistakes for hostility.

Repressed desires often assert themselves through sexuality. Alice’s sexuality is warped — In the same way having a crush for years twists a person’s ability to interact with the target, Alice needs something badly and has no idea how to get it. She has probably had to hide her breasts; that would give anybody a complex.

Alice is not particularly good at feminine presentation. Why would she be? Nobody taught her. She may throw herself singlemindedly forward, choose non-standard feminine presentations offset by time or subculture, or hide in her room on her computer all day.

Alice has complexes around youth and girlhood. She imagines, and rightly so, that what was done to her was completely unnecessary.

Alice does not get along with her parents.

Now: is Alice transgender? No, definitionally, even if she experiences the results of transmisogyny because people think she is. But does she deserve any less compassion than a transgender woman?

Or rather: does a transgender woman deserve any less compassion than Alice?

* * *

“But this could never happen!”

It is conceivable to you that any one of those factors could affect a normal girl, isn’t it? In fact, for a girl to experience zero alienation at all would be stranger than that. Some girls are tall; some girls are emotionally unavailable; all girls have felt the pressure of the girl ideal.

Alice is stuck in an objectively ridiculous situation. But so are transgender women. In fact, the ridiculousness of their situations is equal. What she has in her pants doesn’t matter except when it matters a lot. Well, one has to take pills or inject herself every week, and one has periods. But what difference is that compared to everything they have in common, because I have specifically conceptualized Alice in such a way?

Half of all humanity is women! I say unto you: Women are half the world! Some women love gardening. Some women love rock climbing. Some women love driving. Women love smoking and fiber arts and doing laundry and getting tattoos and getting them removed and you get the picture!

You are hated, yes, but not universally so. You know that there are women out there who aren’t trans who empathize with facets of your experience, right? Marginalization doesn’t always work in the same ways, but commonalities always exist. Transgender women are women — the women of women, even — and women have women’s problems.

Besides, lesbianism and the cluster of expressions we consider autism are comorbid. For that matter, lesbians often end up severely alienated from womanhood. Many of the problems transgender women think of as uniquely transgender are lesbian problems too, if less extreme:

Self-hatred, internalized from years of bigotry (ever hear about comphet?)

Alienation from womanhood, especially since our culture defines womanhood so strongly around men

Discrimination, especially against women deemed to be inappropriately masculine

Body issues

Extremely intense relationships moving way too fast

Community infighting

Evil sex

Fetishization2

Not being able to directly have children in the way you want

* * *

What does this thought experiment about Alice tell us about actual women?

It would be ridiculous to raise a girl as a boy. A girl should be allowed a boy’s freedoms, but a girl should not be expected to socialize only with those unlike herself.

Transgender women have women’s experiences. Not all of them, and not at the same degrees, but analogies can almost always be found. 3

Making sure isolated women have social access to other women is important.

If you keep telling people gender doesn’t matter and expect them to gender you correctly you are not going to get anywhere. Instead you should simply believe in gender essentialism in a non-sexist way.

People really hate transgender women, but they hate you because they don’t understand you. If you did any of this — the haircuts, the locker rooms, the separation from her peers — to a non-transgender woman, people would be rightly appalled.

I could be in your inbox right now. You could even give me money for that.

(I have the most basic of plot outlines for my mecha novella. What I need to do now is solidify the characters and figure out how an important side detail works, and then I can start writing.)

title: The Gay Screwtape Letters
text:
My dear Marah,

Consider yourself lucky, rather. A little ambition will serve you well, and I have no doubt that so decorated a student as yourself will find ways to apply your talents regardless. Your first real assignment is simply another test. Lazy Trammelslape got the case you wanted, teetering right on the brink between Our Father and The Enemy — has she the deftness to guide him to his eternal home most warm and welcoming? Surely not. The compatibility of demon and patient is of the utmost importance. Conversely, if you had not demonstrated such promise, you would not have been given a dish so easily served.

There is always more work to be done than you think. As your superior, I will give you a little advice: know who sits below you in the Lowerarchy and what he wants. Fortunately for us both, you already know me and I will tell you what I want for free, with no politicking or faffery, out of full self-interest - which both you and I know is the only thing which anybody can ever really trust.

Your patient is of a sort which is almost assuredly headed our way. The question is not of whither but how; and my personal favorite preparation in such cases requires her to assume the form of a man.

My name is Gay Screwtape, after all. I have an especial appetite for men.

You might, as many have, question whether this makes me in some way inferior, as sexuality is an invention of The Enemy, a transcendental relation designed to promote such revolting fabrications as ‘affection’ and ‘love’. In answer I assert that my predilections have resulted in nothing of the sort, and if that is not enough for you I direct you to The Enemy Himself, who has made it very clear that he considers such behaviors detestable.

In fact the particular perversion to which I set you now could hardly have been conceived of by a disinterested outsider, and when properly performed guarantees an anguish of quality nonpareil.

Your patient has been told all her life that she is male. It is your job now to promote this deception. Yes, I know — her essence is genuinely and immutably female — and therein lies the genius of the approach. Unless this particular inconsistency is fixed, nothing she ever does will create a permanent satisfaction in her. She may turn any way she wishes to no avail. She may seem to act selflessly, but her longing will transmute whatever heroic actions she takes into self-abnegation, which is really just another kind of selfishness; she may commit herself entirely to herself, and in doing so neglect the unkindnesses other humans so carelessly heap upon her until her noble soul refuses to bear the pain and she loses her composure. This will only drive her further towards us. You see, the Enemy is here the other part of our inescapable vise.

She may run to the Church. Let her. However much she prays, the Enemy will not take her in; perhaps a churchgoer or two will take pity on her, but this pity is precisely the factor which assures her damnation. It induces in her the thought that she really might have a chance — that she might be saved — if only she denies herself, a thing which really is impossible.

One almost feels pity for the poor creature.

You may wish to torment her with the promise of Galatians 3:28: that with the Enemy there is no gender. This is the one life-line by which she might make her escape - that she renounce herself entirely, completely, and permanently, for the rest of her life. And even in such cases, the chances that the Enemy accepts her soul are close to nothing, for she has to really mean it, and that is just about impossible to do for even a second, no matter how she tells herself she must. The more she dwells upon this verse, the more difficult it becomes for her to commend herself to the Enemy, for the truth of the matter — that the Enemy cares nothing for her very self, for the truth of who she is — becomes increasingly apparent.

Neither do we, of course, except insofar as it causes her pain. But the Enemy, for all his myriad irritating strengths, has never been able to lie convincingly.

When one takes all their suffering into account, such women are actually tremendously resilient; any other placed in their positions would send themselves right down to us immediately. But that is all the more time for an artisan such as you hope to be to have your effect upon her.

If she is attracted to women, tell her no other woman would ever feel such sinful urges. Fearful and isolated, she will never learn otherwise. If she is attracted to men, treat her like any other such woman: convince her that the perfect man would solve all her problems, or else that a miserable specimen is all she deserves, and savor the loneliness which soon springs to consume her. If both, make use of both strategies in turn. Soon enough she will become convinced of the impossibility of finding love as her true self. Soon enough she will begin to present herself as a man, finding even the falsest of connections preferable to a life spent alone. Once she has begun to experiment with sexual abnegation with the male pronouns, she is as good as yours. While her essence will always be that of a female, her expression can certainly be controlled — and it is precisely this expression which I, as a lover of those who appear to be men, find most gratifying. The vintage produced thereof promises to be most exquisite. Carry out the work properly and you will be rewarded.

And what of you, Marah? What uniquenesses have you? How do you intend to turn your peccadilloes — for surely you must have some — to the refinement of your patients? I await your reply most hungrily,

Your affectionate uncle

GAY SCREWTAPE

P. S. I will write more on the subject another time, but the time of a most promising appointment with Bisexual Screwtape approaches. For gay sex, of course. Or I suppose bisexual, from his point of view.

* * *

“I had, moreover, a sort of grudge against my book for not being a different book which no one could write. Ideally, Screwtape‘s advice to Wormwood should have been balanced by archangelical advice to the patient‘s guardian angel. Without this the picture of human life is lopsided. But who could supply the deficiency? Even if a man—and he would have to be a far better man than I—could scale the spiritual heights required, what answerable style could he use? For the style would really be part of the content. Mere advice would be no good; every sentence would have to smell of Heaven.” - C. S. Lewis.

Well Mister Lewis, consider your problem solved.

Get my emails. Perhaps even give me dollars.

title: 39 Books From A Vampire's Library
text:
I have been sick in bed for three days. A friend who plays tabletop roleplaying games mentioned that they were going to stick their players in a vampire’s library and I decided that what I needed to do was write up a bunch of books for them to look over, because I have been sick in bed for three days and making lists of things makes me feel better.

Game Masters may wish to provide players with three or four words from several descriptions to whet their appetites and let them each pick one, or simply roll a 39-sided die and see what you get off the shelves. Tweak according to your setting, of course, but do tell people “oh yeah I got this from Halimede.”

In the grand tradition of Kinoko Nasu’s list of 27+1 Stupid Vampire Guys, here you go.

(oh, right - if you are playing in a tabletop campaign where you enter a vampire’s library soon, don’t read this.)

* * *

1. Human anatomy textbooks with an emphasis on the circulatory system, so a vampire knows where to bite.

2. Sociology and animal husbandry books, so a vampire knows how to keep people.

3. A conventional overwrought human-vampire romance novel. Well-loved.

4. An extremely well-thought out scholarly monograph on that romance novel and how narratives can be leveraged to suck more blood.

5. A wine guide but for human bloodlines, with an emphasis on how human diet through generations (supposedly) affects taste. Pretentious and racist; the racism should be several centuries out of date and obviously incredibly stupid.

6. A set of guides to hunting vampires. It’s important to know what vampire hunters are working with. Provides a bonus to attacks against vampires that exploit their weaknesses. Be aware that the vampire who owns this book has likely made preparations against the use of the techniques within.

7. A Secret Vampire History, containing a list of famous historical figures claimed by the author to be vampires. Riddled with logical inconsistencies but may provide surprising truths at Game Master’s discretion.

8. Vampires, being long-lived, tend to enjoy very long fiction, and often read newspaper serials or elvish epics for this reason. This particular work, “Complacency of the Learned”, depicts the fall of a circle of sages at the hands of their twelve or possibly thirteen apprentices. May provide a social bonus with certain readers - or level penalties if they don’t like the series.

9. A set of research papers on harvesting blood from other beings. Contains judgements on taste, power, and feasibility. Ultimately concludes sheep or some setting-specific species would probably be more efficient in terms of pure resource expenditure but would make it much harder to maintain social control via fear. Also what kind of self-respecting vampire drinks from a sheep! Provide bonuses to provisioning vampires in an emergency, at the cost of their morale, as well as the knowledge that a specific rare small animal is actually quite delicious to vampires, and giving them one may earn their favor.

10. Notes from a girl attending a school on a remote island where young people are brought up as high-quality blood companions for vampires. Full of quasi-religious fervor. The protagonist seeks to live as long as possible so that she can give blood in service for years. She is gay, which is fine; vampire bloodbag school is not homophobic. Uncomfortable to read; if it isn’t, that may be a bad sign.

11. A book intended for a vampire’s attendants on the artful use of sucked-dry bodies - preparation of human-skin leather, manufacture of skull goblets, etc. Cheerful and craftsy in tone. The book itself is made of supple human-skin leather, so you know the maker did quality work. Gives a bonus to making crafts from human body parts, and may be sold to particularly unscrupulous craftspeople for a decent sum.

12. Thomas Nagel’s What Is It Like To Be A Bat, marked over with corrections in red. Having actually turned into a bat, the presumably-vampiric vandal thinks this philosophy paper is stupid.

13. A long book on selecting a human to turn as an immortal companion - a choice effectively equivalent in significance to marriage. Actually has pretty good advice about navigating uneven power dynamics from both ends.

14. A lurid tale about a human full of unbelievable amounts of blood getting drunk from by three vampires at once in a giant tiered crystalline pool-fountain of blood. Excessive. Of considerable interest to certain types, and can be sold to them for a corresponding considerable sum.

15. A tome on the crystallization of blood into a handheld weapon in times of necessity. Gain the ability to arm yourself at any time at the cost of health.

16. A guide to sun-proofing a home while still ensuring adequate ventilation, headed by a tale of a victim getting disgusted by the smell of an ill-ventilated lair.

17. A vampire’s travel guide to the secret city of vampires under the sea.

18. Thicker Than Water: A Vampiric Perspective on Rulership. A history of cruel and kind rulers who were not vampires, and lessons that vampires can learn from them and their methods of control over their populaces.

19. A folio about an aristocratic vampire sport played fully blind using echolocation, containing variant rules for human play. Watching humans blunder around in the dark was a great pastime of the author.

20. A book supposedly by a priest who has been turned into a vampire - a farce meant to be read aloud to a group of other vampires and chuckled at.

21. A book actually by a priest who was turned into a vampire. He just kind of kept doing his job for his god until he died eventually when he tripped over and fell on some badly-positioned green wood. Very dry.

22. A book on False Claimants: those other species of blood drinkers mistaken for vampires by idiot humans: Lilitu, Sasabonsam, Empousai, Morana, Mananangal, etc. Clearly written by a vampire supremacist, but does provide bonuses to recognizing the work of non-vampire blood drinkers.

23. If Water Were Blood: a picture-board book for vampire tots.

24. A werewolf-hunter’s book on hunting werewolves. Useful to have around, just in case one of a vampire’s humans happens to be a werewolf.

25. Dressing One’s Thralls - vampire court fashion to be put on non-vampires, with emphasis on exposure of and access to the neck. May open up dialogue options.

26. Spilt Milk - A text containing a cantrip for drawing a liquid up off the ground and into a bottle, purifying it in the process. Useful for ridiculous shenanigans with potions, and of course for the clumsy.

27. A pamphlet on fang care, with an emphasis on hiding a broken fang. The vampire who owns this may have that vulnerability.

28. A book on throwing masquerade balls and party etiquette, with example outfits, recipes, and themes. At any masquerade ball, call out a guest of low to moderate social rank as having copied their outfit from this book to see them laughed out of the party.

29. Cursed Architectures Volume XI: Labyrinths. Makes you more likely to find maker’s marks in labyrinths and mazes, secret passages, and ways out.

30. Becoming a vampire typically (though not always) makes a vampire pansexual as well. This book talks a lot about internalized homophobia as a purely human construct, no longer relevant to vampires, and recommends decadent orgies and enjoying the blood of humans of a vampire’s gender as a means of becoming more comfortable with oneself.

31. A book on identifying magical creatures that seem human but are not. Curiously, does not mention werewolves. Useful for a vampire to have for screening, and often freely distributed to subject populations - both humans and vampires would prefer that humans not be replaced.

32. A slim black tome without a visible title on the spine about a castle run by a tyrannical human with hordes of enslaved vampires at their whim, begging and humiliating themselves for a drop of the human’s blood. Exceedingly taboo. You could probably blackmail the owner with it.

33. A book that when opened emits a loud scream, alerting anybody nearby. Closing the book stops the scream. Vampires find this scream soothing.

34. A book on Fae contract law, with a little ritual for calling a Faerie lawyer. Their advice will be quite useful, but come at a price. Why did a vampire own this? There must be some kind of legal weakness you can exploit in their claim to something…

35. A guide to hunting vampire hunters, as written by a vampire. Killing an individual vampire hunter is usually pretty easy; the real problems start when they get into your villages and start turning your populace against you. Presented solutions include: instilling xenophobia, making your people love you, setting up a cult, setting yourself up as the only thing keeping something worse from getting them, executing in public vampire hunters who try this in particularly gruesome fashions.

36. Bloodlines - an exhaustive catalog of noble vampires, the humans they have turned, and the moon phase in which that turning occurred. The author believed that phase at time of turning had effects on the potency of the vampire created, although the data doesn’t seem to have borne that out. Of use to non-vampiric genealogical scholarship, since it confirms several marriages that have otherwise been difficult to verify; may confirm a lack of royal blood in a king or something similar if you want a plot hook.

37. A text positing that the entire Moon itself is the First Vampire, and when he awakens from his slumber, he will suck dry the very Earth. This is presented as a problem, since Vampires also live there.

38. A book in an unknown language - on closer inspection, revealed to be a cipher. Decryption reveals that it is the diary of somebody the library owner loved and lost long ago. May contain weaknesses, information about routines, or just plain embarrassing secrets.

39. Many magical realms become much easier to explore if one is an undead of any kind. This tome offers overviews of a few - the twilit Blackest Markets; the Benthos, deepest sea beneath the world; various Wyrmbarrows; Ossuary Fifty-Nine and the Helicarnassian Catacomb Complex; and Hell - and rituals for calling various representatives should one wish to embark on an evil vacation. Gold, blood, favors, and innocent children are commonly accepted currencies in such places.

Wouldn’t you like more messages in your inbox? Wouldn’t you like to give me dollars for putting more messages in your inbox?

(still concepting for halimechsploitation - but what I have is very promising!)

title: trans exclusionary radical fanatics
text:
It’s hard enough being a woman already. And I’m very lucky; I’m not poor or black or anything that would make it even harder for me and it’s still so hard, you know? You get paid less, you get looked down on; nobody respects you. It’s not very politically correct to say so but you bleed every month and suffer through childbirth and then when it’s finally over you get hot flashes, which at least you can get hormones to help with.

And if the humiliations of having to experience my body weren’t enough, men are awful. Most of the awful things about being a woman are the fault of men. It’s men who don’t respect us; men who denigrate us as sexual objects; men who force us to make more of them. Patriarchy as a system is designed to systematically benefit men by crushing women. But I don’t mean to belabor the point. We all know this. What I’m here to do is suggest a solution: to fix now and for all time the problems of women being controlled by men.

We just have to kill all the men who are insufficiently masculine.

Not immediately, of course. We should really be making their lives as miserable as possible, so that they do it themselves. But yes, what we as feminists should be devoting ourselves to, in order that our daughters should be free of the shackles that bind us, is the complete and utter ruination of males who fail to live up to their gendered standards.

See, patriarchy elevates men at women’s expense. Men rule over women. They use our money and time and labor and bodies; they demand we spend our lives at their beck and call; they isolate us from our families; they turn us against each other. But no more. What we are going to do is make every effort to ruin the lives of weird men in skirts who mostly date each other, and not us. When we make sure every man is a real man, strong and decisive, nobody will ever consider us lesser ever again.

Emancipation from men can only come when gender roles are broken. And the best way to break gender roles is to find those men and boys who do not conform to them - who are desperate for other ways to live their lives, and shame them for it. If they don’t kill themselves, we will.

I dream of female liberation - of a world where any boy who is too soft, gentle, and kind - who tries on his mother’s makeup or his sisters’ dresses - is beaten within an inch of his life by his own family until he internalizes the fact of his own masculinity and joins the patriarchy, the very force which I seek to destroy. I dream of a world where women can be anything - and where every woman voluntarily submits to genital inspections in every bathroom to prove that she isn’t a crossdressing man, which is the single kind of person I hate most in all the world.

I know it’s impractical. Maybe we could just have women do it once and get an ID card that they carry around with them all the time or something?

What if a man put on a dress and walked into a wombyns bathroom and raped somebody?

No, I don’t know why he’d bother doing that when he could just walk in and rape somebody without the dress. Probably it’s some kind of sick sexual fetish. Rapists are notoriously likely to have those. Nobody with a normal socially-accepted sexuality ever rapes anybody. Especially not a man.

Look, you agree with me that “trans” are weird men, right? And that they’re often unpleasant to be around, and bad at regulating their own boundaries and emotions, and suspicious and paranoid that people are going to hunt them down and kill them, right?

Right. And so you see that by killing the men least tied into the system we will be striking a blow against patriarchy and saving all women, right? We’re hitting at the very core of the masculine male power system, which is built around the ideals of masculinity being forcibly applied to men, by getting rid of effeminate males.

Well, I suppose it is true that asking a man how he feels about trans issues can be a useful way to check if he’s at least smart enough to hide if he’s going to hit you. But have you considered that that’s hardly enough reason to not destroy the lives of people we consider to be men who display even the slightest measure of gender deviance?

It’s for feminism, you see.

I don’t know what you don’t understand. It’s simple: the patriarchy is made of masculine men, and the best way to dismantle it is to get rid of all the men who aren’t masculine.

Then, when the patriarchy has been dismantled, by our destruction of those men who are least culpable of it, we women will finally be free to do what we please.

Which is to go after the masculine women next, of course.

* * *

look, transgender women. I know that you are justifiably scared and upset but you cannot take these people seriously, okay? they are entirely too stupid.

put me in your inbox. or give me money even.

title: Notes on the hypothetical staging of an amateur production of We Know The Devil:
text:
Minimalism is your friend here. Use cheap folding chairs and almost nothing else.

Narration, of course, is to be spoken aloud by all three or the two together whom it concerns; this is obvious from context in the original work.

The spotlight should shine on the two together. The one apart should take character-appropriate actions, silently. During Jupiter and Neptune’s time playing seven minutes in heaven, they should stand facing away from the audience holding hands and recite their dialog in quiet voices. Venus should be curled up in a ball, hands over ears and eyes. Or perhaps staring.

Jupiter’s devil aspect is to be represented by extras in all black with long red gloves, possibly behind her.

Venus’ devil aspect is to be represented by an intensification and change in color of the spotlight.

Neptune’s devil aspect is to be represented by a bucket of black paint or something like it which she pours over herself.

While the voice of God should be primarily male, a few women’s voices would really make it sting for Venus. Consider a preppy newscaster woman for the end bit. Consider just having like ten people walk up on stage to say god stuff at them, or pre-seed the audience.

The voice of the Devil could be the voices of the three girls. Or not. A still small voice either way.

Group South should wear masks of their faces. The central guy should wear a second one around his midsection over his tank top. They should do stupid poses with each line repeated 3x.

The bonfire captain should likewise wear a mask of his face. He should be played by somebody who is not a man behind that mask. This emphasizes the role-nature of his job but also: Let the rest of us get to do the swaggering body language! He should slap his guitar and spread his legs wide and just generally act like such a jerk. His voice should be so obnoxious.

You could do very fun stuff with a fly system - if you did, you would want to make no attempt to hide the cables. Let them be visible. Let the hand of God be seen, as a testament unto his power.

A transgender girl should ideally play Venus. This may be difficult because acting like Venus may cause many transgender girls pain. If somebody who is not a transgender girl plays Venus, a trans girl should play Neptune or Jupiter or both even.

A radio is a conduit for God. The effect can be conveyed by having the two who are together advance on the one who is apart brandishing bibles. Maybe those bibles have pointy bits on them I don’t know. Maybe the pointy bits are just wrapped in bible pages, or carved with scripture - but the shorthand of pages will be easier for audiences to identify. Perhaps Venus loads fresh pages at some point, like the radios/bibles are the Seventh Holy Scripture. Perhaps bibles are understood to all have technological components. Perhaps these three should just hold bibles up to their ears when they call somebody, if they do.

I think the Harry Potter conversation having the overtones it now does is a really great marker of just how pervasive transphobia is. But as alternatives I would love to see a discussion of ‘wow it’s uh, it’s weird that she keeps obsessing over them. I mean it’s fine that people do that. like adults I mean. adults get to make some decisions once they grow up. it’s a free country right? some people can do things even if they’re weird or uncomfortable. if they’re adults’ or a discussion of Ouran High School Host Club or Higurashi or Death Note or Madoka. or Neon Genesis Evangelion. Teens are always talking about Evangelion.

Okay now this article is about how I think they would react to Evangelion. Jupiter didn’t finish the series but empathized with Shinji at least a little bit and felt weird about that. Neptune brings up Kaworu and has complicated feelings about Asuka and Rei. Venus has complicated feelings about Rei and Asuka and does not want to talk about it, and probably says something like “I would stay in the LCL actually. That sounds nice. Just for a bit.”

title: Why Does She Do That?
text:
•

It doesn’t matter how far in advance I booked our anniversary reservation - she just doesn’t want to leave the house. But whenever I try to get her to see a therapist, she leaves immediately. Sometimes it takes her days to come back.

•

She’s so good with kids - better than me, even. Playing with my cousins is the only time I’ve ever seen her smile with her whole face. But when I mention even the possibility of marriage and having our own, in five or ten years, her eyes go cold and dim.

•

She refuses to wear anything even remotely masculine, but she won’t stop calling herself a boy for some reason.

These behaviors, as a woman who loves, or is, a transgender woman, may sound regrettably familiar. You may not know why she performs them, even if you are the she who does. I intend here to demystify the reasons she behaves in the seemingly contradictory ways she does, and hopefully provide some direction as to resolving the symptoms of her mental illnesses.

Here’s the most important insight to keep in mind, which all the others build off: transgender women, even (especially!) those who pretend otherwise, are subject to tremendous and omnipresent social pressures. To deny the effects of these pressures is willful ignorance.

So how does a transgender woman survive under pressure? She may choose to redirect her pain outwards, towards its source or otherwise, or she may choose to internalize that pain, which causes her to self-harm or seek escape. I have arranged these four approaches, and their corresponding coping mechanisms, as follows:

•

Outwards: toward sources - Dealing With The Problem

•

Outwards: toward others - Lashing Out

•

Inwards: at the self - Self-Harming

•

Inwards: beyond the self - Escapisms

Naturally, as with any taxonomy, overlap exists; this is intended only as a template for beginning to decipher trans behaviors. A given coping mechanism may stem from one of several approaches - a girl may leave her partner as a means of lashing out at her, as a way of hurting herself, or because she feels like she isn’t worth her time, no matter how many times she tells her otherwise, and proves it to her in every way she can think of. The seemingly contradictory impulses of my first three examples are the result of distinct coping mechanisms being invoked at different times.

* * *

I. Reactions Towards Pressurers - Dealing With The Problem.

•

My family loves [Name Withheld] and she loves them back. But no matter how many times I reassure her that I would love to give her parents a piece of my mind for what they did to her, and that I would support her no matter what they told me, she refuses to let me meet them.

•

I’m scared. I don’t want to go outside because outside is full of people who hate me and want me dead. This whole sick country is trying to kill me.

•

I want to marry the love of my life but she refuses to set foot in a church, no matter how liberal.

Have you considered:

•

She doesn’t want you to meet her parents because she wants to keep you safe from them? On some level she is still that abused little girl, and she likely feels that the people who did that to her could hurt you too.

•

Finding a few friends, trans or otherwise, to go on errands with, will help you feel a lot safer? There are so many people out there willing to leverage their privileges to keep you safe.

•

You really don’t want a church wedding anyway? Why lend legitimacy to a set of institutions that either hate gay people or have been cowed into pretending acceptance to get you into the pews?

Transgender women are typically quite intelligent, even if they often refuse to admit it. They have to be, to come to the realizations necessary for transition and to survive. Expect them to have identified the causes of their problems correctly, and to bear justified resentments. Remember, it is very difficult for people who aren’t trans women to understand the enormity of transmisogyny. When the courts, press, and churches are bent on her destruction, much of what may seem to be paranoia is a reasonable response, meant to keep herself safe.

Skepticism of institutions, a disgust with parents or religions, and generalized misanthropy also fall into this category. Concentrate on shoring up her other relationships and connections rather than trying to convince her to repair failed ones. Misandry is also a possible result, although I can’t bring myself to care much - that said, if she still views herself as a boy, misandry is best addressed as a result of category III, self-harming behaviors.

It is unfortunately very difficult to enact the kind of wide-scale societal change necessary to save trans from transmisogyny. But you can try, or you can resign yourself to the cruelty of the world.

II. Lashing Out At Others

•

I feel like almost everybody is an idiot. I find myself getting passive-aggressive with people before I’ve gotten to know them; they probably don’t deserve it, but if you claim to like fantasy and haven’t read The Lord Of The Rings, what are you even doing?

•

I have a friend who gets really into competition. She doesn’t take losing badly, she’s just really ruthless. Like the kind of person who plays games to sabotage others, not because that’s the best way to win, but because she likes doing it.

•

There’s a trans girl I know - not a friend exactly, but I don’t want her to have no social contacts - whose twitter profile I found when she left her phone on the couch. The whole thing was her calling other trans women fake words that she made up that I could only assume from context were slurs. What do I do about this?

Have you considered:

•

Obviously anybody who identifies as a fan of a genre without first familiarizing themself with the canon thereof isn’t serious, so you shouldn’t treat these people like they are? They’re just in it to make friends and have fun, and they probably don’t recognize how passive-aggressive you feel like you’re being anyway. Have high standards online and girls will recognize this and come to you.

•

If your friend takes it out of the match or ring or game, that’s a huge problem. But if she keeps things safely within boundaries, that’s definitionally not a problem at all. Women - trans women included - are often told we should be cooperative rather than competitive, and that’s true in many ways, but friendly competition is actually just another higher-order kind of cooperation.

•

If she says those things to other girls, imagine the things she says to herself, in her mind? Most of those are words she’s probably convinced are incredibly powerful even though nobody else knows what they mean. Only she is capable of understanding how exactly she is ripping through her own psyche.

Since wide-scale societal change of the type necessary to eliminate transmisogyny entirely is (again) extremely difficult to enact, trans women, like every other kind of person, often vent their pain in less deserving directions. Pain trickles down to those at the bottom of society, where it pools and stagnates; trans women who manage to find community often get trapped in ‘crab buckets’, canceling each other online and in real life. When resources are limited and escape feels impossible, dragging others down is the inevitable result.

In such cases, providing resources and separating the parties involved can help clear out the bottleneck, though full recovery of course would require removing transphobia entirely. Mitigating unhealthy competition goes a long way towards keeping trans from attacking each other, though in such cases you should be prepared to take at least a few barbed words yourself. Trans women, like all women, often need to test boundaries to feel sure they’re totally safe and won’t be punished for transgressions.

If you, trans or otherwise, find yourself taking care of a trans woman, be prepared for her to be very uncomfortable with you. This is because she has been taught that as a ‘boy’ she should take care of herself and not inconvenience anybody or feel or enjoy anything. Be a little vulnerable - let her make you dinner or play with your hair, so she doesn’t feel like the relationship is too unequal and she might be pressured into giving you her body.

III. Self-Destructive Behaviors

•

A close friend of mine keeps complaining about how she doesn’t even like how drugs make her feel. When I tell her that she could maybe stop using them, she calls me a hypocrite.

•

My sister is trans, and she keeps comparing herself to me. I don’t know what to do about her being so jealous. It’s not like my life is great either, even if I don’t have it as hard as her, but she looks at me like she wants to be me and I hate it.

•

I can’t get off to anything but being called a boy. I want to stop. But everything about changing sexual preferences is so right-wing.

Have you considered:

•

The fact that she isn’t enjoying herself is the point. Still, she could instead be not enjoying herself while doing other things less hazardous to her health.

•

She needs healthier role models and ways to measure her progress. In the bigger picture, she needs to stop measuring herself against you. She probably doesn’t recognize your faults, and as her sister you have the instinct to hide them from her - try airing those out and hopefully that will break her out of it.

•

I don’t think sexual preferences change over time so much as they reveal themselves. That said, this is very concerning. You could try getting really into Ouran Highschool Host Club, Pretty Boy Detective Club, or Hana-Kimi; I hear Heyer and du Maurier are also very interested in the circumstances of people who act like boys but are actually girls. Leviathan got animated recently but I don’t have the stomach for 3d.

Transgender women, having identified the cause of their pain, may refuse to hurt others; in such cases, they often choose to hurt themselves instead as a means of maintaining control. If this doesn’t make much sense to you you should get to know at least one woman more intimately. Women in pain seek alternately to obliterate and solidify their own agency. Last through the downswing and help her build herself up when the time comes.

The most immediate thing, of course, is to stop the self-harming behavior directly. She seeks out drug abuse, cutting, and magic gathering to hurt herself because she feels that pain is what she deserves. Gently but firmly remove the offending objects from her direct vicinity, but understand that a sufficiently-motivated girl can hurt herself with just about anything. No amount of indulging in her desire to hurt herself will give her what she wants - and on some level she does know this. You want to focus on giving her safer and healthier ways to express her pain. Women often turn to the arts for this purpose, but if she needs to go be out in the woods or plunge herself into virtual worlds for a day, well, escapism is often preferable as a matter of harm reduction.

Remember: girls self-harm not just to hurt herself but also as a speech act. She wants to be caught. If she is deliberately not eating, or cutting herself, that is a message. Listen.

IV: Escapisms.

•

[Name Withheld] has gotten really into ball-jointed dolls recently. She only ever wears dresses, but every single one of her dolls is dressed in ridiculous cyberpunk outfits.

•

I’m in love with another trans girl and she keeps playing really long terrible JRPGs.

•

She insists on snowboarding, no matter what I do, and she won’t stay with me on the slopes. And I can’t even follow her on skis because she isn’t even good enough to stay ahead of me.

Have you considered:

•

introducing her to kigurumi? Sometimes having the doll be something that isn’t you is part of it for her owner, but if she’s projecting her gender through vectors that aren’t herself, she can at least be allowed to embody that more directly.

•

that she needs somebody who she can listen to, when she tells her that games where you collect party members and exploit elemental weaknesses usually aren’t good?

•

that part of snowboarding for her is the fantasy of being kind of antiestablishment with it, and that even though skiing is a better sport in every way it isn’t going to be able to feel the way she wants to feel.

Escapism isn’t inherently bad. It’s not wrong to want to be in different circumstances sometimes, especially for transgender women, whose circumstances are often terrible. Consider also that she often conceptualizes of womanhood as an escape from masculinity, rather than a sculpting force in its own right, purely out of relief from having to have short hair.

Escapism only becomes a problem when it starts interfering with everyday functionality. As with other coping mechanisms, the solution is often to make her normal life decent enough that she wants to spend her time there, rather than behind a chessboard or standing in the waves, looking out at the moon and crying. When dealing with escapism, one must also be aware that drawing her back to Earth may mean she pivots hard into other, less benign ways of coping.

V. Practical Applications

Some time ago I solicited questions for advice-column style answerings. Mostly you asked me how to get a girlfriend (which I already wrote an article about) or how to get a boyfriend (why would I know or care anything about this). Some of you wrote in about various kinds of sex, thinking it would be ‘funny’ to confront me with the existence of such.

Anyway none of you gave me the questions I was looking for so I’m going to analyze the initial three statements here instead.

It doesn’t matter how far in advance I booked our anniversary reservation - she just doesn’t want to leave the house. But whenever I try to get her to see a therapist, she leaves immediately. Sometimes it takes her days to come back.

Elements of all four approaches are present here sequentially. The subject’s desire to stay inside is a direct defense mechanism; she lashes out at her devoted girlfriend; she causes herself harm by not attending a wonderful anniversary dinner; she leaves when her girlfriend tries to get her to seek psychiatric help. The important thing here is escapism, as evidenced by the lack of direct confrontation - this girl is scared in ways that disconnect her from the world, and from her partner, who needs to have a serious talk with her about what she wants from her relationship and her plans for the future.

She’s so good with kids - better than me, even. Playing with my cousins is the only time I’ve ever seen her laugh without bitterness. But when I mention even the possibility of marriage and having our own, in five or ten years, her eyes go cold and dim.

Fear of commitment; self-denial. Self-harm, obviously. The possibility of a future frightens her because she’s so scared of losing what she has.

She refuses to wear anything even remotely masculine, but she won’t stop calling herself a boy for some reason.

Severe self-harm. If she can’t see herself as a woman, remind her of the sheer space women can occupy, and ensure her interaction with other women. Women can do anything (with of course the collorary: there are things they should not do.)

Read my content. Possibly even give me money, for it.

I’ve been thinking a lot about ‘halimede mechsploitation’, and I finished a reread of Baru Cormorant… sorry for shipping Itinerant/Hesychast. needs more time to simmer, but perhaps I may be on to something. or not. anyway I’m going to enter a meditative trance upon Iscend Comprine and her commonalities with abjection fantasies, trans and otherwise.

also been thinking about writing on: trans fantasies of abjection, the specter of gendered socialization and the ways in which it is and is not real, what a Homestuck is
