title: Fanfiction I Am Never Going To Write Or Finish 2
text:
Premises and snippets I don’t intend to have anything more to do with, seared to perfection and topped with a fried egg.

* * *

Skills I Would Have In Disco Elysium - Disco Elysium, or Can’t We Just Compromise With The Furies A Little Bit?

MIND - Analyses.

•

Thesis - Make a point; assemble a case. Indicate and contraindicate.

•

Index - Seek and derive context. Know what has been.

•

Alla Maschera - Reference type specimens; play and recognize roles.

•

Networker - Connect professionally. Eke out mutual advantage. Employ logistics.

•

Lancet - Take apart that which you do not understand. Conceptualize binaries.

•

Sight Read - Decrypt by eye. Interpret matrices of force and light.

HEART - High aspects.

•

Agency - Do what you want. Follow your heart. Governs Morale.

•

Wellspring - Weep, feel, and love, ingenue. Trace the edges of your wound.

•

Mirror Heart - Understand others through the lens of yourself.

•

Rainbow Flag - Hold high the banner. Invoke and admit solidarity.

•

Indulgence - Watch anime. Enjoy one glass of wine. Find relaxing projects.

•

Blue Bird - Have fun and be funny! Get serious about taking yourself less seriously.

SOUL - Deep aspects.

•

Tolerance - Put up with it. Keep the mask from slipping. Governs Composure.

•

Capital Column - Leverage hierarchies. Acknowledge cost. Thus unto Jupiter.

•

Red Thread - Subject or object; bind and be bound.

•

Mother’s Daughter - Stand at the end of a long line of women.

•

Animus - Hate. Define yourself in opposition; oppose definition.

•

Neptune Nine - Accept the depths. Choke down hard truths.

HAND - Manipulations.

•

Program (Routine?) - Prepare and execute sequences of movement.

•

Perception - Open yourself to the world. Receive sensory input.

•

Ring Light - Control your image, and detect cracks in the images of others.

•

Little Mary - Be good. Perform. Stand under the spotlight.

•

Fingerwork - Connect to physical systems. Play the instrument of yourself.

•

Arc Tracery - Move with grace. Improvise motions into greater wholes.

I really recommend doing this for yourself, and possibly even posting it in the comments here - I found it very fun to comb my private narrativizations into something more presentable.

* * *

Minecraft Streaming Parasociality Exercise - Minecraft

A project I had planned a few years ago after hearing about minecraft smp roleplay servers and deciding I could do it better obviously but never seriously intended to complete, due to the high time requirements.

A very sad girl decides to mine out the entire world in Minecraft. She only rarely looks at chat and spends hours and hours taking the world down to bedrock chunk by chunk. Because of phantoms and other enemies etc she has to build a little infrastructure - furnaces beds crafting and enchantment tables - but she always prioritizes her mission. A friend or two shows up occasionally but they eventually stop coming. She acquires a dog and it dies - let this be emergent, because Minecraft is very good at killing dogs - and becomes visibly emotionally distraught. Another girl, ideally one who has been in chat for a while, shows up and starts mining with her eventually. She is slow to open up but reveals a tragic story (all carefully plotted behind the scenes) but then says it was fake and the girl who showed up leaves. During her next video she admits it was real. During her next video she cries for the first time. It is critical to writing this that the text all be one big block like this. If you try and space it out to make it read better it would read much worse actually. Likewise with commas.

* * *

FLAME, CLEANSE ME - Elden Ring

A Tarnished on track for the Frenzied Flame ending compels Cleanrot Knight Finlay to accompany her to the Land Of Shadow, where she intends to force every scrap of lore out of Miquella.

The workshop had been available after the death of its previous owner. Aethel might once have considered it to be in terrible taste, but it had at least saved her the trouble of installing manacles.

Not that she would be in any real danger, or that her prisoner might escape, but it made things easier.

The sword and scythe she left visible at the end of the room. The prisoner she left naked, inspected closely, reconsidered, and dressed her in a maiden’s cloth garb. The armor she left in a heap outside, to burn with the rest of the world.

And then she stood and waited, for longer than a human should have been able to, until that prisoner awoke.

The prisoner woke slowly. Well, she’d drugged her; she should have expected that. She looked her captor up and down and tested her manacles throughly.

“Were I unbound,” she said, “I would kill thee where thou standst. I would flay thy skin from thy flesh and thy flesh from thy bones. I would gut thee like a fish and stake out thy body as a feast for the dogs and the birds. I would consign thee to the Frenzied Flame, and to an eternity with execrable Shabriri.”

“You would try,” said Aethel. “And anyway we’ve met. ‘May chaos take the world!’. He made some good points, actually.”

“Release me now and thy death will be swift.”

“No,” Aethel said. “No, I don’t think it will. Are you done?”

The prisoner spat in her face.

“What you should be doing, objectively,” Aethel continued, “is asking me what I want. You don’t even know what you’re withholding.”

“I would forgo burial before betraying the Haligtree,” said her prisoner, glaring downward. “Go fuck thyself.”

“See,” said her captor, “that’s exactly what I’m talking about. I’m not interested in the Haligtree. I’ve been there. That’s where I got you. Cored it out like an apple – not that you’d believe me. Do you even know what an apple is?”

“Go fuck thyself.”

“So you don’t, then.”

The prisoner’s face was incredulous. “Thou thinkest fair Leyndell had no orchards? If thou hadst visited the Haligtree, as thou claimest, thou wouldst surely have seen them.”

Her captor shrugged. “Didn’t see any.” And then, once that revelation had hung in the air for a few seconds: “You really want to talk, don’t you? You can’t help yourself. How long has it been, I wonder?”

“Go fuck thyself.”

“Nearly an age, I think. Or hope. Look, I’ll make this easier for you. Rowa raisins and a whip, right? Here’s your raisins: I know where Miquella is.”

“Where he ever was, despicable whore.”

Aethel tilted her head. “Not a bad bluff. If I didn’t know the truth, I might even have bought it. But it’s your duty to listen to me now, isn’t it? For even the slightest chance you might get to take that info back home.”

She let that sink in, watching her prisoner’s face very closely. Finally, her prisoner said:

“If thou speakest true, I would listen better out of irons.”

“Yes, there you go. But this works best with a whip, doesn’t it?”

…

[PoV change.]

There was a knife in her hand. Finlay hadn’t seen her draw it, but she hadn’t been watching. Her grip was loose, and she waved it around like she thought she could scare her into giving up whatever it was she wanted. Had she not known who Finlay was? What she’d seen?

Her ashes had been left in the Haligtree. Far easier to believe that there had been a traitor within their ranks, who had smuggled her away, than to believe this nearly naked blunderer. The twin demigods had no shortage of enemies.

Although. Praetor Rykard and the Carians would have had more competent interrogators; Capital cultist filth, even Gideon’s, wouldn’t have bothered with this farce, and the Redmanes would not have left her alive. The Golden Lineage, perhaps? Godwin’s get? But not even they were such buffoons.

If not their enemies, then perhaps their so-called allies.

Appropriate, then, that that idiot Tarnished was holding a mercy-knife. Not that she ever would have expressed doubt in Lord Miquella’s choice of allies, but Ranni’s tastes had always been eclectic.

She hadn’t just been testing her bonds when she woke up; she’d been testing her range of motion, and confirming the formless seal remained on her hand.

Enough of this tiresome theater. She’d pull Lord Miquella’s location out of this Tarnished recusant herself.

Law of Regression.

The first of the two fundamental principles: that all things long to be one – to return to the primitive unified state.

Darkness.

And for their blindness in defying the Two Fingers their sight shall be confounded; and therein as wild beasts fall upon them.

(And then she fails, and then Aethel brings out the Charming Branches from the Land of Shadow, craftable only with Empyrean-blood Burgeons… and doesn’t use them. She reminds Finlay that she’s her only hope of tracking Miquella down.)

(Finlay grits her teeth and complies.)

* * *

title: Against 'Gender Identity'
text:
I really hate this whole “identifies as a woman” thing. I don’t “identify” as a girl, and the idea I would is ridiculous. “identifies as” in this construction exists *exclusively* to distance trans women from womanhood. she does not “identify as” a woman; she is a woman. -@HalimedeMF, 9/11/2023

* * *

What, exactly, is a ‘gender identity’?

Let’s take a look at that execrable genderbread person.

A ‘gender identity’ does not inflect on how somebody acts; how they present themselves; who they are attracted to, and how that attraction manifests; or the biological realities of the body; or even pronouns, or personalities, or basically anything really. A ‘gender identity’ is abstracted so far it is meaningless. A ‘gender identity’ is a perfectly irrelevant box to check - a way to say that something doesn’t actually mean any of the things we all know it means.

Everybody already knows what gender is! A gender is a cause, not an effect. A gender colors relationships, sexual and otherwise; it puts pressures on its bearer, moving them towards certain propensities and approaches and away from others. We know there are women, and non-binary people, and even men; we know gender non-conformity doesn’t disqualify one from a gender - women usually do woman stuff but can fix cars and care about sports and do pretty much anything that men can do; men usually do guy stuff but can do drag and even get pregnant sometimes, although the ones who do that were raised wrongly as girls by parents who failed to understand them; non-binary people define themselves as unaffiliated with the two cardinal genders and are still getting solidified as a cluster, although much of their whole deal involves defiance of binary norms so individual variance is obviously going to be higher.

You can defy your assigned gender, of course - but not your real one, not for long, or it’ll take a serious mental toll. You can deviate from its norms, sure - you can be homosexual, or bisexual, or a man who likes marine biology, or a woman with penis envy, or a girl who thinks it’s really hot to wear a little newsie cap and dress as a boy in order to attend the academy in your twin brother’s place until his best friend corners you and asks you what you’re doing there and teaches you how to walk and talk and speak - but only for his best friend, only until he comes back. That’s all normal. In fact, when you’re doing those things which are abnormal for your gender, you are still doing them through the lens of your gender.

You might think “well, my gender doesn’t affect my life that much.” Go on then - go without it! Here is a quote which I keep on my desktop at all times, which I read to keep myself humble:

“You think that I am naive, but it is you who are naive. You have no idea what is happening inside of you when you look at a painting. You think that you are getting close to art voluntarily, enticed by its beauty, that this intimacy is taking place in an atmosphere of freedom and that delight is being born in you spontaneously, lured by the divine rod of Beauty. In truth, a hand has grabbed you by the scruff of the neck, led you to this painting and has thrown you to your knees. A will mightier than your own told you to attempt to experience the appropriate emotions. Whose hand and whose will? That hand is not the hand of a single man, the will is collective, born in an interhuman dimension, quite alien to you. So you do not admire at all, you merely try to admire.”

― Witold Gombrowicz

(Somebody posted this at me once and it is one of the closest things I have to religion.)

So where is this ‘gender identity’ used? Do men ‘identify’ as men? No. The rhetorics of masculinity are clear; one ‘becomes a man’ by action. Do women ‘identify’ as women? No. The passage from girlhood to womanhood is understood to occur on maturity, with the onset of menarche, and/or heterosexual marriage and the subsequent loss of virginity. If you ask a man if he identifies as a man, he will rightly perceive that to be an insult - you insinuate that he is a child, rather than an adult. If you ask a woman if she identifies as a woman, she will rightly perceive this to be an insult - you frame her maturity and the process of undergoing her life as inauthentic.

(If you ask a non-binary person if they ‘identify’ as non-binary, they will tell you all about their gender configuration. This is because nonbinary people are desperate for recognition, and mistake the hostile spotlight of ‘identify as’ as a means of validation. If non-binary people got more respect from society and, consequently, had more self-respect, this problem would fix itself.1)

So where and when does ‘gender identity’ as a term see use? People are told to respect others’ gender identities when those identities are seen as separate from their presentation, with the implication that gender identity is something fully decoupled from reality - hence all those terrible ‘my gender is an attack helicopter’ jokes.

And who does this term ‘gender identity’ get aimed at? All gendered presentation is regulated, but which group in particular stares down the barrel of the madonna-whore complex, as aimed by women who really should know better?

I’ll give you a hint: people really hate transgender women. No, I mean they really hate transgender women. It is very very difficult for people who are not transgender women to understand just how much people hate transgender women; it slides off the mind like the historical reality of marital rape or the evils of factory farming. I am continually surprised and horrified by childhood anecdotes that transgender women drop offhand, or even laugh about. I’ve known a girl who wasn’t allowed to tie a jacket around her waist, because that was too feminine; I’ve known more than one who had her hair cut off as punishment. The fucking Geneva Convention says you can’t do that!

After that interview with M, while I was cleaning up the transcript, I did ask her why, as she was a lesbian, she loved her grandmother so much if she expected her to marry a man. She said that her grandmother’s expectations at least acknowledged her as a woman, and that all her other family members had done far worse. I wanted to disagree, because she might have just considered her a gay man, but held my tongue. Sorry M. She probably thought gay men were a type of woman anyway.

People hate trans women so so much. Did you know the term tr*vesty comes from travesti2? Little wonder the Baeddels, that oft-hated clique of transgender separatists, were so taken with their name; imagine being so hated that the term for you is the root of the very word ‘bad’ itself!

Anyway.

The entire purpose of “gender identity’ is as a prophylactic used to prevent trans women from reaching their rightful place.

Here’s my favorite definition of womanhood, from the incomparable Simone de Beauvoir’s The Second Sex:

“Woman is defined neither by her hormones nor by mysterious instincts but by the way she grasps, through foreign consciousnesses, her body and relationship to the world.”

The condition of this alienation and the ensuing double-consciousness is foundational to womanhood. It is then a particularly a sick and sad irony that those women most historically divorced from the truth of their genders have instead been subject to hyperscrutiny even beyond that applied to most women.

Transgender women, as I keep saying, are the women of women.

get me in your email; consider paying me.

huh. there’s a setting for ‘free subscribers only’? I could make like an anti-patreon, where you would pay me to not see my posts. well, food for thought.

1

Also, non-binary identity seems tied to alienation from the two cardinal genders, which may make it possible someday to “identify as non-binary“ - gendered alignment is not symmetrical! Enough of that. I am a girl and all that is non-binary’s own business.

2

If you have an argument about culturally-bound third-gender identities on the tip of your tongue, go read Talia Bhatt about it.

title: The Tokyo Yushun Is Decadent And Depraved
text:
The air was thick and hot, like a stable after a race. Inside, people hugged each other and shook hands … big grins and a whoop here and there: “By God! You old bastard! Good to see you, stud! Damn good … and I mean it!”

In the air-conditioned lounge I met a little horsegirl from Osaka who said her name was something or other — “but just call me Ossan” — and she was here to get it on. “I’m ready for anything, ya hear me! Anything at all. Yeah, whatcha drinkin?” I ordered a whiskey, but she wouldn’t hear of it: “Naw, naw … what the hell kind of drink is that for Nihon Derby time? What’s wrong with ya, boy?” She grinned and winked at the bartender. “Goddam, we gotta teach ya how it goes in Fuchu! Get him some fresh carrot juice1.”

I shrugged. “Okay, a carrot juice on ice.” Ossan nodded her approval.

“Oi.” She flicked my arm to make sure I was listening; I had to rub it for the sting. “Take it from ol’ Makibao — this ain’t no town to be givin’ people the impression you’re some kinda nag. If ya wanna knock one back after work, sure, go ahead, but stay dry for the Derby. Those Umamusume run with everything they got, and ya owe them your best behavior.”

The carrot juice was cold and sweet. I thanked Ossan, or Makibao, and fitted a Marlboro into my cigarette holder.

“Ya tryin ta give me cancer? Dintcha hear anything I just said?”

I apologized.

“Oi, Oi! Didja honestly think I was running?” She waved her hand in a “come off it” gesture. “Ah’m too old for that shit … Here. Gimme a light, boy.”

I lit the cigarette she was holding, which turned out to be the one I’d inserted into my holder a few seconds earlier. She grinned remorselessly. Horsegirls. They always keep you on your toes.

“You some kinda trainer or somethin?”

“No,” I said. “I’m a photographer.”

“Oh yeah?” She eyed my ragged leather bag with new interest. “Is that whatcha got there — cameras? Who ya workin for?”

“Playboy,” I said.

Now that had her attention.

“Hot damn!” She cried. “Picked a helluva year to show up! You seen the crowdpleasers2 on Narita Top Road? Beautiful eyes, beautiful thighs. And she’s gonna need em for that last Tokyo 200. They oughta give ya some kinda damn medal for gettin ol’ Kaicho to sign off on that, ‘specially when her number two hates cameras so much. So tell me.” She leaned in conspiratorially. “How’d ya do it?”

I coughed and stared at her for a moment, trying to maintain my air of sobriety.

Her voice went low. “Kaicho did sign off, right?” For a moment I saw her as the racer she must have been: a flash of white lightning, each step a thunderbolt.

I chose my next words very carefully.

“There’s going to be trouble.” I said. “I’m here to take pictures of the monster.”

“What monster?”

I tipped the last drops of carrot juice into my mouth, and considered ordering another.

“At Shinagawa. On Derby Day. Coming out of the sea.” I stared at her again. “Don’t you read the newspapers?”

Her grin dripped into a scowl. “What the hell are you talkin about?”

“Well … maybe I shouldn’t be telling you … ” I shrugged, nervous as anyone would be talking to somebody who could crush their ribcage as easily as a beer can. “But hell, everybody seems to know. The cops and the JSDF have been getting ready for weeks. They have tanks and fighter jets and a giant electric fence and they’re working on something called an Oxygen Destroyer if that isn’t enough. They warned us — all the press and photographers — to wear helmets and special vests like flak jackets. We were told to expect massive casualties … ”

“No!” she shouted; her hands flew up and hovered momentarily between us, as if to ward off the words she was hearing. Then she bounced her palm off her forehead. “Three Almighty Goddesses! The damn Nihon Derby!” Her tail swished vigorously. “No! Dammit! I can’t fucking believe it!” Now she seemed to be jagging on the stool, and when she looked up her eyes were misty. “He was supposed to hit Mise, not Tokyo! Next you’re gonna be telling me there’s going to be some kind of giant monkey collab too!3”

I shrugged again.

She sat for a moment, looking hurt and confused and not quite able to digest all this terrible news. Then she cried out: “Christ! Like that damn Tokyo Zelkova wasn’t bad enough! I gotta call Masami-chan right now — get the damn shoes waterproofed — get her ponies front-running ready.”

I picked up my bag. “Thanks for the drink … and good luck.”

“Oi.” She called, from the doorway. “Pay yer own tab, boy!”

The carrot juice had been delicious; mildly resentful of that fact, and of being called boy so often by a girl probably half my age — though of course there was never really any way of telling with horsegirls — I paid and left.

Ω

Umamusume: Pretty Derby (lit: Horsegirls: Pretty Derby. Does that help?) is a game/anime/multimedia project by Cygames about training anime girls who are the personifications of specific Japanese racehorses. They go to horsegirl school for horsegirls and have ear- and tail-care routines and run on racetracks and sing idol songs. I don’t think this really needs any more explanation.

It’s easy to gawk at the premise - the girls are horses? With little horsey ears and tails? And they wear skimpy little outfits and sing songs? How could you possibly get any non-ironic enjoyment out of this, Halimede? We thought your taste was immaculate, as proven by your excellent opinions on literature, feminism, and mecha anime!

I don’t actually care what you think about my taste. We are in this together because you have subscribed to or just bookmarked my substack, as well as my feed of tweets; possibly you have even chose to pay me money for doing this to you. You have proven definitively that you value my opinions and therefore you will have those opinions expounded upon to you at great length, until or unless you leave this page.

Umamusume commits completely to the bit. Cygames anime Akiba Maid War, Brave Bang Bravern, and Apocalypse Hotel all play silly characters and premises incredibly straight - but Umamusume did it first.

You might have seen this image around. The kanji for horse, Uma, is drawn with four marks representing legs; in the world of Umamusume, where horses are girls, it’s drawn with only two. Hm, you might think. That’s a funny joke to put a little thought into.

Special Week (not pictured here), raised by her human mother, uses a human phone before she goes off to Horse Anime School where accommodations for horse girls are normal - like these long phones that go up to their horse ears4. Horse girls use chairs with holes for their tails, and special lanes like bike lanes so they can run on roads safely, and wear horseshoes as cleats on the track. The Statue of Liberty has horse ears because Umamusume are considered by everybody everywhere to be symbols of freedom and power.

But it’s not just worldbuilding that gets this attention. Let me dissect for you Agnes Tachyon’s design:

Her hair color comes from the real life horse.

Her boots are white because of the real horse’s feet; heels, of course, match the angle of the hoof. For my money, the topline’s shape is meant to draw attention to the thinness and fragility of her legs.

She wears a lab coat because of her sciency name - Tachyon, a particle faster than light.

The light blue striping and long yellow shirt come from her jockey’s silks.

The number four - four buttons on her sleeves, four diamond zippers, four stripes, four vials - repeats because the horse won all four races entered before retirement and because four in Japanese is considered unlucky, as its career ended early.

Her moe sleeves make her seem smaller and more vulnerable - fitting for a glass cannon racer - and hide her hands, as she hides her weakness through her route.

Her hair ornament is on the right side, indicating she bears a stallion name. Having a hair ornament on the left side would indicate a mare. One horsegirl, Fine Motion, has one on each side because her namesake has an intersex chromosomal abnormality that makes her unable to bear children.

Her hair ornament is a benzene ring sharing a side with a cyclopentane ring - a volatile biochemical fuel, befitting of a horse that burned out early.

Her hair ornament is also 5/6, referencing her mother Agnes Flora’s race record.

Her eyes have four lines in them - for the previous reasons four is used, but also as an reference to the double-slit experiment, which famously demonstrates light’s behavior as both particle and wave (I trust Sakugabooru on this one!). She obsesses over possibilities and might-have-beens, since her own fragility threatens to destroy her potential.

Everything in Umamusume is like this. If you embed enough details and context into a work, sometimes that’s almost like making it actually good!

And sometimes it even is.

I’ve had more Umamusume hit than miss so far. Sometimes you get a girl like Winning Ticket, who is assiduously based on an actual horse and jockey but isn’t actually compelling at all; but sometimes you get a TM Opera O (horse with a record string of victories, represented as a delightfully self-aggrandizing theater kid), Haru Urara (horse that lost 113 consecutive races but kept on running, represented as a sweet girl who gets very easily distracted), or King Halo (horse from a storied lineage who lost 10 attempts to win a top grade race in a row before finally winning on the 11th represented as a girl whose pride is all she has in the face of her fans’ expectations and her abusive mother). Also sometimes you get a Fuji Kiseki (horse who had to retire early but had many children, represented as a Takarazuka otokoyaku to convey a suave playboy nature) and I am not immune to a butch with open-backed gloves.

Also, if you make enough anime girls some of them will read as transgender. Oguri Cap is a tall girl who runs fast and eats a lot with a dead eyes and a cartilage disorder that gives her joint hypermobility who can only focus on her special interests and gets scared the first time she wears a skirt. And like five girls are desperately trying to get into her pants and she has no idea, just like trans in real life.

Hold on to that thought.

Ω

There was a track, and a clubhouse, and a paddock, but only the miserable heat was befitting of the Derby.

Now, looking down from the grandstands, I pointed to the huge grassy meadow enclosed by the track. “That whole thing,” I said, “should be jammed with people; two hundred twenty thousand max. If this were America they’d all be drunk. Now there’s a fantastic scene - thousands of people, men and women and horsegirls, packed so thick their bodies squeeze the air out of your lungs, fainting, crying, copulating; experiencing the fullness and hideousness of life. But this is Japan, so probably they’ll just clap politely or bow or some shit.”

Kzar, my illustrator, sketched with her head down - either too shy or too proud to show off her work.

“You know what they’ve done to the Tokyo infield? It’s a goddamned playground. They have a bounce house, and swings, and a tiny little track for ponies to run on while their parents take pictures. I went over there. Nobody even looked at me weird, or tried to keep me away from their daughters. I could have just scooped one up and taken her home to do god knows what.”

“No you couldn’t, said Kzar, intent on her sketchpad. “You wouldn’t be able to catch her.”

I went on. “Probably Japanese perverts do it all the time. You know there’s a little button you can press to play the fanfare, and their little gates are padded just in case they get too excited and run into them? And they have a wall full of past winners’ plastic ear ornaments so they can play dress-up? Makes me want to vomit.”

“Mhmm,” said Kzar.

“Up here in the stands it ought to be worse. See, from up here people look down on the roiling mass of meat below us in contempt. That’s the true nature of the human animal; the second we get one single step up on the others, we shit right down on them like they’re a completely different species. When you’ve got something to lose - when your neighbor has something to lose, and you both know it - when a single push down that vomit-slick slippery grandstand slope will send one of you careening into the writhing paste of meat and shit - the humane thing to do is strike first, so he doesn’t have to pollute his conscience with the sordid deed. Take the choice right out of his hands. The further up you go, the lonelier you get; pity the man up at the top, so far up he can barely see the track and nobody to blame but himself. He can faint and cry and fuck himself up there in the rarefied air and nobody else is ever going to do it for him. Nobody ever can.”

“Hm,” said Kzar.

“And that’s what the racetrack is for,” I said. “Here the man at the top and the man on the bottom alike whore themselves out to Lady Luck. Hell, even the women do it. When the race starts everybody but you stares transfixed; you alone are a superior being, betting only what you can afford according to private superstition or ‘the numbers’, in which case you are a soulless robotic hack. By the time those thoroughbreds hit the homestretch you’re one of them, rabid and slavering, incapable even of gulping down your drool at the thought of victory - of humiliating anybody and everybody who’s ever dared to think him or herself smarter than you. That’s the whole fucking point. Pardon my French.”

“Certainly,” said Kzar. One of her ears flicked sideways.

Ω

You’d think that the premise would mean that Umamusume is entirely fetish-based, and there are certainly fetish-based horses, but because of horse licensing Umamusume’s world is so squeaky-clean it doesn’t even allow gambling. Some horses drink out of hip flasks, but that’s always barley tea or electrolyte drinks; horses with wine glasses are always sipping juice.

Which isn’t to say that horse owners are all scrupulous; see Still In Love’s yandere spiral and the owner of Nishino Flower and Seiun Sky introducing himself on twitter as “the man who made that pairing”. 5

Anyways, Umamusume’s original 2018 trailer features bouncing breasts and ass shots and a horsegirl making advances on another horsegirl who is clearly uncomfortable. The horsegirl who did this has never appeared since, and several others in that trailer took years and reworked designs to make their appearances. Presumably behind the scenes somebody said “You can’t make my horse a molester” and pulled their licensing, meaning Cygames had to retool the whole concept.

What this means in practice is that Umamusume fanservice is comparatively restrained and the really juicy stuff exists almost entirely by implication, perceivable only by particularly dedicated database animals.

For instance:

Gold Ship can get dragged off by Maruzensky and Seeking The Pearl to learn about the “world of adults”, after which she is visibly tired, with a strange look in her eyes.

Meisho Doto’s enjoyment of spicy food codes for masochism.

Fuji Kiseki declares Zenno Rob Roy her little sister. Rice Shower declares you her big sister. We’re all familiar with Class S.

Showa-era girl Maruzensky’s fondness for tiramisu is tied to its perception as a date-night food in post-war Japan - specifically to keep a couple going for after-date activities.

Mayano Top Gun is a very precocious little girl who thinks she really wants romantic attention from her trainer.

Super Creek has an event titled “How many do you want?”, and an event where she dreams all her friends have been turned into babies, which she is thrilled by, and the infamous “Trainer! I want to play goo-goo babies today!”

The level of yuri baiting they do with these horse girls really is tremendous; you’ve probably already seen Vodka and Daiwa Scarlet butchfemme, but did you know Special Week canonically has two moms? Jungle Pocket and Agnes Tachyon have an awful toxic codependent mutual hatecrush based on jealousy. Symboli Rudolf is effectively cheating on her basically-wife Air Groove with her basically-mistress Maruzensky and her basically-cousin Sirius Symboli and sixty-year-old single woman permanently on vacation Mejiro Ramonu. Almost every Umamusume (with one exception) is gay, bi, or too young/innocent/obsessed with speed to the exclusion of all else for romance. This isn’t even touching on playersexuality - this is just strictly ship teasing with other horsegirls. As for that, well, Rice Shower calls you her Big Sister if you pick the girl choice so. While I can’t approve I at least appreciate that they put some effort into it.

Ω

“Look,” I said. “I’m not trying to stroke my own ego here. I’m as bad as any other sonovabitch; worse even for knowing it. But this Japanese bullcrap is just over the fucking line. You ‘Umamusume’ are fierce and noble creatures, by divine right the maenads of this whole bacchanalian ecstasy, and they dress you up in these frilly little outfits and make you sing and dance. Don’t get me wrong, I’m a red-blooded heterosexual American man; I had a pinup of Northern Dancer on my wall as a teen. But it’s debasing, is what it is. This is a level of filth I just cannot abide. Warfare revolved around you girls for thousands of years and they have you doing cutesy neotenous choreographies for an audience of virgin nerds, or worse, full-grown married men. And women, of course. Women eat it up; some bullshit about empowerment, probably. No smokes no drinks no cocaine no dirt no trash just this hypocritical insistence that everything at the bloodbath be spick-span clean. Say what you want about America, but we understand horsegirls should be getting dipped in chocolate and drinking entire goddam kegs on the taxpayer’s dollar.”

Kzar said nothing at all.

“What, you wouldn’t turn down a keg, would you?” I said.

She shrugged. “Not usually, no. But races are different. Les fillies cheval are born to run; is that not intoxication enough?”

Perhaps for them. As a mortal man personally I prefer cocaine, but I was smart enough to not say that out loud.

Ω

I also really like how mentally ill Umamusume can get.

As with fanservice, there are many qualifiers here. No anime horsegirl can make the horse look bad, lest the licensor retract permissions. They can’t commit physical violence or participate in clearly sexual activities. Umamusume are beloved; there is no anti-Uma prejudice. Most of their issues (with exceptions, like King Halo’s abusive mother or Agnes Tachyon’s fragile legs) are internal.

Here is a list of problems Umamusume cause for themselves that the owners of their respective racehorses signed off on:

Basically every other Umamusume has an eating disorder and will work herself to the point of injury if you let her. A significant portion of your job as a trainer is to say “No, you need to eat more and not train too hard because you will break your legs.”

Fuji Kiseki’s refusal to back down in front of a crowd means that she forces herself to run races her body isn’t suited for, convinced that her fans want to see her do the impossible.

Symboli Rudolf has decided that all Umanity needs a leader, that only she is worthy, and that the only way she can do this is by never losing a race. Losing only makes her double down.

Nice Nature’s easygoing demeanor conceals pathologically low self-esteem. She alienates those around her by refusing to take them seriously - if a worthless girl like her managed to outrace them, they couldn’t have been that good anyway.

Super Creek constantly projects her own needs onto her trainer and everyone around her and insists on trying to fulfill herself by constantly babying them.

Machikane Fukukitaru tells another horsegirl to her face that all her years of training and effort were meaningless, because luck is the only thing that matters. Her entire room is full of lucky objects she refuses to get rid of - not like, lucky charms, like yogurt lids she had when she came in second in a third grade spelling bee. She keeps trying to convince herself that not dying will somehow make her happy. She loses her lucky handkerchief, which she believes is the only reason that her few friends spend any time with her, and tells them they can leave now.

Admire Vega is haunted by the ghost of her aborted twin horse girl sister, and spends her route punishing herself for having fun running and forgetting about her, I repeat, dead twin horse girl sister. She promises to push her legs until they break as penance, for the selfishness, of forgetting her dead twin horse girl sister.

Their mental illnesses may be near-entirely self-inflicted, but they’re never narratively condemned for that. This has a lot in common with how I think about trans women. Which makes sense, as trans women are a kind of very jumpy and twitchy beautiful and special creature with incredible potential that often cause their own problems. Even in a world where misogyny didn’t exist, I have faith that trans women would develop strange and upsetting mental illnesses, and become cured of them through the power of friendship, eating lots of food, and running very fast.

Ω

The Derby was fine; my horse lost honorably and applauded the winner, resulting in a change of zero dollars to my net worth whatsoever. I drank my body weight in carrot juice and resolved to win my own honor back by getting wasted alone in my hotel room that night.

But there was one more indignity in store. Kzar dragged me kicking and screaming to the Winning Live concert with the unfair incentive of some of those enormous Japanese bottles of sake and a drinking companion. Only afterward, once my head was spinning pleasantly, did I finally understand: horse girls are beautiful creatures no matter what you do to them. Even the stupidest little frilly outfits and begrudgingly catchy Jpop fail to sully the untarnishable truth: they are umamusume. They are born to run.

I was coming off three days of sobriety, counting the plane ride, where the attendants refused to sell me any more alcohol after I set off the bathroom smoke detector. We were sitting on the floor in my hotel room, our heads on the unmade bed, looking up at the ceiling. My knees were drawn up to my chest; Kzar’s long legs sprawled out to the wall.

“It’s so fucked,” I said. “This whole world - all of it. All of it but you.”

I looked over at her. She stared up at the ceiling, golden hair fanned out on the bed, perfectly indifferent to my adulations - just how I liked it.

One of the really wonderful things about horsegirls is that they’re completely and utterly unafraid of you, even when maybe they should be. You ever talk to a woman who’s convinced you’re going to drag her off into an alley and have your way with her even though she is incredibly unattractive? It’s no fun for either of you. Women think of themselves as victims; horsegirls think of themselves as people.

I asked her to fuck and she said no and I respected her boundaries because she could maim or kill me if she wanted and I did not want her to want that. And then she told me a story.

When Kzar had been a child, she been paid once, in candy, to fix an impromptu playground race, by a father who just wanted his daughter to have a victory. And in the heat of the race, legs pounding on the track, the sun beating down on her back, she forgot, and ran all out, and the other girl won anyway. This transaction had haunted her every day and night since; no rivals or titles - and she had several of each, before she went to art school - could erase it. Sleeping with me would only have made it worse, and also she was exclusively sexually attracted to women with ears like her own.

“Heavy stuff,” I said. “Women are so stupid. Stupider than men, but at least they have an excuse.”

“Hah,” she said.

We left it at that.

Ω

Special thanks to The Umamusume Trivia Doc, Fer of Umadacchi Densetsu, and Hunter S Thompson. And Narita Top Road, of course.

title: What are Halimede impersonators really after?
text:
There was no Halimede, and then there was Halimede. And then there were more.

I posted for three years before The Tweet1 took off. Adaptive radiation took its course, and clade Halimeda speciated freely. Evidence of Halimedes has been recorded on twitter, Instagram, Discord, tiktok, tumblr, grindr, Lex, video game lobbies, wplace, and even, in one particularly memorable case, a gay bar bathroom wall.

Yet very few of these Halimedes have persisted.

I tracked down M, a transgender woman behind one of these short-lived Halimedes, and sat down with her over Discord to discuss her reasoning. She was fairly compensated for this interview. During our conversation, which has been edited for length and clarity, we explored the experience of running a Halimede account, the inevitable consequences of Postmodernism, and Hollow Knight: Silksong.

* * *

Let’s get down to it. How do you feel about Halimede?

I really liked your article on dating trans women! Some of that stuff you said was crazy though. But you weren’t wrong. I like how you defend trans women, and I think that it’s funny that you call us transgenders. My grandma was in a home when I came out, and she only ever called me a he-she [sic], but she was always so nice to me. She told me that I looked so much happier when I wore a dress and asked me when I was bringing a nice man to meet her. Halimede might not always have the right words but she really loves trans women and that means a lot.

Thank you. I’m so sorry about your grandmother being like that.

She’s in a better place now. Or just gone maybe.

Alright. Many people like Halimede, but you wanted to take things a step further than most. What led you to try and make your own version?

I think t4t is a good thing. I love my girlfriend. She’s the most important person in my life and I love her more than anything. I wanted to support and encourage transgender women being in love with each other.

Be that as it may, why did you decide to make a Halimede about that?

Your t4t is like incest tweet really helped me make sense of two things.

Two things?

t4t is hot, and incest is hot.

That wasn’t the point of the original tweet.

Yes it was? You’re trans. You get it.

What I wrote in my article on dating trans women, was that trans women as well as non-trans women who get abandoned by family often compensate by fetishizing family-style dynamics. That’s not the same thing as finding those dynamics sexually appealing personally, which I do not. And I am not transgender.

But you do get it.

Trans women are women. You wanted to be ‘the Halimede of t4t’, something of which I specifically do not approve. Why? What does that mean for you?

I was trying to help by fixing your tweets. I think it’s funny if Halimede likes t4t.

You thought it would be funny.

Like a twist on what you do. Where you support transgender women and pretend to be cis.

I am ‘cis.’ I prefer ‘non-trans’.

Are you trans?

No. I am not trans. As I have said repeatedly.

Do you not like me?

I didn’t say that. What does being trans have to do with liking you? Halimede doesn’t approve of t4t; I have made that very clear.

Did you not like my account? Did you not think it was funny? Are you messaging me to tell me that you think an account I made two years ago wasn’t good?

I don’t approve of t4t. Halimede doesn’t approve of t4t. Those are the same thing.

I read Heaven Will Be Mine last year and you’re not really Halimede. She doesn’t have any opinions on t4t in that. She’s barely in it!

That’s not true. That is just obviously not true. I picked her up because I have that bob, and a couple of corresponding life circumstances, and because I felt like I had important things to say.

No, you just made her up out of Heaven Will Be Mine Halimede. And I made Halimede t4t out of yours. Ever heard of the dead author? If I write Italian Halimede, that’s Halimede. If I write t4t Halimede, that’s Halimede. That’s what Halimede is.

I think that viewpoint is stupid and dangerous. In removing the author, Barthes posits the text as a ‘tissue of citations’ which the reader holds within herself, redefining her as the personhoodless recipient condensed at rather than a human recipient of the author’s singular message. If you invoke the Death of the Author, what you’re saying is that you want classical criticism to be applied to the locus of you, and I don’t think you really understand the implications and consequences of that transition. Besides, removing the author from the text as an analytical device in order to highlight a less immediately-visible context in which that text was produced fails when the author’s relationships with those contexts is the main body of the text.

And not Halimedet4t. You think Halimedet4t was bad.

I don’t think you put that much thought into it. You only ran it for like a week. I was interested in what you did put into it and you didn’t really tell me much, and I think that’s because there wasn’t a lot there.

It was just a joke, yeah.

Not every project can carry the weight of a person’s whole value, and very few of them should. This is so irredeemably Modernist of me but I really do value the craft over almost everything else in the world. I know I can get a little tetchy, but it’s only because I care. About words; about transgender women.

Sorry.

I mean I didn’t care that much. It was just a joke.

…

…

We can just chat if you want. How far are you in Silksong?

I beat the game last week! It’s so good! What crest did you use?

I just got into Act III. I’ve been using Reaper for the down attack. I like Witch a lot but the heal is so unreliable…

Hunter is honestly the best one. Just don’t get hit. Changing your tools really helps. Do you have the extra slots?

I had to ask a friend for help but yes.

It’s really good with healing tools but the actual best thing with it is lifeblood. I love Hornet and Lace. Real toxic yuri t4t.

…Lace has to come back after that, right? Down in the Abyss with Grand Mother Silk. Don’t tell me what happens but she has to still be alive right?

;)

Her second fight was so good! That’s my favorite kind of boss fight; an elegant dance where nobody is slamming around the room or trying to crush you with their giant butt.

The positioning is so good. Two blades clashing like sisters. That’s what t4t is all about.

I don’t agree.

You’re not trans. You don’t get to say what t4t is.

It’s not like they’re sisters. It’s like they’re enemies with tension.

That’s what I said.

No it isn’t. Do you have a sister? Not your girlfriend. An actual sister?

She is my sister.

Like you have the same mother?

No, she has a different Mommy.

Please stop willfully misunderstanding me. Words mean things. It’s that same disagreement from earlier. I’m Halimede and you think you can just say whatever and that makes you Halimede. But you don’t say it well enough.

Who is Halimede even really? I got bored. Maybe the real Halimede was the friends we made along the way.

What does that mean?

I dunno.

No, really. What does that mean. Because people keep saying it to me, and what it looks like they mean when they say it is that Halimede is really funny and could be any one of ‘us’, where ‘us’ means trans women. That any trans woman could be Halimede. But that isn’t true. I’m Halimede. And I am not transgender.

I mean you’re somebody claiming to be Halimede.

It’s my account. I’m Halimede.

It’s just a joke.

I don’t really find it funny. I’ve been doing this as Halimede for five years because I believe in it. How is it funny.

I don’t know.

Then why did you say it.

I just thought it would be funny.

…

You don’t think it’s funny.

I don’t like that it implies that I’m trans.

But you are trans.

I’m not trans. You have already convinced yourself of what you want to hear, and will accept nothing else, even the truth.

You, the person behind Halimede, are trans. I have a friend who knew somebody who met you.

Your friend was lying.

No she wasn’t.

We can turn this into “she said, she said” all you want but I am not trans.

Because if you were a trans woman nobody would listen?

That is true, but what I’m saying is that trans women and non-trans women really aren’t that different. Trans women often have deeply internalized shame and so do non-trans women. Trans women are often traumatized and so are non-trans women. Trans women often like women, and so do some other women, called lesbians, or bisexual. Trans women are women! Trans women have women’s experiences, just more extreme in some ways. And unless you, trans women, hear this from a normal woman, you won’t believe it. And also in real life I am actually not trans. As I keep saying.

But you are trans.

Oh my god I am not trans! But nothing I do or say will ever make you girls believe me because you view transness as an insult. If I send you a voice message, you’ll just say that I went to voice therapy. If I showed you pictures, you’d say I got surgery. If I sent you a karyotype you’d dispute my allosomes!

You, as a woman, have been told that you are not worthy of the interest of other women. All women attracted to women have been told this. I say unto you: Women are half the world! Some women love gardening. Some women love rock climbing. Some women love driving. Women love smoking and fiber arts and doing laundry and getting tattoos and getting them removed and crossfit and yoga and sitting at home doing neither, and fish and puzzles and phonics and dizzying heights and Homestuck and the ocean and showering and martial arts and bondage and solitude and topology and ketamine and Final Fantasy and the taste of lavender and anorexia and only wearing blue and the Wars of the League of Cambrai, and terrible card games and the Geisel Library and Coppelia and historical revisionism and having complicated feelings about womanhood and children and child-free lifestyles and anime girl kigurumi and politics and some of them even love men! Is it so unthinkable that any of us could love you?

[response removed, per M’s request].

* * *

Halimede is a fabulist, feminist, and Modernist. You can find her here and on Twitter, and her imitators in many other places.

Receive my emails. Also you can pay me now.

title: Fanfiction I Am Never Going To Write Or Finish 1
text:
Premises and snippets I don’t intend to have anything more to do with, plated and served with a side of our fresh house salad.

* * *

Animorphs But Gay This Time - Character interpretations for a remake of the 90s YA series about teenage guerillas caught in an interplanetary war, with an eye to gayness, transness, and the closet.

Jake is a passing early-transitioning trans guy, keenly aware of gender roles and how easily they can be disrupted. He keeps his birth assignment secret, and he does it well enough that the Ellimist choses him as a pawn against the Yeerk invasion. His whole family has just moved to California, in part because they were worried about his safety1. He does well socially and in school, but that fear of being caught has never left him. His books concern leadership, privilege and invisibility, social institutions, and the costs of power - be that wealth, social clout, or responsibility.

Rachel is a girl’s girl - reckless, competitive, blonde, and (eventually) openly bisexual. She has a strong sense of honor and justice that doesn’t always line up with conventional morality, and a self-sacrificial streak that comes from valuing others over herself. Her books concern the necessity of violence and the costs it enacts on those who suffer and inflict it; social performance and respectability as armor; girl power; and the subjective nature of justice.

Cassie is figuring some things out. She’s more of an ecologist, in this version; her discovering Jake is trans and being supportive but not sure what this means for her crush on him is the climax of her first book. Her books concern peace, trying to keep being a decent person when faced with atrocity; the destruction of the world - both of nature and of humanity; broad-scale systemic changes, both social and ecological; and the personhood of enemies.

Marco is Jake’s sarcastic best friend, and not particularly attached to his gender, using it for the sake of convenience. Though he often flirts with Rachel, he’s had a crush on Jake’s older brother, Tom, for years. His jaded front hides a very different kind of ruthlessness from Rachel’s - where Rachel is willing to charge into battle, Marco is a cold and calculated planner. His books concern the triumph of pragmatism over idealism, loss and sacrifice, hiding true feelings, the pros and cons of selfishness, and the necessity of violence in time of atrocity.

“Tobias” is a closeted lesbian trans girl stuck in the foster-care system. Jake saved her from bullying, once, and is the closest thing she has to a friend. During their disastrous first mission, she gets trapped in hawk morph, and her burgeoning romance with Rachel becomes one of a very few things tying her back to humanity. Her books concern the costs of society remaining the way it is; marginalization and alienation; transmisogyny; and escapism as means of survival and its consequences.

Aximili-Esgarrouth-Isthill is an Andalite. Andalites should have some kind of complex messy gender/sexuality system that makes perfect sense to them (Aristh/Prince related?) and that isn’t immediately understandable to humans. Otherwise he’s probably mostly the same? Is ‘he’ even the right pronoun in this incarnation?

Also there really should be a yeerk defector on the team - maybe from all the way back in the construction site?

* * *

ROCK/SCISSORS was a very short planned Heaven Will Be Mine fangame about a game/conversation between Mars and Halimede. The player, as unvoiced Halimede, picks Rock or Scissors, never Paper.

(on an asteroid, in the last days of the war)

It’s been a while, huh.

I just needed to talk to somebody who couldn’t tell what I was thinking, I guess. Exactly what I’m thinking. You can tell what I’m thinking in a normal way.

Not that I don’t like you! I just. Um.

What you are to me, and what you mean to me, is you’re somebody who isn’t on my side.

I mean, I’m on the side of the children of space. And so are you. But also we have different ideals and we fight each other in giant robots, so we aren’t really on the same side.

Memorial Foundation likes to pretend that it’s on the only side there is, but any side that gets to set the terms like that isn’t playing fair. We’re on the same side, and also different sides, and that’s why I want to talk to you.

I’m not asking you to defect or anything. Even if I think what you stand for is going to hurt everyone, and if you did want to defect I’d vouch for you, and we could spend a lot more time together and get to know each other better. I just want to talk through some stuff.

They all look up to me. Almost all of them, and the only one who doesn’t has it so much worse that that I’d feel awful talking through this with her.

But you’re… I feel safe with you. That’s probably weird. I trust you, even though we’re on opposite sides. I just need to talk with somebody who has a different perspective on things.

You remember this game, right? From testing, back in Academy.

Rock or Scissors.

I need to push against somebody. Prove you’re willing to push back?

[CHOICE 1] {Rock or Scissors?}

[SCISSORS 1] {Mars plays Rock}

If you don’t want to fight me, why aren’t you on my side? {end}

[ROCK 1] {Mars plays Rock}

Okay. Good.

I feel hopeless.

Not like that. I know you think it’s hopeless, and that’s why you’re fighting for them. But I mean hopeless in a different way.

A third of us gave up on humanity.

I can understand wanting to go back to Earth. I tried for a honorable discharge, before my last tour, even if I didn’t really want it. You can understand wanting to stay in space. You’re here, aren’t you?

They dress it up as the Severance Project but what they really want is to fall in a black hole and leave everything and everyone behind. There’s no hope there at all. Can you imagine feeling like that?

[CHOICE 2] {Rock or Scissors?}

[Scissors 2] {Mars plays Scissors}

You hide it really well. I didn’t think you ever felt that way. But part of why I wanted to do this was I wanted to get to know you better.

…Of course I have too. We could leave, you know. Run off together. Never see her again.

But I think we both know that isn’t happening. {end}

[Rock 2] {Mars plays Rock}

Feelings aren’t as important as staying alive, huh. A choice between feelings and living isn’t much of a choice. Memorial Foundation always tries to control the frame.

It’s not like I want to die anymore. But why am I alive if I’m not going to follow my heart? If we don’t fight for what we believe in, do we even really believe in it at all?

Severance is, uh, isometric to death, right? Leaving everything and everyone behind, so that we no longer know and feel them. It’s not death. But it’s just the same thing in every way that matters.

Going back to Earth would be like that. Giving up on the dream of space would be like dying. Not dying. But like dying.

But we both want to fight, right?

[CHOICE 3] {Rock or Scissors?}

[Scissors 3] {Mars plays Scissors}

Okay, yes, both of us would prefer not to fight. But we’re both willing to fight to make everything better. We just have different ideas about what better means.

[Go to rock 3]

[Rock 3] {Mars plays Rock}

It’s one of those Prisoner Problems they used to give us back at the Academy. If we both play the same thing, we have to go again, and it ends when one of us decides it’s over.

I don’t want it to end.

Do you?

* * *

AN UNFORTUNATE SERIES OF EVENTS - A Series of Unfortunate Events

Young actor Olaf and fashonista Esme are pursued by mad inventor Violet Baudelaire, who has some kind of absolutely demented yuri connection to her associate Fiona Widdershins. Olaf descends into nihilism and ultimately turns on the VFD - though in abandoning the ideals of high art he eventually ends up selling himself into absolutely terrible daytime television or tiktok clickbait.

* * *

LYCORIS RED - Full Metal Demon Muramasa

The Red Spider Lily, or higanbana, is a toxic Amaryllis sp. often planted at grave sites. Ingestion, particularly of the bulbs, can cause diarrhea, vomiting, convulsion, and in the severest cases, death. Post-Hero Route. ao3 idiom; indulgent, even for me.

Koryu 44 – or 1943, by the Western reckoning

Three [two?] years have passed since Okabe Sakurako found her mangled and skinless in the shallow salt water, throat too ragged even to scream; clutching, with two fingers and less than half a thumb, at a shard of the dead steel of the masterwork which was the man and hero Goro Nyudo Masamune of Soushuu, First Under Heaven.

Masamune is dead. Three years have passed since Ayane Ichijou took up the cursed tsurugi Muramasa, and still they name her Masamune. She wears that blue shard because she can’t bear to do anything else with his remains. She’s killed with it, once – a demon, thinking her bested, unbuckled his pants. She drove it deep between his eyes and nearly smiled at the thought of the old bug’s grim laughter.

Masamune is dead, and yet her followers’ paeans fly truer than they know. Not even shin’uchi healing could wholly restore the steaming heap of flesh and slag that lay on the beach that day to human form. Parts of herself are missing – not parts she’d ever had cause to think about before she lost them. Digestion is harder now, and alcohol dangerous. Motherhood is no longer a possibility for her, though only in a single moment of delirium did she ever find the prospect even remotely appealing.

In place of these things she has steel, and she has almost managed to forget the possibility she might ever have needed anything else.

Almost.

And yet here, after the death of all beauty, is Sorimachi Ichizou to remind her. In bed, with an elf.

…

“This sucks,” says Sorimachi Ichizou. The Judea girl lies dead on the floor; he killed her himself. If he hadn’t, he might have had more than half a chance.

Ayane Ichijou has no pity for him. He brought her Masamune and, later, a squadron of kazu’uchi for her nameless army, indulging some sick perversion of his; she has accepted but never reciprocated. Sorimachi Ichizou’s evil karma has finally borne its inevitable fruit.

“Hurts-“ he hacks up a bloody piece of something that might once have been a lung, “like a bitch. Keh heh heh. No wonder people always get so mad. Wouldn’ta let that kid go if I knew he had enough spine to run to you.”

He lies, as always. The boy was in no shape to survive for long; his death was a mercy. This worm had the gall to do her what he thought was a favor.

He’s missing an arm and most of his lower half; his eyes are perfectly clear. He gave up his arm for a shot at her head, which she dodged; he purged his tsurugi in a last-ditch attack, which she dodged; his cane sword flashed with a brilliance that might have blinded her if she 1: hadn’t killed Yagyu Jo’ansai, Head of the Shinkage-Ryu, three months earlier, and 2: had given a fuck, which she did not. Instead she cut him nearly in two.

Soon she will finish the job.

“Don’t suppose you’ll let me go for old time’s sake?” he tries. “I gave you a whole boatload of tsurugi. And the truth about Kageaki, didn’t I? Even taught a girl2 some things. I’m a feminist now.”

In a minute or so it will be safe to strike. In a minute or so after that, he will die of his injuries, or he would if Ichijou suffered the wicked to live even a minute longer than necessary.

If Muramasa were here, he would already be dead. But there is other work to do; her tsurugi waits on the roof, watching for the slightest sign of an ambush. Soremachi Ichizou always has something up his sleeve.

Blood spittle froths at the corner of his mouth. “Heh. You don’t gotta answer that. I know you. You’re good as fuckin’ gold. Better. As steel. Said I was a fan and I meant it. I got a little black book on the table with my all my contacts and blackmail. Insurance. All tied up with a pretty little bow on top. You got me - it’s yours.”

Another hacking cough, wet, with a sound that might be bones grinding. Still his sword remains perfectly still. Ichijou has nothing to say.

“Sucks though,” he says. “Shoulda been Masamune. Muramasa’s a bad look on you, kid.”

He continues. “With Masamune, you woulda killed me already. Your sword was slow last time. Spider’s not taking care of you right.”

Louder, now. Yelling. “It fucking hurts! Fuck! Kill me already!” His trick sword wavers, for the first and last time–

Too many people have asked Ichijou to kill them. And yet she always obliges.

* * *

(pov switch to Sansei Muramasa, as indicated by sprites)

[[Mido. Eat.]]

Ayane Ichijou inserts food into her mouth like she loads bullets into her gun. She touches herself the same way; Muramasa has had to disturb her nightly routines more than once due to raids, and Ichijou pauses only to wipe the wet from her fingers before she reaches for her sword.

She keeps her Mido in working order, nothing more. But this one has specific requirements.

Not that she’s had any experience, but sex – if she can even call this sex – isn’t supposed to be like this.

She does not let herself think of maintenance, of polishing cloth on her shell. To think of this would break her; to break would be to deny herself the misery she deserves.

What this is is self-harm.

[[Mido. Bed.]]

Ichijou has agreed without complaint, and she hates her for that. Never once through all the bloodshed and suffering has this perfect little hero complained. She cries alone, on the beach or in the forest, where she thinks nobody can hear, and Muramasa leaves her to it.

This makes her the husband, she supposes.

And acting in the place of the man whose name she never says, even in her head, has a certain twisted appropriateness to it.

Ichijou is already stripping. She drops her clothes in a pile at the foot of the bedding; holds out her wrists, like she’s expecting Western-style handcuffs.

Well. Muramasa’s torinawajutsu is excellent, even if it feels wasted on this child. That’s how he would have done it. He would have taken his time before ravaging her, probably; made her into something beautiful to be consumed.

Steel thread cuts into pale skin. What could he have seen in this miserable little creature?

“It’s not about pain,” Ayane Ichijou says, her voice strangely unaffected. “I mean, it’s fine if you want to hurt me, but that’s not the point. It’s about being a person. Or not being a person. And closeness.”

Muramasa suspects she might understand, if she thought about it; she doesn’t care to.

She draws the binding tighter instead; tight enough to draw blood. Ichijou lets out a small gasp, and Muramasa permits herself cold satisfaction.

“Hate is closer than pain is,” says Ichijou, still in that same empty voice. “Don’t you hate me?”

It isn’t her that Muramasa hates.

PUT ME IN YOUR INBOX. or don’t.

1

There’s potential for some really nasty stuff with The Sharing and LGB transmisogyny here, or The Sharing might be more specifically Church-affiliated.

2

Ichizou’s elf is his cloned and vat-grown de-tsurugi’d Type 90 shin’uchi, explaining her origin as a Judea rather than an Emishi. This hits both Muramasa and Ichijou very hard for different reasons. They will not discuss it.

also, yes, for those of you unfamiliar with FMDM, Jewish people and Japan’s indigenous Emishi are both elves in this setting as a reference to this conspiracy theory: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese-Jewish_common_ancestry_theory

title: Project Proposal
text:
So: WHY NOW? WHY SUBSTACK?

“I’ve been told I would make it big on tumblr. But I like Twitter’s 280 character limit - it keeps me hungry, and my posts sharp” - @HalimedeMF, 9/16/23

What changed?

I’ve been feeling the urge to put out longer-form prose for a while. Five-plus years of dieting makes one want a few little treats. But that alone wasn’t enough to tip me over the edge.

The specific catalyst was a gay wedding I attended, where I ended up in conversation with a groom’s aunt. We talked about work, and retirement, and her lovely transgender niece, one of the groom’s sisters, and then the conversation turned to hobbies.

I mentioned my 20k or so twitter subscribers and was delighted when she reciprocated. She revealed that she’d been putting out a Substack newsletter for her specific hobby for years! Everyone under 30 deserves the joyful experience of discovering that a woman decades older can talk shop about engagement and user retention. She asked if I’d consider it. I told her I didn’t really need the money - but as a woman, she told me, I needed to value my own labor more highly.

And she was right! Women routinely underestimate the value of their labor. I don’t want to squeeze every dollar out of my audience but there are enough transgender women in tech following me that I could buy a few deserving trans I know a few lunches and some healthcare without worrying about impacting my projections for my ex-fiancée’s financial planning.

So here I am, and here you are. I won’t be putting posts up this quickly forever, most likely, but we’ll see what pace I end up at. I’ll probably charge for some of them, and I can’t say there aren’t many beautiful transgender women who you may feel deserve it more, but! Every dollar you send my way will both better the lives of transgender women and make it easier to cite my writing when I eventually take it to a publisher.

And: If you consider using Substack unethical, may I remind you: I’m on twitter.

* * *

WHAT YOU CAN LOOK FORWARD TO:

My twitter speaks for itself, I think. If that isn’t enough for you, here are some longform posts currently in the works:

(I reserve the right to drop these or write anything else entirely)

The Tokyo Yushun Is Decadent And Depraved - “falling down an elevator shaft and landing in a pool of umamusume”

Father of Gonzo Journalism Hunter S. Thompson attends the Japan Derby, becomes disgusted at the excess and vulgarity of Japanese horsegirl racing.

[TITLE TBD] - Halimede Tries Her Hand At Mechsploitation

HR Workplace Drama in the eternal space war. Complicity; Bureaucracy; Anaheim Girls Story but better this time.

Good Trans Fiction I Follow - Halimede Recommends

Self-Explanatory

Premises/Excerpts From Fanfiction I Am Never Going To Write Or Finish

Self-Explanatory. Animorphs, A Series of Unfortunate Events, Elden Ring.

I may also post lists of my own tweets, with commentary - I have five years of backlog and twitter’s search function is less than ideal.

If this sounds like a good idea to you, subscribe! Or just bookmark my Substack and click it every day despite not having an account yourself; I’m told this is how many people experience my twitter.

title: A Cis Girl's Guide To Picking Up Trans Girls
text:
In June 2024, Autostraddle released an article by some guy who probably thinks transmisandry is real named Gabe Dunn entitled “A Trans Guy’s Guide to Picking Up a Trans Girl”.

Dunn’s thesis is very simple: As a transgender man, you [the presumed reader] have so much in common with trans girls, who are also a type of man, or something close enough, that they will fall helplessly right into your lap for you and suck you off. This is self-evidently fucking stupid. I’m probably going to have to write another article about that but suffice it to say Transgender Women Are Women, full stop, and have only universal human experiences in common with men.

If, however, you are a cis girl, you have so much in common with trans girls, who are also a type of girl, and not a third-gendered group, that they will fall helplessly right into your lap for you and let you suck them off. This doesn’t mean that picking up a trans girl is easy! You have to be willing to understand the emotions of a girl severed from her very self, who is likely going to have a hard time speaking up because she was likely abused, in past relationships and/or as a child. You’re always going to be more socially acceptable than her. Your ambivalence towards your womanhood, imposed inescapably on you since childhood, seems alienating to somebody who longs spiritually for that status; you will in all likelihood have more capital, monetary and social. Power imbalances can make this difficult for both of you.

You can do it, of course. She’s not an alien, or a man. You just have to keep certain things in mind.

•

She is a woman. Treat her like one.

That’s it. That’s the whole list.

Now how do you treat a woman? You’re a lesbian, or a bisexual woman; how have your previous relationships gone? What mistakes did you make there? If you’ve never debriefed with any of your exes on friendly terms, go do that immediately. If you don’t have any exes, go make some.

How do you, as a woman, want to be treated? That, as you already know instinctively, depends on the situation. Sometimes you want the door held for you; sometimes having the door held for you presumes your weakness. There’s no shortcut to emotional intelligence and open communication, but here are a few signposts:

•

Be nice because you like her, not because you want something.

•

Take the initiative! She has been told her whole life that she is a sexual predator, and that her desires are dangerous; no amount of hinting will work. You have also been told this but she has been told this more.

•

Pick up the tab sometimes, or agree to split it. You probably have more money than she does, anyway.

•

If you’re butch, treat her like a femme. If you’re femme, be careful that treating her like a butch doesn’t cross any lines. If you are neither, be sure to examine your preconceptions.

ON ASKING HER OUT:

A special note here, on one of Dunn’s most egregious nice guy missteps:

“Only compliment her on what she can control or what is mostly non-sexual. No great tits, even if they are great tits. (You can compliment those later.) ”

Dunn here invokes accepted social consensus to try and elide his typically masculine intentions: aesthetic compliments, we are told, should center around factors within the target’s control, not her body. Her taste is her own; her body is not a thing she can control. Here’s the thing, though: transgender women put a lot of effort into fitting their bodies to their aesthetic tastes.

“’Don’t compliment her body’ she grew those herself!!! And let’s be honest she wants almost anyone to touch them! What, are you going to call her milady and tip your hat next? The most beautiful creatures of Earth long to be desired - give her what she wants!” - @HalimedeMF, 6/20/2024

She has gone to great pains to make herself so beautiful and she has never gotten to be sexually free in her life. Like you she has encountered the inevitable problem of having no way to stimulate both nipples and her most intimate places simultaneously, which only a partner can solve. Like you, gender-deviant as desiring women is by nature for us, she has been scared that nobody she is attracted to will ever find her attractive! So tell her that you find her attractive; give her your socials; let her think about it. If she turns you down, she will still certainly have been flattered, even if she’s straight.

ON FIRST DATES:

You should already have a designated first date option: a restaurant where you can console yourself if things don’t work out with some of your favorite food; a nearby art gallery or museum with rotating exhibits, so visits don’t feel formulaic; a park or beach with a picnic basket or some food trucks. Ask if there’s anything she’d like to do but have that backup plan ready, and supplement beforehand by researching spaces for sitting and talking and food nearby.

Let her get used to being around you. An activity - escape room, chess game, ice skating; fit to spec - will let you both get a better sense of each other and give you something to discuss afterwards.

You want privacy but not to be alone. Stick to public spaces on a first date. As a woman you have the power to call for help at any time. It is good and right that you have this power, because it keeps you both safer, but she may not realize that you have no intent of using it on her, due to awful experiences in her past. Men and women alike have hurt her - and to her, as to you, women’s opinions obviously matter more.

Consider bringing her flowers. Trans women are often worried that you see them as men; flowers make it clear that that is not the case. Ask her beforehand what her favorite flowers are - if she doesn’t have a favorite, pick something light, or lilies1 for the yurizoku connection (if you don’t know what this means, don’t). If you do this, have some kind of solution so she isn’t just holding them, unless you’re a top and you think trapping her a little is cute and something she’d enjoy.

Relax! She has your résumé; you’re doing your best (you’d better be!); nothing more is to be done. Enjoy yourself. Enjoy her!

ON INTIMACY:

Not a first date thing, unless you just wanted to hook up and made that clear from the start. Or things are heading that way; it’s all contextual. Making out and clothed stuff is fine though. Always leave her an out. And an in.

Know what you want; know what she wants. If you can’t tell, ask her. If she doesn’t know, you can figure it out with her or just give her time to think about it.

It is fine and normal to write scripts. Do not send her scripts unless you are absolutely sure she isn’t going to feel like that’s too much commitment.

Don’t treat her like a man. Tops get it easy here but tops get it easy in life. For everybody else: what that means exactly will depend on her. Making sure she knows other women who are tops may normalize topping for her, but can backfire.

(Formerly Hitachi) Magic Wands are anatomy-agnostic. Be aware: if she isn’t used to them, things may take a while, and if things take a while she might get sad, and if she gets sad things will take longer. This isn’t necessarily a bad thing.

People are too weird about anal. To be clear I’m not expressing any opinion on anal sex here, except that people are weirder about it than they should be.

If you date women you know your exes will talk about you; parlay this to your advantage.

Here is the cheat sheet for trans women’s common sexual neuroses and their sources; knowing either will help deduce the others. Keep in mind that without the central sexually-polarizing non-con experience of being perceived as a teenage girl, trans girls are a bit more likely to have more esoteric kinks.

•

Sexual Subjugation - I mean, she is a woman.

•

Ageplay/Petplay/Hypnosis - societal bigotry leads her toward Freudian self-castration. She longs to be less than she is and accepted. If you aren’t into this kind of thing, be clear, lest she keep bringing it up.

•

Watersports/Chastity - lack of control; pathological desire for release. Indulging these will make it harder for her to cheat; worth considering for that reason alone.

•

Bondage - lack of control; pathological desire for restraint/punishment. Fiber arts are a feminine pursuit, and trans women often strive for technical expertise. Get her some good tutorials and safe rope and this will go excellently. You don’t have to be a rope top to enjoy binding and presenting her either.

•

Impact Play - Will probably want to be hit, re-enacting the pain of her childhood. Be gentle, if you can stomach indulging at all. There is no shame in kindness.

•

Faux-Incest - Desperate longing for severed family bonds often leaves transgender women scrambling to recreate sexualized versions of family dynamics. Cis lesbians also do this2 but we are thankfully quieter about it.

AFTERWARDS:

Text her and make sure she got home safely.

If you had sex, offer her the option to stay the night. You should always have extra sealed toothbrushes.

Figure out whether leaving your little wicker basket of sanitary supplies for visitors visible in your bathroom will make her feel safe or uncomfortable.

She desperately wants your approval. Keep in mind, however, that trans women are disproportionately likely to be aware of the harms women can inflict on each other through first-hand experience, most likely via her mother. Family is terrible pillow talk, unless you want her to hold you while sobbing uncontrollably.

THE FUTURE:

Every girl is different! As you’re getting to know her, you can pull back from the generalities of both being women, and find out if you’re compatible beyond that. You have a foundation that puts you leaps and bounds ahead of any guy who’s ever tried to pick her up. You’ve got this, girl. Go get her!!!

1

unless she has a cat! to whom lilies would be poisonous.

2

cf. Goblin Market, Rosetti; The Devil Wears Prada, Weisberger; at least some of your friend group, if they are gay and trust you enough to tell you/are messy enough that it’s obvious
